ἑξαμηνόβιος.definition: living six months, v.l. in Arist.HA558a17

ἑξαπέλεκυς.definition: with six axes, = Lat. sexfascalis, of the praetor, Plb.3.40.9; or simply a praetor, Id.2.24.6, 3.40.11; ib.106.6, D.S.31.42: pl., App.Syr.15

Ἑξάπολις.definition: league of six cities, of the Asiatic Dorians, Hdt.1.144, Sch.Ar.Pl.385

ἑξάπτυχος.definition: with six folds, Sch.Il.12.295, Hsch. s.v

ἔξαρμα.definition: rising, swelling; meridian height or elevation of the heavenly bodies, Str.2.1.18, cf. 1.1.21; Hipparch.1.3.6, Gem.6.24, Plu.Mar.11, Ptol.Alm.2.3,6, Tetr.76; opp. Theol.Ar.25; Plu.2.410f

ἐξαρμόνιος.definition: out of harmony, discordant, Pherecr.145.9, cf. ib.26

ἑξᾶς.definition: a coin, Lat. sextans, as adopted by the Sicil. Greeks, Arist.Fr.510, cf. Hsch.; cf

ἑξάσημος.definition: of six times, Heph.14.1; Aristid. Quint.1.14

ἑξασκελής.definition: six-tailed, of a bandage, Heliod. ap. Orib.48.22 tit., Gal.18.774, Paul.Aeg.6.60

ἑξάστερον.definition: the six stars, i.e. the Pleiades, Sch.Hes.Op.383, Eust.870.26

ἔξαυλος.definition: piped away, worn out, of a flute, Poll.4.73

ἐξέλκωσις.definition: causing of sores in or on, D.S.3.29

ἐξεπερώτησις.definition: formal question put to a contracting party, PMasp.243.22

ἐξεσία.definition: sending forth, mission, embassy, Hom. only in phrase, Il.24.235, cf. Od.21.20: acc. pl. in Hsch

ἐξήλυσις.definition: way out, outlet, Hdt.5.101; of a river, Id.3.117; Id.7.130

ἕξις.definition: having, being in possession of, possession, opp. Pl.Tht.197b; Id.Cra.414b; Id.Lg.625c, cf. R.433e, Sph.247a, al., Arist.Metaph.1022b4; opp. ib.1055b13, S.E.P.3.49

ἐξίτηλος.definition: going out: hence, losing; metaph., food that has lost its properties during assimilation, Hp.Alim.4; so of seed sown in alien soil, Pl.R.497b; of a drug or wine that has lost its power, Phylarch.10J., Dsc.5.6; of a fa…

ἐξιτήριος.definition: of or for departure, IG3.1184.21 : day of leaving office, at Athens, Hsch

ἑξίτης.definition: the throw of six on the dice, = Epigr.Gr.1038.2 , Poll.9.100

ἔξοδος.definition: going out, opp. S.Aj.798, 806; procession, Hdt.3.14; esp. of women of rank with their suite, Pl.Lg.784d, cf. Thphr.Char.22.10; D.48.55, cf. Lex Solonis ap.Plu.Sol.21

ἐξωκέλης.definition: barebacked horse, Suid; piratical craft, Id

ἐξώκοιτος.definition: sleeping out, Hsch.:—as Subst., a fish which comes upon the beach to sleep, = Clearch.73, Thphr.Fr.171.1, Ael.NA9.36, Opp.H.1.158

ἐξώμαλλος.definition: with the nap outside, Sch.D.Chr.72.1 p.789 Emp

ἐπάγαθος.definition: = used in CIG4991, 5020 ; also of the Nile, Sammelb. 991.4

ἐπάγχιστος.definition: next of kin, IG9.334.17; neut. pl.as Adv., GDI4986

ἔπαθλον.definition: prize of a contest, mostly in pl., E.Ph.52, etc.; Plu.Flam.15; rewards, D.S.28.4, cf. OGI455.3 , Hdn.1.17.11; not even if the advantages were obvious, Archig. ap.Orib.8.23.2: also in sg., Inscr.Prien.113.31 ; D.S.4.64…

ἐπάϊστος.definition: heard of, detected, usu. c. part., Hdt.2.119; Id.8.128, cf. 6.74; Id.3.15, cf. 7.146; perceived, Ant.Lib.34.4. Adv. Onat. ap. Stob.1.1.39

ἐπαίτιος.definition: blamed for a thing, blameable; of persons, Il.1.335; for a thing, A.Eu.465, E.Hipp.1383 ; accused of a thing, Th.6.61; Plu.Comp.Dion.Brut.2

ἔπαιτον.definition: dub. sens. in PFay.81.13 , BGU792.12, etc

ἐπακταῖος.definition: = Opp.H.2.127,4.273; epith. of Poseidon at Samos, Hsch

ἐπάκτιος.definition: E.Fr.670.2, and S.Tr.1151,Fr.549, E.Andr.853 : :—on the strand or shore, ll.cc., S.Aj.413 ; epith. of Apollo, A.R.1.403 codd.; of Hermes at Sicyon, Hsch

ἔπαλπνος.definition: cheerful, happy, Pi.P.8.84 codd.; expld. by Sch

ἐπάμερος.definition: Dor. and Aeol. for Pi.P.8.95, Theoc.30.31: neut. as Adv., = IG4.800

ἑπάμων.definition: = attendant, restored in Clitarch. Gloss. ap. Ath.6.267c, cf. Hsch

ἐπάρατος.definition: accursed, laid under a curse, Th.8.97; which it was accursed to inhabit, Id.2.17; Pl.Lg.877a; of persons, Arist.Fr.148, Ev.Jo.7.49, J.AJ6.6.3: Sup., Ph.1.516; used in imprecations on those who violated graves, CIG2824…

ἐπασσύτερος.definition: Ep.Adj. one upon another, one; frequent, repeated, Nic.Th.246: with sg. word, perh. following breeze or ever- freshening, A.R.1.579; and so ever-growing penury, Id.2.472

ἐπασσυτεροτριβής.definition: following close one upon another, A.Ch.426

ἐπαυχένιος.definition: on or for the neck, Pi.P.2.93; AP6.34

Ἔπαφος.definition: a son of Zeus and Io, A.Pr.851 ; the Hellenic representative of the Egyptian god Apis, Hdt.2.153, 3.27,28

ἐπείκοστον.definition: a sum greater by 1/20 than another, PPetr.2p.156 :—also PRev.Laws56.15

ἐπέραστος.definition: lovely, lovable, Lyr.Alex.Adesp.4.18, D.S.4.7, Ph.1.671, Vett.Val.18.29, Luc.Tim.17, Im.10; Porph.Antr.12; Heph.Astr.1.1

ἔπεργος.definition: assistant, Sammelb.5680.3; work done in addition to payment of rent, IG12.62.15

ἐπέτειος.definition: Dor. gen. pl. A.Ag.1015; lasting for a year, Arist.Long.466a2; ib.464b25, cf. Thphr.HP1.1.2; having force for a year, D.23.92; Plb.6.46.4

ἐπετήσιος.definition: = from year to year, yearly, Od.7.118, cf. PSI4.320.12 ; Th.2.80; Jul.Or.4.131d; lasting the whole year, Call.Ap.78; for a year, Epigr.Gr.815

ἐπετίνη.definition: name of a plant, dub. in Thphr.HP7.8.1

ἐπεχές.definition: Adv., = following, next, IG 4.841.30,32 : Delph. GDI2642.47

ἐπήορος.definition: uplifted, A.R.2.1065, cf. Nonn.D.37.47: c. dat., lifted upon, A.R.3.856, cf. Nonn.D.10.205

ἐπήρατος.definition: lovely, delightsome, Il.9.228; Od.8.366; freq. of places, 4.606; Hes.Fr.76.4; also Id.Op.63; Id.Th.67; Sapph.Supp.20c.4; Alc. Supp.23.13; later of persons, A.Eu.958 ; A.R.3.1099

ἐπήρεια.definition: insulting treatment, abuse, D.18.12, cf. Is.4.5, etc.; D.21.25; order haughtily or by way of insult, Th.1.26; is done to insult him, Amips.9; BGU180.8 ; Philem.92.2; D.18.13; Arist.Pol.1287a38; ib.195.20 ; OGI262.24 :…

ἐπηρεφής.definition: overhanging, beetling; Pass., covered, sheltered, Hes.Th.598; of a dragon, A.R.4.144; Id.2.736; Simm.1.8; Nic.Fr.74.24, cf. Hld.8.14

ἐπήτριμος.definition: prop. woven to, closely woven: hence, generally, close, thronged, torch upon torch, Il.18.211; . . ib.552; . . too many one after another, 19.226, cf. A.R.1.30, etc.: later in sg., Q.S.14.248; Opp.C.3.382: neut. pl. a…

ἐπιβάθρα.definition: ladder or steps to ascend by: scaling; metaph., means of approach, stepping-stone, Plb.3.24.14 ; Id.16.29.2; J.AJ11.8.2; towards . . , Plu.Demetr.8; Arr.Epict.1.7.22, cf. Plot.1.6.1; Gal.9.149

ἐπιβάλλον.definition: a kind of ephemeron , Sch.[Arr.]Peripl.M. Eux.60 , Sch.Antig. Mir.85

ἐπίβδα.definition: the day after a festival, Sch.Pi.P.4.249; new-year's day, Aristid.Or.51 .26

Ἐπιβήμιος.definition: epith. of Zeus at Siphnos, Hsch

ἐπιβλαβής.definition: hurtful, Aret.CD1.2; Hierocl.in CA13p.448M.; Procl.Par.Ptol.166. Adv. Poll.5.135

ἐπιβόθριος.definition: in or at the trench, Aristid.Or.48.27

ἐπιβουκόλος.definition: = Od.3.422, al., usu. in pleon. phrase, without 22.292

ἐπιγάστριος.definition: over the belly: the covering of the abdominal cavity from thorax to pubes, Ruf.Onom.97, Sor.2.55, Gal.17.534, Aret.SA2.10, Plu.2.559f, PSI3.252.37 : esp. of the part above the navel, Poll.2.170, Ps.-Gal.14.705

ἐπίγειος.definition: on or of the earth, terrestrial; creeping, of plants, Thphr.HP3.18.6,6.2.2, al.; but land-plants, opp. water-plants, Arist.PA681a21; living on the ground, Id.HA633b1, PA657b24

ἐπιγειόφυλλος.definition: with radical leaves flat on the ground, rosulate, Thphr.HP7.8.3,9.10.1

ἐπιγναφεῖον.definition: and angle-stone of a so called from its resemblance to a carding comb, SIG245 G21,22

ἐπίγναφος.definition: cleaned, of clothes, Poll.7.77; cf. II

ἐπιγόνειον.definition: Egyptian harp, with forty strings arranged in pairs as in the named from the inventor Epigonus, Juba ap. Ath.4.183c, Poll.4.59

ἐπίγρυπος.definition: somewhat hooked, of the beak of the ibis, Hdt.2.76; of the muzzle of the Arist.HA499a7; of horses and men, somewhat hook- nosed, Pl.Phdr.253d, Euthphr.2b, PPetr.3p.7, al. , etc

ἐπίγυιον.definition: or stern-cable, Ar.Fr.80, cf. 426: written in Aristid.Or.23.17, Zonar., in IG22.1611.255-8 , Plb.3.46.3, Harp.s.v. : scanned ⏑⏑⏑⏑ in Ar

ἐπίδαιτρον.definition: additional dish, dainty, Philem. ap. Ath.14.646c; = Hsch

ἐπιδεής.definition: poet. , in need of, Pl.Ti.33c, v.l. in X.Cyr.8.7.12, etc.: pl., v.l. in Hdt.4.130: Comp. inferior to . . , Pl.Plt.311b: Sup. most in need, Id.R.579e. Adv. inadequately, Id.Lg.899d

ἐπίδειγμα.definition: pattern, example, X.Smp.6.6; display, X.Cyr.8.2.15; show-pieces, gauds, Demetr.Eloc.108

ἐπίδειξις.definition: Ion. showing forth, making; exhibition, display, demonstration, Th.6.31; of a military demonstration, Id.3.16; showing off, Pl.Grg.447c: generally, . . exhibit how . . , Id.Phd.99d; come to display oneself to one, Ar.…

ἐπιδέμνιος.definition: on the bed or bed-clothes, E.Hec.927

ἐπιδευής.definition: poet. for in need or want of; lacking, failing, that thou may'st have no point of right wanting, Il.19.180: c. gen., failing in strength, Od.21.185; A.R.2.315: as Comp., inferior to Ulysses in strength, Od.21.253, cf.…

ἐπίδημος.definition: Dor. = Antiph.11; sojourning in a place, Call.Dian.226; of Artemis, Id.Aet.3.1.26; GDI5040 , cf. Milet.3.149

ἐπιδορατίς.definition: tip, point of a lance, spear-; spear-shaft, gloss on Sch.Pi.Dith.Oxy.3.13

ἐπιδοχή.definition: reception in addition, Th.6.17; undertaking, POxy.102.18, 103.16

ἐπιδώτης.definition: the Bountiful, epith. of gods, esp. Zeus at Mantinea, Paus.8.9.2, cf. Plu.2.1102e:—hence temple at Epidaurus, IG4.1492.24

ἐπιείκελος.definition: = like, the masc. freq. in Hom. , but only in phrases Il.1.[265], 4.394, Od.24.36, etc.; so Hes.Th.968

ἐπιελίκτωρ.definition: one who rolls round, coined to explain the Homeric Sch.Il.19.398

ἐπίελπτος.definition: to be hoped or expected, Archil.74.5, Opp.H.4.311

ἐπιζάφελος.definition: vehement, violent, Il.9.525. Adv. vehemently, furiously, Il.9.516, Od.6.330; h.Merc.487: also neut. as Adv., A.R.4.1672

ἐπιζέφυρος.definition: towards the west, western, Euph.121: the Italian Locrians were called Hdt.6.23, etc., f.l. in Pi.O.10.13

ἐπίζηλος.definition: Dor. enviable, happy, B.5.52, cf. A.Ag.939, Ptol.Tetr.186: written in TAM2.245.12

ἐπιθαλέωσις.definition: perh. celebration of the festival of the Corybantes SIG1014.95

ἐπιθέατρον.definition: building adjoining a theatre, IG11.287 A94,120

ἐπίθεσις.definition: setting on its base; laying or putting on, opp. Arist.Juv.470a11; Act.Ap.8.18, etc.; application, Plu.2.102a, cf. Luc.DDeor.13.1

ἐπίθημα.definition: something put on; lid, cover, lids of chests, Il.24.228, cf. Hippon.56, Hp.Morb.2.26, Hdt.1.48, Arist.Ath.68.3, IG22.1408; Ar.Fr.295; Hegesipp.Com.1.13; slab, used as the top of a table, Ath.2.49a

ἐπιθυλλίς.definition: f.l. for in Ath.9.371f, cf. Eust.1155.20

ἐπίθυμα.definition: that which is burnt in magic, PMag.Par.1.1308, al.; sacrificial victim, Hsch. s.v

ἐπιίστωρ.definition: privy to a thing: c.gen; acquainted with, practised in, AP11.371 , App.Anth.7.2 ; IG3.946, cf. Doroth.in Cat.Cod.Astr.2.172

ἐπικαδεία.definition: fixing of buckets on a water- wheel, PLond. 3.1177.178, al

ἐπικάλυμμα.definition: in animals, covering of any orifice, of the gills of fish, Arist.HA505a1, PA696b3; of the opercula of crabs and other crustacea, Id.HA527b26, 541b26, cf. 530a21

ἐπικαταλλαγή.definition: money paid for exchange, discount, Thphr.Char.30.15, SIG252.7

ἐπικιθάρισμα.definition: piece performed after a play, Tertull. Valent.33

ἐπικλάω.definition: bend, in lit. sense only Pass., bend double; metaph., move to pity, Plu.Per.37; Ael.NA10.36:—Pass., Th.3.67; ib.59; Hp.Ep.13; Jul.Or.2.90d

ἐπίκλειθρον.definition: = Il, dub. in Gal.UP11.13 : fort. cf

ἐπίκλημα.definition: accusation, charge, S.OT227,529, E.Or.570, X.Oec.11.4, D.C.Fr.23.1

ἐπικλιβάνιος.definition: at or presiding over the oven, Carnead. ap. S.E.M.9.185

ἐπικλινοπάλη.definition: wrestling on the couch, in mal. part., Mart.14.201

ἐπικοκκάστρια.definition: mocker, Ar.Th.1059: Ar. Byz. ap. Eust.1761.26 refers it to a verb masc. cj. in Timo43

ἐπικόλπιος.definition: in or on the bosom, Ael.NA2.50, Nonn.D.8.78 codd

ἐπικόλωνος.definition: on or over a hill, f.l. in D.S.19.19

Ἐπικούρειος.definition: of Epicurus, Epicurean, AP11.93 ; Act.Ap.17.18, etc., cf. Str.14.2.20; `utilitarian' doctrine, Cic.Fam.3.9.2; the Epicureans, Luc.Herm.16

ἐπίκρασις.definition: mixing of wine, IG 11 .159 A7 , al.; tempering, Diph.Siph. ap. Ath.3.91f; of humours, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.5.30.3, Gal.10.640; Dsc.2.49

ἐπικυλίκειος.definition: or said or done over one's cups, Ath.1.2a, Plu.2.1146d, cf. D.L.4.42, Poll.6.108

ἐπίκυφος.definition: bent over, crooked, LXX3 Ma.4.5, Sch.Opp.H.1.342, Suid

ἐπίκυψις.definition: of the head, stooping, Hp.Epid.2.1.8, Antyll. and Heliod. ap. Orib.44.8.4 ; bending forward, Sor.1.93, prob. cj. in Ruf.Sat.Gon.34

ἐπιλαμπάδιον.definition: a surgical instrument used as a trocar, Mulomed. Chironis64

ἐπιληκυθίστρια.definition: Dor. comic nickname of the muse of Mnasalcas, the bombastical, AP13.21 ; cf

ἐπιλήνιος.definition: of or at a wine-press or the; commission on the vintage, PLond.ined.2135

Ἐπιλίμνιος.definition: by the lake, title of Poseidon, Hsch

ἐπιλιπής.definition: defective, wanting, interpol. in Sor.2.53, Hsch; fatty, Heliod. ap. Orib.46.22.4

ἐπιλοβίς.definition: lobe of the liver, PAmh.2.14 , Hsch

ἐπίλογχος.definition: barbed, E.Hipp.221; reserve candidate for an office, PRyl. 77.43, al

Ἐπιλύκειον.definition: at Athens, office of the polemarch , Arist.Ath.3.5

ἐπιμάρτυρος.definition: witness to one's word, etc; Astrol., supporting by aspect, Man.6.231 , Doroth.ap.Cat.Cod.Astr.6.113.1

ἐπίμαρτυς.definition: = foreg., Ar.Lys.1287 : acc. Musae.1, Epigr.Gr.905: pl., nom. Call.Aet.3.1.48; acc. A.R.4.229: in Astrol. sense , Man.3.285, Doroth.ap.Cat.Cod.Astr.6.101.12

ἐπιμαστίδιος.definition: on or at the breast, not yet weaned, of infants, A.Th.349 , E.IT231 , Nic.Dam.13J., Luc.Tox.61; of birds, S.Fr.793

ἐπίμεικτος.definition: mixed, Nic.Th.528, Gal.7.433; combining the features of . . , App.BC5.95: LXXNu.11.4

ἐπίμειξις.definition: = foreg., Thgn.297, Babr.12.23: pl., Chor.in Rev.Phil.1.73

ἐπιμεσουράνημα.definition: culmination of a star just after sunrise or just after sunset, Ptol.Alm.8.4

ἐπίμεστος.definition: filled up, in full measure, Call.Cer.134, Poll.4.170: neut. pl. as Adv., Pherecr.190, Phryn.PSp.70B

Ἐπιμηθεύς.definition: Epimetheus, Afterthought, brother of Prometheus, Forethought, Hes.Op.85, Pl.Prt.320d; Hes.Th.511; Pi.P.5.27; Luc.Prom.Es7

ἐπιμήλιος.definition: guardian of flocks, epith. of Apollo at Camirus, Macrob.1.17.45; of Hermes at Coronea, Paus.9.34.3

ἐπιμηνίδιον.definition: monthly allowance, PGiss.16.3 , PMich.in Class.Phil.22.250 , POxy.1070.45

ἐπιναύσιος.definition: feeling nausea, sickish, Plb.31.14.1; subject to vomiting, Hp.Dent.3

ἐπίνοια.definition: thinking on or of a thing, thought, notion; invention, device, conceit, Ar.Eq.539; Id.V.346; Id.Eq.1322, etc.; Arist.Mu.399b17; Secund.Sent.10

ἐπίνοσος.definition: subject to sickness, unhealthy; unwholesome, Porph.Abst.1.36; Gp.1.12.34; Hierocl.Facet.73; Lyd.Ost.37

ἐπίξηνον.definition: [not as Suid.], chopping-block, Eust.1443.16; executioner's block, A.Ag.1277, Ar.Ach.318,355,359,365

ἐπίουρος.definition: = , guardian, watcher, ward; wooden peg, pin, IG4.1484.63 , HeroAut.16.2, al., Hippiatr.26, Gp.10.61, prob.l.in Arist.Pr.915a11; nickname of Secundus , Philostr.VS1.26: Lat. epiurus, Pall.Agr. 12.7.15, prob. in Sen.Be…

ἐπιούσιος.definition: either, sufficient for the coming day, ), or, for the day ), Ev.Matt.6.11, Ev.Luc.11.3; dub. sens. in Sammelb.5224.20

ἐπίπαγος.definition: congealed or hardened crust on the top of a thing, Dsc.1.101.2, Aret.SA1.9, Gal.Lex.s.v. capsule of lens, Ruf.Anat.17; Plu.2.627f; = II, scum, Hsch., cf. Gal.6.252

ἐπιπαματίς.definition: = prob. in Delph.3.294 V. 7, GDI 4969 , cf. Sch.Ar.V.581, Hsch

ἐπίπαππος.definition: grandfather's grandfather, Poll.3.18, Sch.rec.S.OT183; or, grandfather's father, Jul.Or.2.82b, Hsch.; grandfather, Lib.Or.1.3, al., prob.l.in BCH17.532

ἐπιπαρουσία.definition: presence of a planet in a Cat.Cod.Astr.5.88.5, Paul.Al.O.4

ἐπίπληξις.definition: in strong sense, punishment, LXX2 Ma.7.33, PSI5.542.30 , Mitteis Chr.31 iii 14 : pl., of plagues, Ph.2.100

ἐπιπλοεντεροκήλη.definition: hernia of omentum and intestines, Paul.Aeg.6.65

ἐπιπλοκή.definition: plaiting together; union, intercourse, Plb.5.37.2; Str.14.2.28; Plb.2.12.7 : c. dat., Phld.Ir.p.47 W.; connexion of people with one another, Stoic.3.90, 161 ; friendly relations . . , ib.254; sexual intercourse, D.S.4…

ἐπίπλοον.definition: = Homer's fold of the peritoneum, omentum, Hp.Aph.5.46, Arist.HA495b29, 519b7, PA677b12, etc.:—also Hdt.2.47; contr. Epich.80 codd. Ath., Ion Hist.3; and Eub.95.3, Hsch.: Philetaer.17

ἐπίπλοος.definition: sailing after, D.S.20.50.3; on board ship: as Subst., = Arr. ap. Suid., cf. POxy.276 , etc

ἐπίπνοος.definition: contr. breathed upon; inspired, Pl.Cra.428c; Id.Men.99d; Id.Smp.181c; Ael.NA11.10; Plu.Pomp.48. Adv. Poll.1.16

ἐπιποντία.definition: Goddess of the Sea, epith. of Aphrodite in Hsch

ἐπιπρόσωπος.definition: with a face represented on it, Annuario 4/5.463

ἐπίπρῳρος.definition: at the prow of a ship, Hsch

ἐπιπυργιδία.definition: on the tower, epith. of Hecate at Athens, Paus.2.30.2; of Artemis, ibid., IG3.268: so of Athena at Abdera, Hsch

ἐπίπυρον.definition: hearth of an altar, HeroSpir.2.21; brazier of a censer, IG11.199B16 , al., PCair.Zen.13.34

ἐπιπώλησις.definition: going round, visitation, a name given by Gramm. to the latter half of Il.4, IG14.1290.59 , cf. Str.9.1.10, Plu.2.29a

ἐπίρραμμα.definition: that which is sewn on, Gloss.; dub. cj. for in Poll.4.119

ἐπίρρητος.definition: exclaimed against, infamous; agreed upon, Sch.Patm.D. in BCH1.153

ἐπίρριμμα.definition: winding-sheet, dub. in; slave's outer garment, dub. cj. in Poll.4.119

ἐπίρροια.definition: = Thphr.Sud.20; Ael.NA12.20: pl., Placit.4.22.1, Ph.2.151, Archig. ap. Orib.47.13.12; of rivers, D.S.5.25: metaph., Id.33.18

ἐπιρρυγχίς.definition: hook of a bird's beak, Ar.Byz.Epit.4.11, Suid

Εὐρυφάεσσα.definition: Far-shining, wife of Hyperion and mother of Helios, h.Hom.31.2,4

Εὐρωπαῖος.definition: European, D.H.1.2; Ion. Hdt.7.73:—later D.P.152:—fem. St.Byz

Εὐρώπη.definition: Europa, Europe, as a geog. name, first in; fem. pr. n. in Hes.Th.357, Hdt.1.2, etc.:—also Mosch.2.15

Εὐρωπία.definition: = I, S.Fr.39, E.Fr.381; broad surface, Pi.Fr.249b Schroeder

εὐρώς.definition: mould, dank decay, Thgn.452, Simon.4.4, B.Fr.3.8, E.Ion1393, Pl.Ti.84b, Arist.GA784b10, Theoc.4.28, Call.Fr.313, Ph.2.461; Plu.2.48c; Com.Adesp.53 D

εὐρωστόψυχος.definition: stout-hearted, Et.Gud.s.v. perh. corrupted to in PMag.Par.1.2231

Εὐρώτας.definition: Eurotas, the chief river of Laconia; pudenda muliebria, with allusion to AP5.59

εὔσελμος.definition: Ep. well-benched or -decked, Hom. always in Ep. form, Il.2.170, Od.2.390, al., cf. Stes.32, E.Rh.97; cj. in Id.IT1383

εὔσηπτος.definition: easily putrefying or decaying, Arist.GA785a2, Pr.861a38, Dsc.2.160: Comp., Plu.2.912c

εὐσίδηρος.definition: well-ironed, i.e. bound with iron, Sch.Hes.Sc.270

εὔσκαρθμος.definition: Ep. swift- springing, bounding, Il.13.31; Q.S.14.10; AP6.32

εὐσκέπαστος.definition: well-covered, well-protected, Th.5.71 ; good shelter, D.C.49.30

εὔσκοπος.definition: Ep. keen-sighted; far-seen, of stars and light, Ar.Ec.2 , A.R.4.1716; of places, commanding a wide view, X.Cyr.6.3.2, cf. Arist.HA628a11 , Plu.Cat.Ma.13

εὐσκωμμοσύνη.definition: quickness in jesting or repartee, Poll.5.161

εὐσκώμμων.definition: gen. of ready wit, esp. in bantering or repartee, Poll.5.161, Lib.Decl.15.25. Adv. Poll.5.161

εὔσοος.definition: safe and well, happy, Theoc.24.8: Bato5.10 is corrupt; cf. , Hsch

εὐσπάθητος.definition: closely woven, Hsch. s.v. prob. l. for Id

εὔσπορος.definition: Ep. well-sown, Ar.Av.230; rich in seed, cj. in AP4.1.36

εὐστάφυλος.definition: Ep. rich in grapes, epith. of Dionysus, IG7.3098 ; PSI7.845.16

εὐστείλεος.definition: with a good haft or handle, Hsch

εὔστερνος.definition: broad-chested, Man.4.96; Gp.17.2.1: metaph., of the earth, Emp.96.1

εὐστέφανος.definition: Ep. epith. of Artemis; graced with beauteous garlands, Ar.Nu.309 ; IG5.734 ; crowned with flowers, Opp.C.1.462

εὔστιπτος.definition: Ep. closely-woven or well- fulled, A.R.2.30

εὐστόρθυγξ.definition: Ep. consisting of a fine branch, AP6.35 ; ib.232

ἐϋστρεφής.definition: well-twisted, of a bow-string; shapely, Simm.1.10

εὐστροφία.definition: suppleness, versatility, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.178, cf. Porph.Abst.3.23; Plu.2.510f, cf. 975a, LXXPr.14.35

εὔστροφος.definition: Ep. well-twisted; easily turned, manageable, E.IA293 ; turning easily on a pivot, HeroAut.26.2: metaph., of man, Pl.Criti.109c; Plu.2.803f; Philostr.VS2.10.5. Adv. APl.4.385, cf. Alex.Trall.1.16

εὔστρωτος.definition: Ep. well spread with clothes, h.Ven.157, cf. h.Cer.285, Nonn.D.18.164

εὐσύλληπτος.definition: easily taken or caught, Horap.1.54; Act., receptive, Gp.17.1 : abs., conceiving easily, Gal.19.153, S.E.M.5.60, Ptol.Tetr.72; of the earth, Corn.ND28

εὐσυλλόγιστος.definition: well-concluded, conclusive; easily inferred, . . Plb.12.18.8, cf. 8.37.1

εὐσυνεσία.definition: old Att. shrewdness, CritiasFr.73 D., Arist.EN1143a10

εὐσύνετος.definition: old Att. quick of; easily understood, E.IT1092 ; Phld.Po.2.40; Epigr.Astrol.Oxy.464.42

εὔσφυκτος.definition: with a good pulse, Gal.9.802 , Aret.CA2.4

εὔσφυρος.definition: Ep. with beautiful ankles, of women, Hes.Sc.16, Th.254, Theoc.28.13, etc.; E.Hel.1570

εὔσχιστος.definition: easy to split, Thphr.HP5.6.3, Dsc.5.127; well-split, of a pen, AP6.227

εὐταξία.definition: good arrangement, of a gem; good order, discipline, Th.6.72; orderly behaviour, Pl.Alc.1.122c, etc.; as a subject of competition, SIG1061.4 , cf.IG22.417; in a state, orderliness, order, Arist.Pol.1326a30, cf. 1321a4;…

Εὐτέρπη.definition: the Well-pleasing, name of a Muse, Hes.Th.77, etc.: Pythag. name for eight, Theol. Ar.55

εὔτηκτος.definition: easily melted or dissolved, Arist.Pr.865b1 , de An.422a19, LXXWi.19.21, Man.6.524: hence fusibility, Arist.Mir.834a7

εὔτομος.definition: well-divided, regular, of a city; well-cut, of a gem, POxy.1449.14

εὐτράπεζος.definition: with good table, hospitable; luxurious, E.Fr.670.2; of men, Eriph.6; dainiy, sumptuous, Plu.2.667c

εὔτρεπτος.definition: easily changing, Arist.Mu.400a23; Medic., of diseases, mild, Gal.15.590; but easily turning to . . , Aret.CA1.1

εὔτρητος.definition: Ep. well-pierced, Il.14.182; Hes.Th.863; APl.1.8 ; with many orifices, Thphr.Sens.56; porous, Q.S.9.429; AP6.21.5

εὐτρίαινα.definition: acc. with goodly trident, epith. of Poseidon, Pi.O.1.73

εὔτριπτος.definition: easy to pound, Damocr. ap. Gal.14.130; friable, Dsc.2.24, Gal.13.124

εὔτροπις.definition: with good keel, gloss on Sch.A.R.1.401

εὔτροπος.definition: versatile, etym. of; morally good, Sch.Od.1.1; of diseases, mild, Hp.Hum.13; dub. sens. in PHib.1.2.6 . Adv. gloss on Sch.Th.1.122

εὐτρόχαλος.definition: well-rounded, A.R.3.135, Man.2.130; Nic.Al.134; on the rounded threshing-floor, Hes.Op.599,806

εὔτροχος.definition: Ep. and Lyr. poet. metapl; smoothly-running, Pl.Ti.37c; running easily, of a cord put through loops, X.Cyn.2.4; a ready, glib tongue, E.Ba.268; Plu.Per.7; of style, D.H.Comp.20; Ph.1.240, Dam.Isid.80, cf. 32; Plot.2.2…

εὔτυκτος.definition: well-made, well-wrought, Il.3.336, etc.; 8.44, etc.; 10.566, Od.4.123; B.17.50; to get meat ready for eating, v.l. in Hdt.1.119

εὐτύπωτος.definition: easily taking an impression, Gal.UP6.13, cf. Id.1.322, Phlp.in de An.605.16, Eust.633.23, prob. in Plu.2.660c

εὔυπνος.definition: sleeping well or soundly, Hp.Dent.15, cj; Act., granting good sleep, of Zeus at Delphi, Hsch

εὐφαρέτρης.definition: Dor. with beautiful quiver, S.Tr.208 , Maced.Pae.1

εὐφλεβής.definition: = I.1b, Neophr. Medea in PLit.Lond. 77 Fr. 2.19

εὔφλεκτος.definition: easily set on fire, X.Cyr.7.5.22, Arr.An.2.19.1

εὔφορος.definition: well or patiently borne; easy to bear or wear, manageable, light, X.Cyr.2.3.14 ; Id.Eq.7.8 ; CritiasFr.34 D. ; Luc.Dom.7; ductile, of clay, Ph.1.418 ; of wines, Ruf. ap. Orib.6.38.15

εὐφρασία.definition: good cheer, Epict.Gnom.19, cf. Melamp.p.24 D., al., PFlor.391.1, al. , PRyl.28.47, al. , Hsch. s.v

εὐφρόνη.definition: the kindly time, euphem. for; = Hsch., cf. E.Hel.1470 codd

εὐφρόσυνος.definition: also dub. in AP5.39.6; Act., cheering, making cheerful, Dsc.4.127; Orph.H.3.5, etc

εὐφύλακτος.definition: easy to keep or guard, A.Supp.998; easy to guard against, Arist.SE174b35 , D.C.57.1

εὐφύσητος.definition: gloss on Sch.Il.18.471; easily blown away, EM273.35

εὐφώρατος.definition: easy to detect, Gal.13.333; Plu.2.63c; Lib.Decl.49.79: Comp., Gal.6.95: dub. in Lyr Alex. Adesp.19 tit

εὐχαίτης.definition: with beautiful hair, Call.Epigr.53; epith. of Hades, Ath.Mitt.24.257 ; ofhorses, with beautiful mane, Poll.5.83; of plants, with beautiful leaves, AP4.1.51 ; ib.9.669 : also Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.60

εὔχαλκος.definition: wrought of fine brass or well-wrought in brass, Il.7.12; 13.612; 20.322; Od.15.84; A.Th.459; Id.Pers.456

εὐχειρία.definition: Ion. manual dexterity, skill, Hp.Art.35, cf. Ruf. ap. Orib.inc.20.1; in flute-playing, Poll.4.72; in battle, Plb.11.13.3, 16.19.1, Fr.158 , Hdn.1.17.12, etc

εὐχείρωτος.definition: easy to master or overcome, A.Pers.452, X.HG5.3.4, etc.; easy to train, Arist.Pol.1332b9; simply, easy, Porph.Abst.3.4

εὐχήμων.definition: gen. to be wished for, Hsch

εὔχλοος.definition: contr. fresh and green, epith. of Demeter, S.OC1600, cf. Nonn.D.41.15

εὔχορτος.definition: of pasture, fattening, Arist.HA595b26; Poetae ap.Poll.7.184: neut. pl. pastures, IGRom.4.1349

εὔχρωμος.definition: = Gloss. Adv. 'safe and sound', PRyl. 237.8 ; also in an epitaph, Rendic.d.Pontif. Accad.Rom.Ser.iii vol.3.192

εὔχυτος.definition: easily dissolved, Dsc.5.153; Aret.CD1.3; gloss on Sch.DIl.18.612

εὐψηλάφητος.definition: gloss on Suid.; on EM391.30. Adv. gloss on Hsch

εὔψυκτος.definition: easy to cool or chill, Arist.Sens.444a12, Pr.887b31 , Gal.1.329

εὔωνος.definition: of fair price, cheap, Hp.Nat.Mul.59 , Epich.42.10, Pl.Euthd.304b , D.18.89 , PCair.Zen.48.5 , etc.; Epich.34; X.Mem.2.10.4 ; AP11.169 ; of persons, App.BC2.120: irreg. Comp. Epich.121. Adv. Sup. IG12.169 . short in Hi…

εὐῶπις.definition: fair-eyed, or fair to look on, Od.6.113,142, h.Cer.333, cf. S.Tr.523 , Pae.Erythr.13, Call.Dian.204; Pi.O.10.74: in later Prose, of Hera, Max.Tyr.14.6

εὐωρία.definition: fineness of the season, Longus1.9; freedom from care, Sammelb.4324.7

εὔωρος.definition: careless, neglectful; fruitful land, Hsch.; Lat. maturae nuptiae, S.Fr.200

ἐφάμιλλος.definition: a match for, equal to; Pass., regarded as an object of rivalry or contention, D.18.320; Id.20.102; Plu.2.214d; . . IG22.1227.20, cf. 1292.18

ἐφεκκαιδέκατος.definition: containing the ratio 17:16, Theo Sm.p.69 H., Aristid.Quint.3.1; cf

ἔφεκτος.definition: containing 1 + 1/6, Vitr.3.1.6; when 1/6 of the principal was paid as interest, = 16 2/3 %, D.34.23: charge of 1/6 on payments for grain-transport, PLond.ined.2093

Ἔφεσος.definition: Ephesus, Hdt.1.142, etc.:—Adj. a magic formula, Plu.2.706e, Eust.1864.16 ): = Ps.-Dsc.3.4; = ib.113: festival of Artemis at Ephesus, Th.3.104 : victor in these games, Ephes.2.72 : in pl., title of poem by Aeschrio, Sc…

ἐφεστρίδιον.definition: Dim. of sq., Luc.Merc.Cond.37, DMort.10.4, al

ἐφεστρίς.definition: upper garment, wrapper; coverlet, Poll.6.10, 10.42, Hsch

ἐφήβαιον.definition: pubes, Dsc.1.3, Gal.8.4; hair of the pubes. Suid. s.v. more freq. in pl., Heraclid.Syrac. ap. Ath.14.647a, etc

ἐφηβοφύλαξ.definition: title of official at Pergamum, IGRom.4.396

ἔφηλος.definition: nailed on or to, Suid; with a white speck on it, Ael.NA15.18; Call.Fr.anon.106; of persons suffering from the complaint, LXXLe.21.20

ἐφημοσύνη.definition: command, behest, Il.17.697, cf. Od.12.226, Pi.P.6.20, S.Ph.1144 : pl., A.R.1.33

ἑφθημιμερής.definition: containing seven halves, i.e. 3 1/2: esp. in metre, a measure of three feet and a half, such as the first 3 1/2 feet of a Hexameter or Iambic Trimeter, Heph.7.3, Sch.Ar.Pl.302 , etc.; a caesura after such a phrase, Ar…

ἐφίμερος.definition: desired, delightful, Hes.Sc.15, Th.132; Archil.21; Thgn.993, Theoc.1.61; A.Ch.840; S.OT1375; Anaxil.38; Opp.H.4.110

ἔφορος.definition: overseer, guardian, ruler; at Sparta, the ephors, Hdt.1.65, 6.82, 9.76, Pl.Lg.692a, Arist.Pol.1265b39, 1272a5; also, title of magistrates at Heraclea, Tab.Heracl.1.1, al.; at Thera, Test.Epict.4.1; in the Eleuthero- L…

ἐφυδάτιος.definition: in or of the water, A.R.1.1229

ἐφ.definition: ’ , keeper of the water-clock in the Athen. law-courts, Poll.8.113 )

Ἐφύρα.definition: Ion. Ephyra, old name of Corinth, Il.6.152; also perh. of other cities in Elis and Thesprotia, Sch.Od.1.259, 2.328:—hence A.R.4.1212: Call.Del.42

ἐχέβωμον.definition: altar-base or chapel containing an altar, IG12.595 B24, Mus.Belg.25.108

ἐχείδιον.definition: Dim. of little adder, Suid. s.v. cf

ἐχεόδηκτος.definition: bitten by a viper, Str.13.1.14 codd., Dsc.2.120, Philum.Ven.17.11

ἐχέτρωσις.definition: Bryonia cretica, Hp.Nat.Mul.33, Gal.19.101, cj. in Dsc.4.182

ἐχινῆ.definition: hedgehog's skin, Hdn.Gr.1.334; prob. = IG11.161 B 125

ἐχινίσκος.definition: Dim. of hollow of the ear; Dim. of II, Id.10.95

ἔχιον.definition: a plant, Echium plantagineum; = Dsc.4.28, Sch.Nic.Th.637

ἑωθινός.definition: ) in the morning, early; eastern, D.P.697: Comp. Str.11.2.2: Sup. Id.4.5.1

Ἑωσφόρος.definition: Dor. Bringer of morn, the Morning-star, Il.23.226, Hes.Th.381, Pi.I.4.24; = and Ibyc.42, Pl.Ti.38d, Eudox.Ars5.2, Placit.2.15.4. : is cj. in Pi. l.c.)

ἑβδομαγενής.definition: born on the seventh day [of the month], epith. of Apollo, Plu.2.717e

ἑβδομαγέτης.definition: epith. of Apollo, to whom the Spartans offered sacrifices on the seventh of every month, A.Th.800, cf. Hdt.6.57

ἐγγαμέω.definition: marry into a family, Aesop.21c, Hsch

ἐγγαστρίμαντις.definition: one that prophesies from the belly, Poll.2.168, Suid. s.v

ἐγγαστριμάχαιρα.definition: comic name of a glutton in Hippon.85, one who makes havoc with his belly

ἐγγαστρίμυθος.definition: ventriloquist, mostly of women who delivered oracles by this means: hence, = Hp.Epid.5.63, Philoch.192, LXXLe.19.31, Ph.1.654, Plu.2.414e, Luc.Lex.20; also, the familiar spirit of such a person, LXX1 Ki.28.8

ἐγγειότοκος.definition: or growing in the earth, of truffles, Thphr.HP1.6.9, cf. Fr.167

ἐγγειόφυλλος.definition: having leaves close to the ground, Id.HP6.6.7

ἐγγενής.definition: native, Hdt.2.47; opp; born of the same race, kindred, S.OT1168, 1506, Inscr.Cos124; connexion with a kinsman, E.Supp.134. Adv. like kinsmen, S.OT1225

ἐγγίζω.definition: aor. Arist. : pf; mostly intr., approach, Arist.Mir.845a20; Plb.18.4.1: c. gen., Id.4.62.5, etc.; LXXEx.19.21; ib.Jb.33.22; ib.Si.37.30; Ep.Phil.2.30; to be imminent, Ep.Jac.5.8: also, c. gen., approximate to, Phld.He…

ἐγγλύφω.definition: carve, Hdt.2.4; ib.124; ib.138; J.AJ19.2.3; hollow out, Dsc.2.110, al.:—Pass., having a groove, Gal.2.255

ἐγγραφή.definition: Dor. IG 4.1485.126; engraving of an inscription, 1911.141

ἐγγύησις.definition: security, CIG2953 b38 ); betrothal, Is.3.53; Alciphr.3.1

ἐγγυητής.definition: one who gives security, surety, guarantor, Hdt.1.196, Antipho5.17, Lys.23.12, IG22.1172.22, etc.; Thphr.Char.18.6; Pl.Lg.871e; D.33.7; Plb.12.16.3, etc.; under securities, X.Vect.3.14; for the money, Pl.Ap.38c; those …

ἐγγυιόω.definition: stretch the limbs upon, v.l. for LXX4 Ki.4.35; cf. Hsch

ἐγγυμνάζω.definition: exercise in, Luc.Salt.6; Polyaen.3 Praef.:—more freq. in Med., to practise upon you, Pl.Phdr.228e; practise oneself in . . , Plu.Caes.28, cf. Ph.1.551, Luc.Lex.22, Jul.Or.1.37c; D.C.36.32, cf.BKT3p.25:—Pass., Hp.Vict.…

ἐγερτήριον.definition: excitement, Ael.VH2.44: pl., of the ears of a hare, Id.NA13.14

ἐγκαθέζομαι.definition: fut. sit or settle oneself in, Ar.Ec.23; Id.Ra.1523; Arr.Tact.15.5; encamp in a place, Th.3.1, 4.2; J.AJ6.11.2

ἐγκαθείργω.definition: and shut up, enclose, ib.5.1.2; Plu.2.456c:- Pass., ib.951b, Jul.Or.7.206b:-also Agath.1.11, al.:- Pass., Aret.SA1.5, Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.44

ἐγκάθημαι.definition: sit in or on, X.Eq.1.11; lie in ambush, Ar.Ach.343, cf. Th.600; Aeschin.3.206; of garrisons, lie in a place, Plb.18.11.6, J.BJ5.1.2; lie couched in, as the men in the Trojan horse, Pl.Tht.184d: metaph., . . Id.Prm.156…

ἐγκαθιδρύω.definition: erect or set up in, E.IT978, cf. Ath.11.473b, J.BJ2.13.7:—Pass., Philox.3.5 codd. Ath., Arist.Mu.397b27, Hld.5.13

ἐγκαθίζω.definition: Ion. seat in or upon; administer a sitz-bath to one, Sor.1.64, Herod.Med. ap.Orib.6.20.18, etc.:—Pass., Hp.Mul.1.35; also, to be used for such, Dsc.5.13,30

ἐγκαθίημι.definition: let down, Ar.Lys.308; send in as agents, Plu.Pyrrh.11:—Pass., of a catheter, to be passed, Ruf.Ren.Ves.7.11

ἐγκάθισμα.definition: sitz-bath, Dsc.3.113, Gp.12.23.5; dwelling on a syllable in pronunciation, D.H.Comp.20,22 fin

ἐγκαθίστημι.definition: place or establish in, as king or chief; Pass., with aor. 2, pf. and plpf. Act., to be established as ruler in a place, Lys.2.59, Th.1.122; also Id.5.70

ἐγκαθορμίζομαι.definition: Med., run into harbour, come to anchor, Th.4.1, cf. D.C.48.49: aor. Pass., Arr.An.2.20.8

ἐγκαινίζω.definition: restore, LXXIs.16.11; 1; innovate, prob. in PPar.16.24

ἔγκαιρος.definition: timely, seasonable, Pl.Plt.282e, Lg.928a, Them.Or.26.331a: Sup., Pl.Lg.717a. Adv. Aristaenet.1.15: Sup. Them.Or.9.120c

ἐγκαλέω.definition: invoke, Str.14.1.44; bring a charge or accusation against a person:—Constr.: c. dat. pers. et acc. rei, charge something against one, S.El.778, cf. Pl.Ap.26c, etc.; Hyp.Lyc.18, cf. Eux.24; S.Ph.328: folld. by a relat.…

ἐγκαλινδέομαι.definition: roll about in, Aret.CD1.2: metaph., Hp.Ep.17; Agath.4.27; wallow in, Ath.6.262b, cf. Them.Or.29.346b

ἐγκαλλωπίζομαι.definition: take pride in, Plu.Ant.36; Agath.1.13, cf. Arr.Epict.3.22.59, Ael.VH9.35; boast of, J.AJ18.3.4: abs., Ph.2.28

ἐγκαλλώπισμα.definition: ornament, decoration, Th.2.62, Plot.3.5.9, Them.Or.6.83c; of a person, Agath.Praef.p.135 D

ἐγκαλυμμός.definition: covering, wrapping up, cj. in Ar.Av.1496

ἐγκαλυπτέος.definition: fit to be veiled, hidden, Ap.Ty.Ep.18

ἐγκαλύπτω.definition: veil, wrap up, Ar.Ra.911:—Pass., to be; Med., hide oneself, hide one's face, Ar.Pl.707, etc.; And.1.17; of persons at the point of death, X.Cyr.8.7.26, Pl.Phd.118a, etc.: metaph., conceal one's feelings, c. part., App…

ἐγκάλυψις.definition: concealment, Str.10.2.12 ; Plu.2.266e; to be wrapped in obscurity, M.Ant.5.10

ἐγκανάσσω.definition: pour in wine, E.Cyc.152, Ar.Eq.105; Alciphr.3.36

ἐγκαναχάομαι.definition: make a sound on a thing, blow on a conch, Theoc.9.27

ἐγκαρτερέω.definition: persevere or persist in a thing, v.l; c. acc., await stedfastly, E.HF1351, Andr.262

ἐγκαταβαίνω.definition: go down into, put oneself in, c. acc., Pi.N.1.38: c. dat., dub. l. in D.S.14.28; Gal.UP2.15: abs., Id.8.686

ἐγκαταβιόω.definition: pass one's life in, Plu.2.783d, Longin.44.11

ἐγκαταγηράσκω.definition: = grow old in, Arist.Ath.17.1; Plu.Phoc.30; become inveterate in, Din.2.3:—also Them.Or.19.232c

ἐγκατάγομαι.definition: put up at a place, Nic.Dam.p.138 D., Poll.1.73

ἐγκαταγράφω.definition: write down among, Ael.Fr.67; portray, Aen. Gaz.Ep.12

ἐγκαταδαρθάνω.definition: sleep in, Plu.2.647f; go to sleep over a thing, ib.688f

ἐγκαταδέω.definition: bind fast in, Pl.Phd.84a, Them.Or.23.297a , Opp.H.3.201

ἐγκαταδύνω.definition: aor. of the sun, set upon a place, Hp.Aër.6; sink beneath, AP7.532 ; Opp.H.1.153: abs., sink, be absorbed in, Archig. ap. Aët.3.167, Gal.7.217: metaph., to be immersed in, c. dat., Dam.Pr.10:—Med., Procop.Arc.1

ἐγκατάκειμαι.definition: lie in, c. dat., Thgn.1191; lie in bed, sleep, Ar.Pl.742

ἐγκατάκλειστος.definition: shut up in a place, E.Fr.1132.39

ἐγκατακλείω.definition: shut up in, enclose, Alex.40.3, cf. Arist.Pr.937a29; Thphr.CP5.13.2:—Pass., Hp.Acut.16, Arist.Mete.378a29

ἐκβλαστάνω.definition: aor. I Hp.Alim.6, but inf; c. acc., grow out of, Hp.l.c

ἐκβλάστημα.definition: new shoot, sprout, v.l. in Dsc.5.92, cf. Ph.1.48, Gal.12.349

ἔκβλητος.definition: cast overboard, E.Hec.699; to be thrown out, Heraclit.96, cf. Ph.1.477

ἐκβόλιμος.definition: thrown out, ejected; metaph., abortive, futile, Phld.Po.5.29, cf. Plu.2.44d; to be rejected, PGrenf.2.71 ii II

ἐκβόμβησις.definition: shouting in token of approbation, Them.Or.23.282d

ἔκβρασμα.definition: cutaneous eruption, Ruf. ap. Orib.8.24.30 , cf.Crito ap.Gal.12.448; scab, Sm. Le.13.6

ἐκβρασμός.definition: = foreg. II, Suid. and Phot. s.v; trembling, shaking, LXXNa.2.10; confusion, Hsch

ἐκβρέχω.definition: cause to rot, of water, in Pass., PPetr.3p.120

ἐκβροντάω.definition: to strike out by lightning; intr., thunder loud, Poll.1.118

ἐκβρυχάομαι.definition: bellow forth or aloud, E.Hel.1557; Id.IT1390

ἐκγαλακτόω.definition: turn into sap, Thphr.CP3.23.1; —Pass., to be turned into sap, of the seeds of plants, Id.HP8.6.1; also, become like milk, Sch.Hes.Th.353

ἐκγαμέομαι.definition: Pass., to be given in marriage, AB259, Suid

ἐκγαυρόομαι.definition: Pass., to be proud of, admire greatly, E.IA101

ἐκγεννάω.definition: beget, v.l. in LXXPs.109.3; also, bring forth, Eup.99; Boeot. 3pl. fut. Corinn.Supp.2.62

ἐκγιγαρτίζω.definition: take out the stone from, Dsc.1.25, cf. Androm. ap. Gal.13.23, Archig.ib.12.585; Gp.8.27.1

ἐκγλευκίζομαι.definition: cease fermenting, newly fermented wine, Hp.Epid.7.64

ἐκγρυτεύω.definition: search out from old lumber, aor. Hsch

ἐκδακρύω.definition: burst into tears, weep aloud, S.Ph.278, E.Ph.1344; of trees, exude drops of gum, J.BJ1.6.6, Plu.2.384b

ἐκδανεισμός.definition: lending at interest, ib.12.515 , BGU362xiv21 ; OGI509.16

ἐκδανειστής.definition: one who lends at interest, Test. Epict.6.30, BMus.Inscr.481*.131

ἐκδαπανάω.definition: exhaust, Plb.21.10.9; Id.24.7.4, cf. PBaden19.19 ; Gal.10.192, 15.86; metaph., J.AJ15.5.1; Lib.Decl.37.30; —Pass., 2 Ep.Cor.12.15

ἐκδασύνομαι.definition: Pass., pf. inf. become hairy, Hsch

ἐκδειματόω.definition: strengthd. for Pl.R.381e, Porph.Chr.49, Aen.Gaz.Thphr.p.68 B.:—Pass., LXXWi.17.6, D.H.Dem.54

ἐκδερματίζω.definition: flay, skin, Hsch. s.v. Suid. s.v

ἐκδηϊόω.definition: destroy, ravage, in aor. I, Hsch.; —Med., Procop.Arc.19

ἐκδημαγωγέω.definition: win by the arts of a demagogue, D.H.7.4

ἐκδημοσιεύω.definition: in Pass., to be made known, D.C.61.12, 52.31

ἐκδιαιτάω.definition: decide a case as; more freq. Med. or Pass.,regulate one's habits, Hp.Insomn.89; change one's mode of life, Th.1.132, cf. D.H.5.74; Ath.13.556c: abs., having gone astray, Ph.2.48; undisciplined, Men.Prot.p.2 D.: later …

ἐκδιαίτησις.definition: change of habits, Ph.1.360, Plu.Alex.45: c.gen., Ph.2.76, Plu.2.493c

ἐκδιαφορέω.definition: draw out and dissipate, Phlp.in GC146.37, cf. Olymp.in Mete.278.18:—Pass., Pall.in Hp.2.121 D., Phlp.in Ph.625.25

ἐκδιηγέομαι.definition: tell in detail, Hp.Prog.1, Arist.Rh.Al.1434b4, Ph.2.118, LXXJb.12.8, etc

ἐκδικάζω.definition: pf. OGI7.3 :—Med., fut; avenge, .. E.Supp.1215, cf. 154

ἐκδικέω.definition: avenge, punish, Ctes.Fr.37; 2; decide a case, Ph.2.432, POxy.1020.6

ἐκδικία.definition: decision of a case, D.C.38.7; office of II.3, CIG2719 , 2771 , POxy.901.3 ; BMus.Inscr. 481*.219

ἐκδιφρεύω.definition: throw from a chariot, in Pass., Luc.DDeor.25.3, Electr.2

ἐκδιώκω.definition: chase away, banish, Th.1.24; Arist.HA618b12; Luc.Tim.10; attack, persecute, PMasp.2 iii4 , etc.:—Pass., Hyp.Fr.238

ἐκδόσιμος.definition: contracted for, let out, Poll.7.200; certificate of delivery of a document, service of summons, etc., POxy.34vii6 , etc

ἐκδότης.definition: one who farms out contracts or taxes; one who gives his daughter in marriage, POxy.497.15

ἐκδοχεύς.definition: forwarding agent, PEdgar5.11 , OGI140.8 , Ptol.Tetr.179, POxy.1669.2

ἐκδοχή.definition: Arc. IG 5.6.40; —receiving from; receiving, containing, J.BJ5.4.3, cf. Paul. Aeg.6.106

ἐκδρακοντόομαι.definition: Pass., become a very serpent, A.Ch.549

ἐκδυάζομαι.definition: Pass., to be conjoined, Phld. Herc.1003

ἐκδυσωπέω.definition: put to shame, Hld.8.3; J.BJ1.2.2; Id.AJ15.4.1

ἐκδωριεύομαι.definition: Pass., become a thorough Dorian, Hdt.8.73

ἐκζητέω.definition: seek out, Aristid.1.488 J., PMag. Osl.1.354; demand an account of, LXX2 Ki.4.11, al., cf. Ev.Luc.11.50

ἑκηβολία.definition: Ep. skill in archery, Il.5.54 : later in sg., Call.Ap.99,Str.8.3.33, AP6.26

ἐκθάλπω.definition: warm thoroughly, metaph. in Pass., Phryn.PSp.71 B., cj. in S.Fr.474

ἐκθαμβέω.definition: to be amazed, Orph.A.1218; trans., amaze, astonish, LXXSi.30.9; —Pass., Ev.Marc.9.15, Gal.16.493

ἐκθαυμάζω.definition: strengthd. for Aristeas312, D.H.Th.34, Longin.44.8; LXXSi.27.23; Ev.Marc.12.17

ἐκθεατρίζω.definition: bring out on the stage, metaph. in Pass., Ath.11.506f; in bad sense, make a public show of, Plb.11.8.7; expose to public shame, Id.3.91.10, etc

ἐκθειάζω.definition: make a god of, deify, Luc.Tox.2, S.E.M.9.35; of things, treat or regard as supernatural, Plu.Sert.11, Hdn.1.14.6

ἐκθεραπεύω.definition: cure perfectly, Plb.3.88.1, Agath.1.15; —Med., get oneself quite cured, Hp.Vict.3.83

ἐκθήλυνσις.definition: becoming soft, relaxation, Hp.Aph.5.16, cf.Art.52; —also Nic.Fr.135

ἐκθηράομαι.definition: hunt out, catch, X.Cyn.5.25, Plu.Pomp.26; .. Max.Tyr.31.3

ἐκθηριόω.definition: make savage, Ph.Fr.98 H.; Longus1.20:— Pass., become quite wild or savage, Ph.1.430, Iamb.Protr.5; also, assume animal shape, E.Ba.1331

ἐκθνῄσκω.definition: fut. aor. —die away; to be in a death-like swoon, Hp.Epid.5.42, cf. Philem.1.6 D.; opp. Pl.Lg.959a; opp. Arist.HA521a11, cf.Pr.962b4:—so in S.Tr.568 may retain its usual sense, fainting away, at the point of death

ἐκθροέω.definition: speak out loud, Poll.6.207; Pass., to be startled out of, Gal.16.221

ἐκθρόμβωσις.definition: coagulation, Dsc.1.128.7; curdling of milk, Gal.14.142

ἐκθυμιάω.definition: burn as incense, E.Ion1174; turn into vapour, Str.15.1.22, Heraclit.Ep.6.4; —Pass., to pass off in fumes, Arist.Mete.388a8, v.l. in Dsc.1.98, Ph.1.500, M.Ant.6.4

ἑκκαιδεκάγωνος.definition: having sixteen angles, HeroGeep.164, Simp.in Ph.55.3

ἑκκαιδεκαδάκτυλος.definition: sixteen fingers long, broad, etc., Ath.Mech.35.1

ἑκκαιδεκαέτης.definition: sixteen years old, Plu.2.754e; consisting of sixteen years, D.C.69.8

ἑκκαιδεκαπλάσιος.definition: sixteen times as great, Androm. ap. Gal.13.913

ἐκκαρυκεύω.definition: make into , in Pass., Hsch., Suid

ἐκκαυλέω.definition: run to stalk, Arist.Pr.924b27, Dsc.2.136, cf. Hsch.; develop a stem, Thphr.HP1.2.2, CP4.3.5

ἔκκαυμα.definition: wood for lighting fires, in pl., S.Fr.225, D.S.2.49; sg., Thphr.Ign.73; metaph., E.Fr.1031; source of heat, Aret.CA2.11

ἔκκαυσις.definition: kindling, burning, Arist.Mete.342a2; heating of the body, Aret.SA1.7 ; of baths, PFlor.385.88 , Cod.Just.1.4.26 Intr

ἐκκεντέω.definition: prick out, put out, Arist.HA508b6; pierce, stab, Plb.5.56.12, LXXNu.22.29, Polyaen.5.3.8

ἐκκεράννυμι.definition: pour out and mix, Ath.2.38a codd

ἐκκηλέω.definition: cast a spell upon, in aor. Hsch

ἐκκηριόω.definition: amaze, confound, Hsch., in pf. Pass.; cf. Id

ἐκκινέω.definition: move out of [his lair], put up, S.El.567; metaph., Id.Tr.979 ; Id.OT354; so Id.Tr.1242; —Pass., Plu.2.631c

ἐκκληματόομαι.definition: Pass., put forth run to wood, Thphr.CP3.15.4, Gp.5.40.1

ἐκκλησιάζω.definition: to be a member of the Assembly, ib.1294b3; trans., summon to an assembly, convene, Aen.Tact.9.1; D.S.21.16; LXXLe.8.3,al.:—Pass., to be called together, ib.Je.33.9, al

ἐκκλησιαστήριον.definition: the hall of the IPE12.24.9 , BCH35.76 , CIG2270.4 ; = Lat. Comitium, D.H.4.38

ἐκκλησιαστής.definition: member of the Pl.Grg.452e, Ap.25a, Arist.Pol.1275a26, Rh.1354b7

ἐκκλητεύω.definition: summon a witness under subpoena, Aeschin.2.68; —Pass., Id.1.46, cf

ἐκκλιμακίζω.definition: torture on the rack, EM322.38; cf

ἐκκοβαλικεύομαι.definition: cheat by juggling tricks, cajole, dub. in Ar.Eq.270

ἐκκοδοάζω.definition: Dor. aor. 1 pour out, Hsch.; cf

ἐκκοιμάομαι.definition: sleep off the effects of a potion, Pl.Lg.648a

ἐκκοιτία.definition: night-watch, bivouac, in pl., Aen. Tact.13.3, Ph.Bel.93.5, D.S.30.10

ἐκκομιδή.definition: removal, Hdt.8.44; IG22.655.12; purgation, Dsc.4.176, cf.2.103

ἐκκομψεύομαι.definition: Med., set forth in fair terms, E.IA333

ἐκκονίομαι.definition: Pass., to be in the dust, Hp.Vict.3.76 ; cf. Hsch

ἐκκοπεύς.definition: a knife for excising, Heliod. ap. Orib.44.11.6, Gal.2.592, prob. in Paul.Aeg.6.88

ἐκκοπρόω.definition: empty of excrement, Hp.Acut.71, cf. Dieuch. ap. Orib.4.8.11; —Pass., Aret.CA1.4

ἐκκόπτω.definition: cut out, knock out; cut [trees] out of a wood, fell, Hdt.6.37 , 9.97, Th.6.99, etc.; X.HG6.5.37; laid waste the park, Id.An.1.4.10; D.H.8.87; Plu.Pomp.24; hence

ἐκκορακίζω.definition: in Suid., Zonar., perh. f.l. for or

ἐκκοσμέω.definition: deck out, adorn, in Pass., LXX4 Ma.6.2, Aristid.1.148 J

ἐκκοττίζω.definition: in pf. part. Pass. ruined at play, Hsch. s.v

ἐκκουφίζω.definition: raise up, exalt, Plu.Mar.9; relieve pain, etc., Id.Crass.33 , Ruf.Fr.117

ἐκκράζω.definition: cry out, cj. in S.Fr.722; Plu.Mar.44; D.C.66.15

ἐκκρέμαμαι.definition: Pass., hang, be suspended, v.l. in; depend upon, Id.Lg.732e; Plu.Mar.12; AP9.411

ἐκκρεμάννυμι.definition: fut. hang from or upon a; Pass., like hang on by, cling to, c. gen., Th.7.75, cf. Luc.Tox.6

ἐκκρέμασις.definition: hanging from or upon, v.l. in Hp.Art.76

ἐκκρήμναμαι.definition: or = v.l. in Hp.Art.76; c. gen., E.HF520; we hang on to the doorknocker by the hands, Id.Ion1612; —later in Act. part. or hanging up, Iamb.VP33.238

ἐκκροτέω.definition: beat or knock out, J.AJ6.2.2; hammer out, form, educate, Phryn.PSp.68 B

ἔκκρουσις.definition: beating out, driving away; deduction, PTeb.121.133

ἐκκτυπέω.definition: burst forth with noise, of thunder, Poll.1.118

ἐκκυβιστάω.definition: tumble headlong out of, E.Supp.692; to throw a somersault over a thing, of dancers, X.Smp.2.11, cf. An.6.1.9

ἐκκύκλημα.definition: theatrical machine, used to display an interior, Poll.4.128

ἐκκυλίομαι.definition: to be unrolled, Arist.Mech.855a30, al., S.E.M.3.75,al

ἐκκύμανσις.definition: breaking of waves on a beach, Eust.31.45

ἐκκυματίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be cast up by the waves, Str.6.3.9

ἐκκυνέω.definition: of hounds, keep questing about, X.Cyn.3.10, Poll.5.65:—also ibid

ἐκκυνηγετέω.definition: pursue in the chase, hunt down, E.Ion1422, prob. in A.Eu.231

ἐκκωδωνίζω.definition: proclaim by a bell, publish abroad, Ath.5.219b

ἐκκωπέω.definition: furnish with oars, or generally, equip, fit out: S.Fr.145 ap.Hsch

ἐκκωφόω.definition: make quite deaf, Pl.Ly.204c:—Pass., become so, Luc.Nav.10, etc.; Ath.5.188c; Ael.NA1.38, v.l. in E.Or.1288

ἐκλαγχάνω.definition: pf. condemned by Luc.Sol.5; —obtain by lot or fate, S.El.760; Id.OC1337; Ar.Th.1071

ἐκλάκτισμα.definition: dance, in which the legs are thrown up behind, fling, Poll.4.102

ἐκλαλέω.definition: blurt out, blab, divulge, D.1.26, Ph.1.64, al., Aen.Gaz.Ep.7; talkativeness, E.Fr.219; —Pass., Hp.Jusj.1, Lib.Or.18.213

ἐκλαχαίνω.definition: dig or hollow out, A.R.1.374, Tryph.208

ἔκλειγμα.definition: medicine that melts in the mouth, lozenge or jujube, Aret.CA1.5, Dsc.2.158 , Archig. ap. Orib.8.2.27, Sor.1.123

ἐκλείχω.definition: lick up, of taking honey, Hp.Acut.56, cf.Ph.1.458,527: —Pass., to be taken as an Dsc.1.72,2.158

ἐκλεκτόω.definition: in Pass., to be separated, i.e.purified, LXXIs.52.11

ἐκλέπισις.definition: taking off the shell: hatching, Suid. s.v

ἐκλέπω.definition: free from shell or rind, peel, Hp.Mul.1.81,84; of crocodiles and birds,hatch their young, Hdt.2.68, Cratin.108, cf. Ar.Av.1108; of serpents, Hdt.3.109; of insects and tortoises, Arist.HA553a8, 558a10:—Pass., fut. v.l.…

ἐκλῃτουργέω.definition: undertake and complete a public burden, Is.7.40

ἐκλιμνάζω.definition: flood completely, App.BC4.107: pf. Pass. Sch.Th.Oxy.853x12:—also abs., of a river, overflow its banks, App.Fr.1.3

ἐκλιμπάνω.definition: = abandon, E.Med.800, PHamb. 27.14; intr., cease, E.El.909

ἐκλιπαρέω.definition: entreat earnestly, move by entreaty, Str.17.1.29: c. inf., Plu.Them.5, Jul.Or.7.220b: abs., Ph.2.521, J.AJ5.7.8, Apollon.Mir.3; D.L.4.7:—Pass., D.H.7.10, Str.14.5.10, Memn.7.2

ἐκλογεύς.definition: collector of first-fruits, taxes, etc., IG12.76.14; Lys.Fr.9, IG12.1001.14 , Ph.2.33, al

ἐκλογίζομαι.definition: compute, reckon, Harp.s.v; consider, reflect on, Hdt.3.1,E.IA1409, Th.4.10; Id.2.40, And.1.57; .. Th.1.70; D.21.123; Aeschin.1.64: aor. in pass. sense, to be calculated, Plu.Publ.15

ἐκλογισμός.definition: keeping of accounts, in pl., Inscr.Prien.108.214 , Phalar.Ep.24; computation, calculation, Haussoullier Cinquantenaire de l'école des hautes études p.88 , Plu.Cat.Mi.36; consideration, reckoning, in pl., Plb.1.59.2, D…

ἔκλογος.definition: balance of accounts, PLond.1.131.6 , etc; picked out, choice, Ph.2.479,539

ἐκλουτήριος.definition: for washing out or rinsing, IG4.39.18

ἐκλούω.definition: wash out, Hp.Steril.241; wash thoroughly, Plb.3.88.1:—Pass., A.Fr.32; PPetr.2pp.72,73

ἐκλοφίζω.definition: quarry from a hill, Anon. ap. Suid.s.v

ἐκλοχεύω.definition: bring forth, Orph.A.129, AP9.602 :—so in Med., E.Hel.[258]: metaph., Orph.A.43:—Pass., to be born, E.Ion1458

ἐκλυτήριος.definition: bringing release, S.OT392: expiatory offering, E.Ph.969

ἐκλυτρόομαι.definition: Med., redeem by payment of ransom, SIG588.70 , Sch.Od.4.33.—Act. only in Hsch

ἐκμαιεύομαι.definition: bring to the birth, Simp.in Ph.786.21

ἐκμαίνω.definition: drive mad with passion, Pl.Epigr.7.6, cf. Theoc.5.91; with love for her, Ar.Ec.966; E.Hipp.1229; to kindle mad desire, S.Tr.1142; to drive one raving from the house, E.Ba.36:—Pass., with pf. 2 Act. go mad with passion…

ἐκμαλάσσω.definition: Att. relax, weaken, Plu.Fr.20.1; soften, mollify, Dsc.Eup.2.17: metaph., J.AJ2.6.8

ἐκμανθάνω.definition: learn thoroughly, and, in past tenses, to; examine closely, search out, Id.7.28, E.IT667, X.Cyr.1.6.40

ἐκμαραίνω.definition: aor. AP12.234 :—make to fade or wither away, Thphr.Ign.11, APl.c.:—Pass., wither away, Theoc.3.30

ἐκμαρτυρέω.definition: to bear witness to a thing, c. acc; make depositions out of court, Is.3.21, Test. ap. D.35.20, Aeschin.2.19

ἐκμαρτυρία.definition: the deposition of a witness taken out of court, Is.3.21 , D.46.7, Aeschin.2.19, SIG953.41

ἐκμαρτύριον.definition: evidence, Anon. ap. Suid; official certificate, PMasp.87.21 , BGU1094.16

ἐκμασάομαι.definition: chew completely, in aor. Pass. Ph.1.334

ἐκμάσσω.definition: wipe dry, Hp.Acut.65 , cf. Herod.6.9; of bees, Arist.HA624b1

ἐκμαστεύω.definition: track out, A.Eu.247, Ph.Bybl. ap. Eus.PE1.9

ἐκμειλίσσω.definition: soften, Gal.11.317; mostly Med., appease, Corn.ND21, App.BC1.97, Plu.2.380c, D.C.79.19, Conon18

ἐκμείρομαι.definition: obtain for one's lot, aor. 2 Nic.Th.791; Od.5.335

ἐκμελαίνομαι.definition: to be darkened, grow dark, Heraclit.All.39; ib.45

ἐκμελετάω.definition: train or teach carefully; learn perfectly, con over, practise, Antipho3.2.7, Pl.Hp.Ma.286d; Men.715

ἐκμεταλλεύω.definition: empty of ore or metal, Str.14.5.28

ἐκμετρέω.definition: measure out, measure, E.IA816; Id.Fr.382; to end life, to die, Tz.H.3.800: abs., measure a distance, LXXDe.21.2:—freq. in Med., measure for oneself, measure out, .. measuring, calculating its position by the stars , S…

ἐκμέτρησις.definition: measurement, Plb.5.98.10, BGU432 ii 10 , measurer, surveyor, PAmh.2.79.16 , etc

ἐκμιαίνω.definition: pollute thoroughly, defile, Opp.H.4.663; —Pass., ejaculate semen, Hp.Superf.31, Ar.Ra.753, LXXLe.18.20

ἐκμιμέομαι.definition: imitate faithfully, represent exactly, E.HF1298, Ar.Av.1285, X.Mem.3.10.1, Duris89 J

ἐκμισθόω.definition: let out for hire, X.Vect.3.14; Lys.7.4; SIG1044.30 , etc.: c. inf., Aeschin.1.13; —Med., contract for, Them.Or.4.53a

ἐκμοχλεύω.definition: lift out with a lever, Hp.Art.72 ; to force them open with crow- bars, Ar.Lys.429; generally, force, compel, Plu.2.662c; dislodge, Gal.7.195, cf. Archig. ap. Orib.8.1.22; Olymp.in Grg.p.143J

ἐκμυκτηρίζω.definition: hold in derision, mock at, LXXPs.2.4, Ev.Luc.16.14

ἐκνευρίζω.definition: cut the sinews, Plu.2.451d; broken down, enfeebled, D.3.31; Plu.2.755c, cf. Ph.1.258, al.; exhausted soil, Id.2.434

ἐκνεύω.definition: aor. turn the head out of its natural; c. acc., shun, avoid, Phld.Sign.27, Ph.1.146, Orph.A.458; Hegesias ap.D.H.Comp.18; D.S.17.100

ἐκνέω.definition: fut. aor. I pf. Men.Epit.355:—swim out, swim to land, E.Hipp.823; escape by swimming, Th.2.90; generally, escape, get safely through, Pi.O.13.114, E.Hipp.470, Men.l.c., E.IT1186

ἐκνήχομαι.definition: aor. I Plb.38.16.12; pf. inf. Ath.7.315d; — = swim out or away, Plb.l.c.; .. Arist.Mu.398b32, Luc.DMar.8.2; Apollod.1.9.25; abs., Luc.Merc.Cond.2

ἐκνίζω.definition: wash out, purge away, E.IT1224; of; washed away, POxy.1469.6

ἐκνικάω.definition: achieve by force; c. acc., Ael.VH10.1; — Pass., Hld.5.23, cf. Ruf. ap. Orib.5.3.9

ἐκνιτρόω.definition: cleanse with .. Alex.2.4, cf.IG7.3073.86 , Archig. ap. Gal.12.406

ἐκνοσηλεύω.definition: cure completely, Ph.1.631, Gal.10.522:—Pass., convalescents, Gal.6.726, Orib.3.15.7

ἑκουσιάζομαι.definition: offer or be offered freely, LXXJd.5.2; ib.1 Ma.2.42

ἑκουσιασμός.definition: free-will offering, ib.2 Es.7.16, Aq.Jd.5.2, etc

ἐκπαγλέομαι.definition: to be struck with amazement, to wonder; wonder at, admire exceedingly, c. acc., A.Ch.217, E.Or.890, Tr.929; rarein Prose, D.H.1.40

ἐκπαίζω.definition: laugh to scorn, mock at, LXX1 Es.1.49, Phld.Rh.2.216S

ἐκπάλλω.definition: shake out:—Pass., spring or spurt out, .. Il.20.483; also Hsch

ἐκπαππόομαι.definition: Pass., of seeds, become plumous, Thphr.HP3.16.6, 6.4.8, Dsc.3.118

ἐκπαταγέω.definition: deafen, Them.Or.21.253c; but aor. I Hsch

ἐκπάτιος.definition: out of the common path : excessive, A.Ag.49 ; expld. by Sch. as lonely. Adv. v.l. for in Hp.Mul.2.171

ἐκπείθω.definition: persuade completely, over-persuade, S.OT1024, Tr.1141, E.HF469, PHal.7.6 , etc

ἐκπειράζω.definition: tempt, c. acc., LXXDe.6.16, al., 1 Ep.Cor.10.9

ἐκπειράομαι.definition: aor. make trial of; inquire, ask of another, Ar.Eq.1234.—Late in Act., Hld.7.19

ἐκπελεκάω.definition: hew, cut away with an axe, IG2.1054b9, Thphr.HP9.2.7, IG11.144A64

ἐκπεπαίνω.definition: make quite ripe or mellow, Thphr.HP5.1.1, CP1.16.2:—Pass., Medic., to be concocted, Hp.Epid.4.56

ἐκπεραίνω.definition: finish off, A.Fr.78; E.HF428 :—Pass., of oracles, to be fulfilled, Id.Ion785, Cyc.696; of works, to be accomplished, X.An.5.1.13

ἐκπεριάγω.definition: lead out round, Plb.3.83.3; tie behind the back, Lys. ap. Iamb.VP17.78:—Pass., to be passed round, Porph.Hist.Phil.Fr.4

ἐκπερίειμι.definition: go out and round, go all round, X.Cyn.6.10, dub. in Hld.7.19; Luc.Rh.Pr.5; Jul.Or.7.225c

ἐκπεριέρχομαι.definition: = foreg., Plb.10.31.3, Onos.22.4; surround, envelop, Hdn.3.3.8

ἐκπεριοδεύω.definition: go all round, ib.3.6.8; metaph., survey completely, Phld.Mort.37, S.E.M.7.188

ἐκπεριπλέω.definition: fut. to sail out round, so as to attack in flank, Plb.1.23.9; J.BJ3.10.9; circum-navigate, Arr.An.4.7.5: abs., ib.6.28.6; Plu.Aem.15:—Ion. Arr.Ind.20.1

ἐκπεριπορεύομαι.definition: make a detour, 'fetch a compass', of; march round, Ael.Tact.34.4

ἐκπερισπασμός.definition: an evolution consisting of a right- about-face followed by a wheel to r. or l., Plb.10.23.3, Ascl.Tact.10.8, etc

ἐκπερισπάω.definition: execute this manoeuvre, ib.12.7, Arr.Tact.32.1:—Pass., Ascl.Tact.10.11

ἐκπετάννυμι.definition: fut. spread out, of a sail; metaph., wholly given up to the revel, E.Cyc.497 : pf. part. Pass. wide open, Hp.VM22; of gaping wounds, Id.Off.11; Ael.NA2.12

ἐκπέτομαι.definition: fut. Ar.V.208; aor. part. Id.Av.788; also E.El.944, Pl.Ti.81e, 20.249 : also in act. form Hes.Op.98, Batr.211, Ant.Lib.1.5, Palaeph.12; for aor. v. —fly out or away, ll. cc.: Luc.Rh.Pr.6

ἐκπήγνυμι.definition: make stiff or torpid, l.c.; esp. of frost, congeal, freeze, Thphr.CP5.14.2; —Pass., become stiff, congeal, Str.7.5.11; to be frozen, frost-bitten, Thphr.HP5.14.3

ἐκπηδάω.definition: fut. Luc.Zeux.8, App.Hisp.20; make a sally, X.An.7.4.16, App.l.c.; Hell.Oxy.16.2; escape, Men.Per.Fr.3, cf. Wilcken Chr.1 ii 13 , Plb.1.43.1; metaph., Pl.R.495d

ἐκπηνίζομαι.definition: fut. spin a long thread, Arist.Pr.947b2; metaph., of an advocate, will wind these things out of him, Ar.Ra.578

ἐκπιέζω.definition: oppress, LXX1 Ki.12.3; a form ib.Ez.22.29; —Pass., Plb.3.74.2

ἐκπικραίνομαι.definition: to be embittered, Nic.Dam.p.34 D; = sq. II, Hp.Mul.2.133

ἐκπικρόομαι.definition: become very bitter, Arist.Pr.880a29; have a bitter taste in the mouth, Hp.Aph.4.17

ἐκπίμπλημι.definition: fill up, E.Cyc.388; fulfil, fulfilled his destiny, Hdt.3.142; Id.1.43; to satisfy the requirements of the law, Id.1.199,4.117; paid the full penalty of the sin of Gyges, Id.1.91

ἐκπιπράσκω.definition: sell off, pf. Pass. D.9.39, cf. Poll.7.9

ἐκπλανάω.definition: delude, cause to go astray, Hsch.s.v

ἐκπλατύνω.definition: flatten out, Sor.1.102; broad at the top, Sch.Il.23.243

ἔκπληκτος.definition: terrifying, Luc.Herm.18; amazed, terror-stricken, Orph.H.39.10, Man.4.81, Poll.5.72

ἐκπληρόω.definition: make up to a certain number, Hdt.7.186; .. Id.8.82; making up the number of ten chariots, S.El.708; X.Cyr.5.3.24

ἐκπλήρωμα.definition: filling up, Hp.Art.9; pad or cushion to fill up, Id.Mochl.5

ἐκπλήσσω.definition: Att. strike out of, drive away; drive out of one's senses by a sudden shock, amaze, astound, Od.18.231 ; Aeschin.1.134; .. Antipho2.1.7; Trag.Adesp.465; frightens me in speaking, E.Or.549:— in this sense most freq. in…

ἐκπλίσσομαι.definition: gape, of a wound, Hp.Fract.25; of the womb, Id.Prorrh.2.24

ἐκπλύνω.definition: fut. IG7.3073.87 :—wash; wash out, i.e. wash thoroughly, Ar.Pl.1062; Id.Fr.686; SIG1025.35 ; IGl.c.:—Med., Hdt.4.73

ἐκπνευματόω.definition: turn into vapour, Arist.Pr.866a3, Thphr; deflate, metaph., Plu.2.39d

ἐκπνέω.definition: breathe one's last, expire, A.Ag.1493 , E.Hel.142; Id.Or.1163; alone, S.Aj.1026; E.HF886 : abs., Id.Hyps.Fr.60i38, Parth.4.6: metaph., lose power, Gp.15.1.28; lose lustre, of pearls, PHolm.10.18

ἐκποίησις.definition: putting forth: emissio seminis; giving out a child in adoption, Poll.6.178, D.C.37.51

ἐκπολεμέω.definition: go to war with, LXXDe.20.10, al

ἐκπολεμόω.definition: make hostile, involve in war, Hdt.4.120, Hell.Oxy. 2.2, 13.1, D.1.7,3.7, Plb.15.6.6; Th.6.77:— Pass., fut. Med. , become an enemy to, be set at feud with, Hdt.3.66, 5.73: abs., Th.8.57

ἐκπολιορκέω.definition: force a besieged town to surrender, force to capitulate, Th.1.94,134, X.HG2.4.3, etc.: metaph. of argument, ChioEp.10:—Pass., to be forced to surrender, Th.1.117; ib.131, cf. Inscr.Prien.37.112; Arist.Ath.19.3: metaph…

ἐκπονέω.definition: work out, finish off, Sapph.98, Pi.P.4.236; practise, X.Cyr.5.1.30; Plb.4.20.12:—Med., Pl.Lg.834e:—Pass., of persons, to be in good training or practice, X.Cyr.3.3.57; Id.HG6.4.28

ἐκπορεύω.definition: make to go out, fetch out, E.Ph.1068, HF723:—Med., with fut. Med. and aor. Pass., go out or forth, march out, X.l.c., etc.; Aen.Tact.24.4; to march out to a place.., Plb.11.9.4: c. acc. loci, ib.8; but Id.6.58.4; LXXP…

ἐκπορίζω.definition: invent, contrive, E.Ba.1042; discharge a cargo, OGI 521.27,30

ἐκπορνεύω.definition: commit fornication, LXXGe.38.24; metaph., of idolatry, LXXEx.34.15

ἐκπράσσω.definition: Att. bring about, achieve; exact, levy, Id.HF43; SIG 554.19 ; ib.672.39 : c. dupl. acc., Th.8.108: abs., Pl.Lg.774e, cf. IG12.79:—Pass., to be made to pay, Paus.7.12.1

ἐκπρόθεσμος.definition: beyond the appointed day, for the debt, Luc.Herm.80; after seven days have expired, Id.Sat.2; past the time of, i.e. too old for, the games, Id.Anach.39; honours deferred till too late, Id.Nav.40; Ph.2.169

ἐκπροθρῴσκω.definition: spring out or forth, aor. part. Orph.A.346, Man.6.33; Max.226

ἐκπροκαλέομαι.definition: call forth to oneself; invoke, Orph.H.7.1

ἐκπροφεύγω.definition: flee away from, Hld.8.11; escape, Orph.L.397; AP6.218

ἐκπτερόομαι.definition: to be furnished with wings, Hp.Vict.1.25

ἐκπτοέω.definition: = Tz.H.5.484:—Pass., to be struck; to be scared, Plb.5.36.3,14.5.7

ἐκπτώσσω.definition: to be in fear of, Man.5.237

ἐκπυέω.definition: suppurate, Hp.Epid.1.20, Prog.15,Epid.2.1.7:—Med., Id.Aph.7.38, Fract.27:—Pass., Id.Aph.6.20

ἐκπύημα.definition: sore that has suppurated, Id.VM22,Prog.15, Coac.278

ἐκπυΐσκομαι.definition: Pass., = Id.Prog.15, v.l. ib.22:— later in Act., Gal.11.728

ἐκπυρηνίζω.definition: squeeze out the stone: generally, squeeze out, Arist.Ph.214a33, Steph.in Hp.1.82 D.:—Pass., Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.119, de An.132.29

ἐκπυρήνισις.definition: squeezing out, Olymp.in Mete.38.25, Mich.in PN117.15

ἔκπυρος.definition: burning hot, Str.15.1.26, v.l. in Hdt.4.73; Sor.2.54: metaph., Poll.1.192: neut. pl. as Adv., AP5.81

ἐκπύρωσις.definition: conflagration, Str.12.8.18; Philos., conversion into fire, Zeno Stoic.1.32, Chrysipp. ib.2.131, etc.; Epicur.Ep.2p.45U

ἔκπωμα.definition: drinking-cup, beaker, Hdt.9.41,80, S.Ph.35, Th.6.32, IG2.649.13, etc.:—Dim. Diph.19, Str.16.2.25

ἐκπωματοποιός.definition: cup-maker, name of a play by Alexis, Ath.15.691d

ἔκριζος.definition: neut. as Adv., by the roots, Et.Gud

ἐκριζόω.definition: root out, LXXJe.1.10, al., Aesop.179, Ev.Matt.13.29:—Pass., LXXWi.4.4, Babr.36.8, etc.; IG12.405.24 ; in a form of execration, ib.3.1424

ἐκριπτέω.definition: = sq., f.l. for Plu.2.654e:—Pass., Agatharch.48, Lib.Decl.31.33

ἐκροιβδέω.definition: empty by gulping down, in Pass., Mnesim.4.17

ἐκροφέω.definition: drink out, gulp down, cj. in Ar.Eq.701, cf. Pl.Com.149, Arist.HA612a30; swill, Jul.Caes.318c: metaph., Ar.V.1118

ἐκρύομαι.definition: deliver, E.Ba.258,Fr.190, A.R.4.83 : c. gen., Lyc.190

ἐκρύπτω.definition: wash or rinse out, Poll.1.44,7.39:—Med., Ph.1.613

ἐκσαλάσσω.definition: shake violently, AP5.234 , v.l. in Theoc.2.85

ἐκσαλεύω.definition: = foreg., Sammelb.4324.16, Hsch.s.v. shake out, Suid

ἐκσαόω.definition: Ep. for Il.4.12; Od.4.501; v.l. in Archil.6; A.R.1.10

ἐκσαρκίζομαι.definition: Pass., have the flesh stripped off, LXXEz.24.4

ἐκσάρκωσις.definition: formation of such an excrescence, Gal.13.317

ἐκσβέννυμι.definition: in pf. part. intr. run dry at the source, Hsch.s.v

ἐκσήπομαι.definition: to be or become quite rotten, Hp.Aff.5, Thphr.CP5.16.2

ἐκσιγάομαι.definition: to be put to silence, AP7.182

ἐκσιφωνίζω.definition: emply by a siphon : metaph., drain, in Pass., LXXJb.5.5

ἐκσκάπτω.definition: dig out, PTeb.50.23 ; POxy.1758.10 :—Pass., to be hollowed out, Gal.18.618

ἐκσπένδω.definition: pour out as a libation, E.Ion1193, Eub.71

ἐκσπερματίζω.definition: semen emitto, of a woman, conceive, LXXNu.5.28

ἐκσπογγίζω.definition: wipe off with a sponge, Eub.83, Aen.Tact.31.13

ἐκσπονδυλίζω.definition: or break the vertebrae, LXX4 Ma.11.18: condemned by EM324.44

ἐκστραγγίζω.definition: squeeze or strain out, v.l. in LXXEz.23.34, Dsc.4.150

ἐκστρατεία.definition: going out on service, Luc.Gall.25, Anon. ap. Suid. s.v. D.C.41.39

ἐκστράτευμα.definition: expeditionary force, Memn.15: metaph. of Nature, Steph.in Hp.2.418 D

ἐκστρατεύσιμος.definition: fit to take the field, Sch.Th.6.30

ἐκστρατεύω.definition: march out, Th.5.54; in Med., abs., take the field, Hdt.1.190; Id.4.159: pf. Pass., to be in the field, Th.2.12; And.1.45

ἐκστρατοπεδεύομαι.definition: encamp outside, Th.4.129, X.Cyr.6.3.1:— later in Act., J.BJ3.7.5

ἐκστροφόω.definition: force a door from its hinges, Hsch.s.v

ἐκσυριγγόομαι.definition: Pass., of an abscess, discharge itself by a fistulous opening, Hp.Coac.389

ἐκσυρίζω.definition: Att. fut. LXXSi.22.1; hiss loudly, D.C.l.c

ἐκσφενδονάω.definition: throw as from a sling, Hld.9.5, Mich.in PN93.32

ἐκσφραγίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be shut out from; to be sealed, of a contract, BCH35.43

ἐκσφράγισμα.definition: official copy, CIG3276 , cf. IGRom.4.513 , POxy.1882 : generally, Mich.in PN20.10

ἐκτάδιος.definition: also Opp.C.3.276:— outstretched, .. double, with ample folds, Il.10.134; Orph.A.359; D.P.643

ἐκταλαντόομαι.definition: to be stripped of money, Sopat.19

ἐκταμιεύομαι.definition: dispense, Agatharch.102; receive from store, PRein.15.16, al

ἐκταφρεύω.definition: to dig trenches, in Pass., J.BJ5.2.2, App.BC3.65, Hsch

ἐκτειχίζω.definition: Att. fut. fortify completely, Th.7.26, X.HG3.2.10, etc.:—Pass., Ar.Av.1165

ἐκτεκμαίρομαι.definition: aor. I part. Pass. to be made out by guessing, Orac. ap. Eus.PE5.23

ἐκτελής.definition: brought to an end, perfect, A.Pers.218; of corn, ripe, Hes.Op.466; also of persons, E.Ion780, cf. A.Ag.105 . Adv. in full, completely, BGU1116.9

ἐκτένεια.definition: zeal, assiduousness, Molpis3, PPetr.3p.18; abundance, Hdn.7.2.4, cf.8.2.6

ἐκτεφρόω.definition: burn to ashes, calcine, in Pass., Str.5.4.9, Dsc.1.68.4, 5.81, Plu.2.696b: metaph., of bile, Alex.Trall.Febr.7

ἐκτεχνολογέω.definition: set forth in technical language, reduce to system, Phld.Rh.1.203S

ἐκτήκω.definition: fut. E.Or.134:—melt out; metaph., let melt, pine or waste away, E.Or.134, cf. 529; Id.Hel.1419; Pl.R.411b; Critias6.12 D.; Plu.Lyc.5; Id.Brut.23; Ael.NA10.41

ἐκτίλλω.definition: fut. Hsch. s.v. aor. inf; pluck, strip bare, Hippon.84; D.53.16

ἐκτιναγμός.definition: shaking out, violent shaking, LXXNa.2.10, Ph.1.415; perh. winnowing or threshing, PFay.114.22

ἐκτίννυμι.definition: = sq., v.l. in D.S.16.29, J.BJ3.8.5, Hermog.Inv.2.3, etc.: Cyr

ἐκτιτράω.definition: fut. bore through:—Pass., Orib.46.20.10: pf. Pass. HeroBel.96.2, part. Poll.2.70

ἐκτιτρώσκω.definition: bring forth untimely, D.S.3.64, 4.2; abs., miscarry, Hdt.3.32, Hp.Aph.3.12, Arist.HA585a22:—so in Med., Hp.Aër.10

ἐκτοιχωρυχέω.definition: break into a house and rob it: generally, pillage, plunder, Plb.4.18.8; Id.18.55.2

ἑκτολογέομαι.definition: to be subject to a tax of one- sixth of the produce, Arch.Pap.5.392

ἐκτομίας.definition: one that is castrated, eunuch, Hdt.3.92; Id.6.9; Arist.Pr.897b27; Antiph.133.5

ἐκτοπίζω.definition: remove from a place, PTeb.38.18 (ii B.C; metaph., pervert into a fable, Str.4.1.7

ἐκτοπισμός.definition: being away, distance, Str.4.5.5, prob. in Cic.Att.12.12.1

ἐκτραχηλίζω.definition: Att. fut. prop. of a horse, throw; metaph., ruin, pervert, D.9.51, Luc.Rh.Pr.10, Alciphr.3.40, Porph.Abst.1.42; Mich.in EN523.20:—Pass., Ph.Fr.102 H

ἐκτραχύνω.definition: metaph., exasperate, Plu.Alc.14; App.BC2.12:—Pass., Plu.Arat.49: abs., App.BC1.10

ἐκτρέπω.definition: Ion. turn out of the course; turn a person off the road, order him out of the way, S.OT806:—Pass. and Med., get out of one's way, D.19.225, cf. Ar.Pl.837, Luc.Tim.5; avoid, Plb.35.4.14; Jul.Or.7.223d: c. inf., AP10.56…

ἐκχλοιόομαι.definition: Pass., to be or grow sallow, Hp.Coac.480
