ἐξομοίωσις.definition: assimilation, Thphr.CP4.3.1; becoming like, Ph.1.35, Plu.Per.2, Dam.Pr.341, Procl.in Ti.3.200D

ἐξομολογέομαι.definition: confess, LXXDa.9.20; make grateful acknowledgements, give thanks, sing praises, LXX2 Ki.22.50, al., Ph.1.59, al., Ev.Matt.11.25: c. acc., LXXGe.29.35

ἐξομολόγησις.definition: admission, confession, Plu.2.987d; i.e. of the possession of a loaf, J.BJ5.10.3; confession of gratitude, Ph.1.60, al

ἐξομόργνυμι.definition: fut. wipe off from; metaph., wipe off one's folly on another, i.e. give him part of it, Id.Ba.344, parodied by Ar.Ach.843

ἐξονειδίζω.definition: c. acc. rei, cast in one's teeth, S.El.288, E.IA305; J.AJ5.1.18; having foul reproaches cast upon one, S.Ph.382

ἐξονομάζω.definition: utter aloud, announce, h.Merc.59; call by name, Plu.Cic.40:—Pass., to be referred to by name, PTeb.28.17 , etc

ἐξοπλίζω.definition: arm completely, Hdt.7.100, X.Cyr.4.5.22; generally, fully prepared, ready, Ar.Pax566; . . Antiph.226.2, cf. 217.19

ἐξόπλισις.definition: getting under arms, X.Cyr.8.5.9, cf. Arist.Pr.922b14

ἐξοργίζω.definition: enrage, X.Eq.9.2; Aeschin.1.192; X.Mem.3.3.7:—Pass., to be enraged, furious, Batr.[184a], Satyr.Vit.Eur.Fr.39x33 , Plb.6.57.8, al., Phld. Mus.p.78 K., Aristaenet.2.20

ἐξορίζω.definition: expose a child, E.Ion504; banish, get rid of, Pl.Smp.197d; Arist.Pol.1336b5; Id.EN1180a10: c. gen., Jul.Or.6.186b

ἐξορισμός.definition: sending beyond the frontier, D.H.5.12; Plu.2.549a; prob. cj. in Porph.Abst.1.10

ἐξορκίζω.definition: conjure, LXXGe.24.3, cf. PMag.Lond.121.269; ib.892; Ev.Matt.26.63; also PMag.Par.1.356

ἐξορκόω.definition: earlier form of administer an oath to one, c. acc. pers., or abs., Foed. ap. Th.5.47, cf. D.21.65, IG22.1174.15: c. fut. inf., ib.2.841b35: folld. by Hdt.3.133,4.154: later, c. pres. inf., J.AJ9.7.4: c. acc. pers. et …

ἐξόρκωσις.definition: binding by oath, Id.4.154; exorcism, J.AJ8.2.5

ἐξορμενίζω.definition: shoot forth, sprout, S.Ichn.275; run to seed, Poll.6.54

ἐξορμέω.definition: to be out of harbour, run to sea, Lycurg.17, And.1.11, Is.6.27: metaph., Aeschin.3.209; to be out of one's senses, Paus.3.4.1

ἐξόρμησις.definition: urging on, Arr.An.3.9.7; rushing forth, Sch.Th.3.89; vehement attack, D.C.75.6; setting out, start, Arr.An.1.11.5

ἐξορμιστόν.definition: a fish similar to the Cassiod.Var.12.4,14

ἐξόρνυμι.definition: in Med., rush out, aor. , A.R.1.306

ἐξορύσσω.definition: Att. dig out the earth from a; dig out of the ground, dig up, Hdt.1.64, cf. BGU1024iv4 ; Ar.Ach.763; Lys.7.26:—Pass., PHal.1.109 ; X.Oec.19.4

ἐξορχέομαι.definition: dance away, hop off, D.22.68; c. acc. cogn., dance out a figure, go through it, Philostr.Im.2.12; Suid. s.v

ἐξοστεΐζω.definition: take out the bones, prob. l. in Horap.2.38, cf. Suid. s.v. take out of the bone, Dsc.2.77: metaph., of fruits, remove the seeds or kernels, . . Id.5.75; Ruf. ap. Orib.8.47.7

ἐξοστρακίζω.definition: banish by ostracism, Hdt.8.79, And.4.32, Lys.14.39, Pl.Grg.516d; Luc.Sacr.4:—Pass., Themist.Ep.2; also Ar.Fr.593; Demad.53; Anon.Alch. in Gött.Nachr.1919.14

ἐξοστρακισμός.definition: banishment by ostracism; formation of any external shell, interpol. in Corn.ND17

ἐξοτρύνω.definition: stir up, urge on, excite, A.Th.692 , cf. E.Supp.24; Th.1.84, etc.:—Pass., Ph.2.564

ἐξούρησις.definition: passing with the urine, Aët. ap. Phot.p.179B

ἐξουσιάζω.definition: fut. Phld. :—exercise; exercise authority over, CIG4584 ; Ev.Luc.22.25, cf. 1 Ep.Cor.7.4; PMasp.15.170 :—Med., LXXNe.5.15; ib.Ec.8.9:— Pass., to be held under authority, 1 Ep.Cor.6.12

ἐξουσιαστής.definition: mighty one, person in authority, LXXIs.9.6, Cat.Cod.Astr.5.86, PGen.53.2

ἐξοφθαλμιάζω.definition: have no eye for, disregard, PGoodsp.Cair.15.22

ἐξοφρυόω.definition: in pf. part. Pass. supercilious, Hsch., EM350.22

ἐξοχετεύω.definition: draw off, Hp.Aër.18; Gal.UP10.11: metaph., Emp.35.2; Procl.H.1.4

ἐξοχή.definition: prominence, elevated; metaph., pre-eminence, in nullo est, Cic.Att.4.15.7; Longin.10.3; Hierocl.p.55 A.; par excellence, Str.1.2.10, Ph.1.65, A.D.Synt.26.15, OGI764.52 , etc.; leading men, Act.Ap.25.23

ἔξοχος.definition: standing out, jutting, Pi.N.4.52; more freq. metaph., eminent, excellent, Il.2.188; Pi.N.6.47: Comp. ib.3.71: Sup. ib.2.18, A.Ag.1622, E.Supp.889; Phld.Lib.p.20O.; = Lat. eminentissimus, OGI640.16 , POxy.1469.1 , cf. …

ἐξυβρίζω.definition: break out into insolence, wax wanton; c. acc. pers., treat with insolence or violence, Id.12.2; also Conon24.2:—Pass., Hyp.Phil.9; despised things, Longin.43.5

ἐξυγραίνω.definition: saturate, Arist.Pr.877a33, al.:—Pass., to; make watery, of the blood, Id.HA521a12 , cf. Plu.2.97b : metaph., ib.136b:—Pass., to be so, of plants, Thphr.CP6.6.4

ἐξυδατόω.definition: make into water or make watery, Hp.Fist.7; Thphr.Od.66; Sor.1.93:—Pass., Corn.ND17, Archig. ap. Orib.44.26.6, etc.; become dropsical, Hp.Epid.4.49

ἐξυλακτέω.definition: bark out: burst out in rage, Plu.Arat.50; Aeschin.Socr.38: c. acc. cogn., yell it out, Lyc.764

ἐξυμνέω.definition: strengthd. for Plb.6.47.7, Phld.Rh.1.219, 2.148 S., D.S.9 Fr. 26, Procl.in Alc.p.84 C.:—Pass., Lyc.1195

ἐξυπηρετέω.definition: assist to the utmost, S.Tr.1156; Lys.12.23, cf. Chrysipp.Stoic.3.123; J.AJ13.3.1: abs., Phld.Sto.339.9:—later in Med., IG12.406 :—Pass., every emergency will be provided for, Ael.Tact.35.1

ἐξυπνίζω.definition: awaken from sleep, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.334, cf. Ev.Jo.11.11:—Pass., wake up, LXXJd.16.14, Plu.Ant.30, M.Ant.6.31

ἔξυπνος.definition: awakened out of sleep, LXX1 Es.3.3, Act.Ap.16.27, J.AJ11.3.2, Zos.Alch.p.118 B. Adv. PGiss.1.19.4

ἐξυφαίνω.definition: weave, Hdt.2.122,9.109, cf; finish weaving, Artem.4.40; Gp.15.5.2

ἐξωκεανισμός.definition: a placing out in the ocean, Str.1.2.10

ἐξώλεια.definition: utter destruction, IG12.10.15, cf. Antipho5.11, Lys.12.10, Jusj. ap. D.24.151; D.21.119, 57.22; ib.53

ἐξωμίς.definition: = tunic with one sleeve, leaving one shoulder bare, worn by slaves and the poor, Id.V.444 , Lys.662, X.Mem.2.7.5, etc.; by Laconizers, Ael.VH9.34; by Cynics, S.E.P.1.153; by the rich when not on ceremony, Suid. s.v.; …

ἐξωτάτω.definition: Adv., Sup. of outermost, Pl.Phd.112e, Arist.Cael.279a20, Ph.2.331, etc.:—later, Adj. LXX3 Ki.6.30; Ph.1.95

ἐξωτέρω.definition: Adv., Comp. of more outside, A.Ch.1023, cf. Arist.Metaph.1055a25, LXXJb.18.17, etc.:—hence later, Adj. outer, LXXEx.26.4, etc., Ev.Matt.8.12; POxy.896.14

ἑορτάζω.definition: in Ion.Prose impf. (with; celebrate as a festival, celebrate it by a festival, Plu.2.349f, cf. Ant.56; at Rome, celebrate by a triumph, D.C.51.21

ἑορτάσιμος.definition: of a festival, J.AJ11.6.13, cf. Plu.2.270a, OGI524.8 ; though I was in no holiday mood, Luc.Sat.11

ἐπαγαίομαι.definition: Pass., exult in, A.R.3.1262; feel a malignant joy in, ib.470: Ep. aor. Epic. ap. Parth.21; Hsch

ἐπαγανακτέω.definition: to be indignant, abs., J.BJ2.13.3, Plu.Alc.14, Ages.19

ἐπαγγελία.definition: command, summons, Plb.9.38.2; announcement, notice, IG22.1235.7 ; SIG561.9 , prob. in LXX1 Ma.10.15; v.l. in 1 Ep.Jo.1.5

ἐπαγγέλλω.definition: aor. Pass. IG12.188.25; give orders, command, abs., Id.1.70: c.acc. et inf., give orders that . ., ib.77, cf. Th.6.56: c. dat. et inf., order one to do, D.42.7, etc.: c. acc. rei, send them orders to furnish their con…

ἐπάγγελμα.definition: promise, profession, D.19.178; subject of a treatise, that which it purports to contain, D.H.Dem.33; Ael.Tact.Praef.7

ἐπαγγελτήρ.definition: envoy who announces a festival, etc., SIG558.5

ἐπαγινέω.definition: Ion. for bring to, Hdt.2.2, Q.S.6.235

ἐπαγκυλίζομαι.definition: Pass., to be fitted with an Sch.E.Or.1476

ἐπαγρύπνησις.definition: watching for, ibid.; Aristeas167; watchfulness, Phld.Lib.p.7 O

ἐπάγρυπνος.definition: wakeful, sleepless, Mitteis Chr.77.11 , cf. Vett. Val.11.16, Aristaenet.1.27

ἐπαγωγεύς.definition: coat of clay on a wall, IG22.1672.61

ἐπαγωνίζομαι.definition: contend with, Plu.Fab.23; continue; c. dat. rei, contend in, IG12.860.19 ; contend for, Ep.Jud.3: lay stress on, Gal.14.246; Plu.Num.8; Aristid.Rh.1p.500S.: abs., S.E.M.3.93; exert oneself, IG22.1343.16

ἐπαείδω.definition: contr. Att. fut. Ar.Ec.1153; sing as an incantation, X.Mem.2.6.11; Pl.Phd.114d, cf. 77e; Id.R.608a; sing to one so as to charm or soothe him, Id.Phdr.267d, Lg.812c, al.:—Pass., Porph.Chr.35: abs., use charms or incant…

ἐπαιδέομαι.definition: fut. E.IA900 : aor; c. acc., reverence, A.Fr.135, Antipho Soph.Oxy.1364.270, Pl. l.c., Herod.2.39

ἐπαινέτης.definition: praiser, commender, Hp.Acut.6; rhapsodist, Pl.Ion536d; cf. IV

ἔπαινος.definition: approval, praise, commendation, Simon.4.3; complimentary address, panegyric ; Pl.Phdr.260c; Id.Smp.177d; Id.Phdr.260b; Aeschin.3.50; Pl.Lg.947c; Plb.1.1.1, D.S.13.22, D.H.10.57

ἐπαισθάνομαι.definition: have a perception or feeling of, c. gen; abs., become sensible, recover one's senses, Hp.Morb.3.8

ἐπαίσθησις.definition: perception, Epicur.Ep.1p.13U., cf. Phld.Mus.p.42K., al., Sor.2.19; Epicur.Nat.125 G., Porph.Abst.1.57, 3.15

ἐπαισχύνομαι.definition: fut. to be ashamed at or; late in Act., make ugly, mar, Nonn.D.20.61, 42.421

ἐπαίτης.definition: beggar, Telesp.14 H., Nech. ap. Vett.Val.290.2, Ath.5.192f, D.C.66.8 codd

ἐπαιτητάριον.definition: little beggar, name of an amulet, PMag.Par.1.2378

ἐπαιτιάομαι.definition: fut. Ion. bring a charge against, accuse, etc.; Hp.Aër.22; accuse one of a thing, Th.6.28, D.21.114; for your mishaps, A.Pr.974; also I accuse her of this burial, that she planned it, S.Ant.490: c. inf., Id.OT645; . .…

ἐπαΐω.definition: contr. E.HF773 : aor. 1; perceive, feel, Pi.Fr.75.15 ; Hdt.3.29; Ael.NA1.5; Hierocl.in CA24p.472M.: c. part., Ar.V.516; Hp.Prorrh.2.16; A.R.1.1023, 2.195: abs., when he perceived it, Hdt.9.93

ἐπαιωρέω.definition: keep hovering over another; Pass., hover over or on the surface, float upon, Dsc.5.92, cf. 75; buoyed up by . ., Luc.Alex.16; hang over it, conduct it remissly, Plu.Pel.29; in Hp.Art.75, of one who throws his whole we…

ἐπακολουθέω.definition: follow close upon, follow after, pursue; attend to, follow mentally, understand, Pl.Phd.107b; Id.Lg.861c; Id.Sph.243a; Id.Lg.963a, etc

ἐπακολούθησις.definition: cognizance, concurrence; consequence, consequentially, opp. Stoic.2.333, Stoic. ap.Plu.2.1015c, M.Ant.6.44, S.E.M.1.194; result, Gal.19.382

ἐπακόλουθος.definition: following, Aristid.Rh.2p.522S.: Comp., PMag.Par.1.1536. Adv. agreeably to, Antip. ap.Stob.4.22.103, cf. PMasp.97 ii 68

ἐπάκριος.definition: on the heights, epith. of Zeus; a district in Attica, Str.9.1.20

ἐπακροάομαι.definition: = abs., Pl.Com.16, Nic.Dam.Vit.Caes.29: c. gen. pers., Act.Ap.16.25, Luc.Icar.1: c. gen. rei, Hld.2.17: c. acc. rei, Men.Epit.Oxy.1236v16; Ant.Lib.11.6 hearkening, obedience, LXX1 Ki.15.22

ἐπαλαλάζω.definition: raise the war-cry, A.Th.497,951 , D.S.19.30; X.Cyr.7.1.26; Jul.Or.1.36b

ἐπαλγής.definition: painful, Aristeas167, Str.11.13.2, Philum. ap.Aët.5.127, Aët.15.13, Opp.H.4.508: Comp., LXX4 Ma.14.10, Onos.42.19, Aret.SD2.3. Adv. Poll.3.99

ἐπάλειμμα.definition: unguent, Dsc.1.43.4, cf. Inscr.Prien.112.90, al. , Michel544.20

ἐπαλείφω.definition: metaph., from anointing athletes, prepare for contest, stir up, irritate, Plb.2.51.2; set them upon him, D.L.2.38; Ph.1.680; so perh. in physical sense, irritate, Hp.Mul.1.99, Epid.5.20

ἐπαλινδέομαι.definition: Pass., lit., roll on: hence had been effaced, A.R.4.1463:—also Nic.Th.266

ἐπαλλαγή.definition: premium on exchange of currency, PCair.Zen.22.2

ἐπαλληλία.definition: sequence, unbroken series, Eust.11.32 , cf. EM576.2; taking one drug after another, 'mixing medicines', Gal.19.679

ἐπαλφιτόω.definition: add meal to wine, prob. in Ath.10.432b

ἐπαμάομαι.definition: scrape together for oneself, heaped him up a bed , Od.5.482; Thgn.428, cf. Thphr.HP4.13.5, AP7.446 ; having heaped up a grave or barrow, Hdt.8.24; so Polyaen.2.1.23; Plu.2.982b; Porph.Abst.4.9:—later in Act., D.L.6.79…

ἐπαμπέχω.definition: and , put on over, overwrap, E.Tr.1148; enwrap, Ph.2.379; Plu.Oth.5:—Med., Ph.1.358, al., D.Chr.6.26; Plu.2.1102d:— Pass., Id.Sert.10

ἐπαμύντωρ.definition: helper, defender, Od.16.263; as fem., Orph.L.587

ἐπαμφιέννυμι.definition: cloak or veil, prob.l. in Men.404.5; in later form Aristid.Or.30.18:—Pass., [S.]Fr.1127.2

ἐπαμφοτερίζω.definition: to be double: hence, play a double game; of statements or arguments, to be ambiguous, susceptible of two interpretations, Isoc.12.240, cf. Pl.R.479b; . . Luc.DDeor.16.1

ἐπαμφοτερισμός.definition: inclination both ways, wavering; uncertainly of parentage, Ph.2.202

ἐπαναβαίνω.definition: poet. Opp.H.3.638:—get up on; of animals, cover, Id.HA540a22, Clearch.36

ἐπαναβάλλω.definition: throw on or over:—Med; lift up, Ath.12.529a

ἐπαναβιβάζω.definition: causal of make to mount upon, Th.3.23, cf. D.C.50.23

ἐπαναβιβασμός.definition: in pl., ascending steps in argument, Herm.in Phdr.p.64A

ἐπαναβλαστάνω.definition: grow upon, Choerob. in An.Ox.2.198.30, Sch.Dsc.p.362 Matth

ἐπαναγιγνώσκω.definition: read over, read out, f.l. in Lys.10.18, cf. Plb.31.13.10; PPetr.2p.3 ; of a teacher, S.E.M.10.19, Porph.Chr.58:—Pass., D.7.19

ἐπαναγκάζω.definition: compel by force, constrain, c. acc. et inf., A.Pr.671, Ar.Av.1083, PHib.1.34.3 , etc.:—Pass., Ar.Pl.525, etc.: freq. with inf. omitted, Hdt.8.130, cf. Ar.Pl.533, Th.5.31

ἐπαναγορεύω.definition: proclaim publicly:—impers. in Pass., proclamation is made, Ar.Av.1071

ἐπαναδίδωμι.definition: intr., increase more and more, Hp.Epid.1.25

ἐπαναδιπλόω.definition: repeat yet again, Arist.Pr.910b25, Gal.15.879:—Pass., to be repeated, Arist.APr.49a11, Metaph.1003b28

ἐπαναδίπλωσις.definition: doubling, folding, of the; repetition, Arist.APr.49a26

ἐπαναζώννυμαι.definition: Med., gird on one's clothes, Ph.2.479

ἐπαναθέω.definition: run up against, Onos.18: abs., Id.6.1

ἐπαναίρεσις.definition: slaughter, destruction, Plb.2.37.8: pl., Nech. in Cat.Cod.Astr.7.140

ἐπαναίρω.definition: lift up, raise high, X.Cyn.6.23:—Med., raise the spear one against the other, S.OC424; but raised his staff against him, Th.8.84, cf. Hsch. s.v. rise up, Ar.Eq.784

ἐπανακαινίζω.definition: renew, revive, LXXJb.10.17, Phld.Acad.Ind.p.4 M.:—also Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.49.549

ἐπανακαλέω.definition: invoke besides, A.Ag.145; recall, Aret.SD2.13 :—Med., Arr.An.4.27.1, cf. Dam.Pr.245, Procl.in Alc.p.182 C.:—Pass., Hierocl.in CA7p.429M

ἐπανακάμπτω.definition: intr., come back again, Arist.Pr.916a32: abs., bend back, of ducts or veins, Id.HA510a21,514a11; return, Aq., Sm., Thd.Is.35.10

ἐπανακλαγγάνω.definition: give tongue again and again, X.Cyn.4.5,6.23

ἐπανάκλησις.definition: recall, reaction; double inspiration, Hp.Epid.2.3.7, Gal.7.899

ἐπανακλίνω.definition: make to lie down, Hp.Acut.37, cf. Sm.Ca.2.5; incline one valve of the heart towards the other, Hp.Cord.10

ἐπανακράζω.definition: call out to, in aor. imper. Poll.5.85

ἐπανακρούω.definition: poet. put a ship back , Hsch.: metaph., Isyll.6:—Med., put back, Ar.Av.648

ἐπανακυκλέω.definition: recur, of intermittent fevers, Gal.7.412; Pass., make a counter revolution, Pl.R.617b; but simply, revolve, Dam.Pr.23

ἐπανακύκλησις.definition: return of a circle into itself, Pl.Ti.40c

ἐπανακύπτω.definition: have an upward slope, X.Eq.12.13; rise up to thwart, J.BJ1.31.1

ἐπαναλαμβάνω.definition: take up again, resume, repeat; revise, correct, Id.Lg.781b; Thphr.CP3.7.8

ἐπανάληψις.definition: in Rhet., resumption, repetition; = III, Gal.7.433

ἐπαναλίσκω.definition: consume still more, D.50.42: aor; spend in addition, IG 12.24 ; but PCorn.1.88

ἐπαναμένω.definition: poet. wait longer, Hdt.8.141; wait for one, Id.Nu.803; Id.Lys.74: impers., what there is in store for me to suffer, A.Pr.605 ; Id.Pers.807; . . S.OC1718

ἐπαναμιμνῄσκω.definition: remind one of, mention again to one, Pl.Lg.688a, cf. Arist.Mem.451a12, Porph.Abst.1.30; . . D.6.35

ἐπανανεόομαι.definition: Med., revive, Pl.R.358b; renew, POxy.237 viii41

ἐπαναπαύω.definition: Med., come to rest, of a machine, HeroAut.24.4: metaph., come to rest in, Iamb.Comm.Math.8; Ev.Luc.10.6; LXXNu.11.26

ἐπαναπέμπω.definition: send back to a point, Hp.Mul.2.133, prob. in PPetr.2p.64

ἐπαναπέτομαι.definition: aor. 2 inf. fly up, Hsch. s.v

ἐπαναπήγνυμι.definition: fix in or on:—Med., fix their spears in the ground, Orph.A.319

ἐπαναπιπράσκω.definition: put up to sale again:—Pass., aor. part. PPetr.3p.120 : fut. PTheb.Bank1.24 , cf. UPZ112iii12

ἐπαναπλέω.definition: put to sea against, Hdt.8.9, cf; sail back again, ib.24, D.56.29, Plb.1.28.10

ἐπαναπρίασθαι.definition: acr., buy at a re-sale, IG7.3073.26

ἐπαναρρήγνυμι.definition: tear open again, Plu.Cat.Mi.70:—Pass., burst open afresh, Hp.Loc.Hom.14

ἐπανασείω.definition: lift up and shake, Hp.Foet.Exsect.4: metaph., threaten one with it, D.H.11.6; Procop.Arc.23:—Pass., of soldiers, being used to overawe . ., J.AJ19.1.16, cf. 17

ἐπανασκοπέω.definition: consider yet again, Pl.Cra.428d, Hp.Mi.369d; Id.Tht.154e

ἐπανάστασις.definition: rising up to go to stool: hence; rising up again, D.S.18.31

ἐπανάστημα.definition: rising, blister, Sch.Ar.Ra.238; eminence, hill, Phlp.in de An.311.24

ἐπαναστροφή.definition: = return, of the chorus; Rhet., repetition of the last word or words of a sentence at the beginning of the next, Hermog.Id.1.12; of the syllables in Eust.1751.40

ἐπανάτασις.definition: stretching upwards, holding up; metaph., threatening, Ph.1.282 , al., POxy.237 viii 10 , Iamb.Myst.6.6; brandishing, PHal.1.186

ἐπανατείνω.definition: poet. Orph.A.61,332:—stretch; freq. in Med., brandish threatingly, PHal.1.186 ; Luc.Cat.13, cf. Jul.Or.6.196b; Plb.2.44.3: c. inf., threaten to do, Id.15.29.14:—Pass., POxy.1408.17

ἐπανατέλλω.definition: intr., rise, Hdt.2.142; Id.3.84; Id.7.54; AP12.178 ; H Arist.Mete.376b29; of a star, Sammelb.2134.7; rise again, Gem.6.10; having risen from bed, A.Ag.27; Plu.Aem.18; show oneself, appear, A.Ch.282; E.HF1053 ; the tim…

ἐπανατρέπω.definition: overturn, upset, Hdn.3.8.5; intr., return, Cratin.181

ἐπανατρέφω.definition: feed up, recruit, nourish, Hp.Aph.2.7, Aret.CD1.5

ἐπανατρέχω.definition: aor. 2 return, recur; of property rights, pass, PLond.3.1044.14 , 5.1727.46

ἐπανατρυγάω.definition: glean after the vintage, c. acc., LXXDe.24.21, Le.19.10

ἐπαναφέρω.definition: intr. in Act., rise or be referred to a cause, Pl.Ly.219c; put into the account, D.41.20, cf. IG22.1607a7

ἐπαναφυσάω.definition: play on the flute in accompaniment, Ar.Th.1175

ἐπαναφωνέω.definition: pronounce in addition or after, opp. S.E.M.1.130

ἐπαναχωρέω.definition: retreat, return, CharonFr.2, Ar.Lys.461, Th.6.49; Pherecr.59; Hdt.9.13; Th.1.63, cf. 3.96; Id.4.44; Pl.Lg.781e; return from . ., Plu.2.580a; withdraw from, PLond.5.1727.16

ἔπανδρος.definition: manly, Demad.37, Phld.Ir.p.65 W., Vett. Val.14.24, al.; D.S.4.50; IG4.951 ; masculine spirit, Corn.ND20; Hierocl.p.63 S. . Adv. S.E.M.11.107; CIG4239 , cf. SIG709.6

ἐπανείρομαι.definition: or , question again; ask again, Pl.Prt.329a, cf. Grg.451b; . . J.AJ18.6.6

ἐπανέρχομαι.definition: go back, return, Anacr.23; recur, of intermittent fevers, etc., Gal.7.412, 16.711

ἐπάνεσις.definition: abatement, of fevers; name of a bandage, Heliod. ap. Orib.48.43.1

ἐπανήκω.definition: pf. PAmh.2.50.5 :— to have come back, return, E.IA1628 , Pl.Com.68 , Ph.2.117; D.47.55; Plb.6.58.3; Paus.3.9.2; LXXPr.7.20

ἐπανθέω.definition: bloom, be in flower, Theoc.5.131, LXXJb.14.7; metaph., of any thing that forms on the surface, Hdt.2.12, cf. Str.11.13.2; Ar.Nu.978; . . Id.Ec.903; ib.13; also of hair turning grey, . . Id.V.1065, cf. X.Cyn.4.8

ἐπανθίζω.definition: deck as with flowers, make bright-coloured; metaph., deck as with flowers, decorate, adorn, A.Ch.150; Id.Th.949:—Pass., Philostr.VS1.15.4.—The aor. Med. is prob. corrupt in A.Ag.1459

ἐπανθρακίζω.definition: broil on the coals, Cratin.143 (cod. A; blacken with charcoal, AP11.66

ἐπανθρακόομαι.definition: Pass., to be broiled on the coals, Poll.6.55

ἐπανιάομαι.definition: to be annoyed at a thing, X.Eph.1.15, Poll.5.129

ἐπανίημι.definition: let go, give up, c. acc., D.2.30; dismiss, Id.18.177; remit, Plu.Lyc.22; release from, X.Cyn.7.1; relax, Ruf. ap. Orib.6.38.5

ἐπανισόω.definition: make equal, balance evenly, Th.8.57; IG22.1013.15; Just.Nov.92.1 Intr.; Ruf. ap. Orib.inc.4.2; Polyaen.7.16.2; reduce, Arist.Resp.478a3; the others like wise he made equal to one another, distributing to them their fa…

ἐπάνοδος.definition: return, LXXSi.17.24, etc.; Plu.Tim.38; Iamb.inNic.p.76P.; to one's country, E.Ep.2.2, cf. Hdn.8.7.7: metaph., ascent of the soul, Dam.Pr.75; simply, journey, PLips.45.17

ἐπανοιδέω.definition: swell up, rise on the surface, Hp.Nat.Mul.2, Arist.HA531b3:—Pass., in same sense, Hp.VC13

ἐπανορθόω.definition: impf. with double augm; correct, amend, revise, Pl.Lg.769e; Is.1.18; Pl.Prt.340d; correct one, teach him better, Ar.Lys.528, cf. Isoc.1.3, Iamb.l.c.; IG12.108.49:—Med. in proper sense, correct oneself, Pl.R.361a: but …

ἐπανορθωτής.definition: corrector, restorer, D.H.8.67; of writings, Gal.7.894; = Lat. corrector morum, D.C.54.30; also, = Lat. corrector civitatis, IG4.1417 , 5.541 , 7.91

ἐπαντιάζω.definition: to be present, prob. in h.Ap.152

ἐπαντλέω.definition: pump over or upon, pour over, Pl.Phd.112c ; Id.Phdr.253a; pour a flood of words over, E.Fr.899.4, cf. Ael.NA6.51; Diph.107; irrigate, Plu.2.688e: metaph., Philostr.VS1.25.2; Id.VA6.11: abs., Luc.Tim.18:—Pass., to be i…

ἐπάνω.definition: Adv., above, on the upper side or; as Prep., c. gen., Id.1.179 , Pl.Phd.109d; IG12.872.32 ; having risen superior to . ., Plu.2.1063c; J.BJ1.4.2; D.L.6.28

ἐπάξιος.definition: worthy, deserving of; deserved, Pi.I.4.44; worthy, meet, A.Th.865 ; S.El.971, etc.; meet with one's deserts, A.Pr.70. Adv. S.OT133, Iamb.Myst.3.20

ἐπαοιδία.definition: later form of foreg., Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.9, Hsch

ἐπαοιδός.definition: = LXXEx.7.11,22,al., Ph.1.449 , Arr.Epict.3.24.10, Man.5.183 . Adv. by way of a charm, Steph.in Hp.2.458D

ἐπαπερείδομαι.definition: Pass., lean upon, Posidon.26; support, Ph.Byz.Mir.6.2

ἐπαποδύω.definition: strip one for combat against another, set him up as a rival to, Plu.2.788d:—Med., strip and set to work at a thing, Ar.Lys.615; Ph.1.360; set upon, attack, Plu.Marc.3

ἐπαποθνήσκω.definition: die after another, Pl.Smp.180a, 208d, J.BJ5.12.3; die while yet speaking, Id.AJ13.11.3: abs., Plu.Aem.35

ἐπαπολαύω.definition: revel in, D.S.37.3: c. gen., Tz.H.9.315; profit by, Anon.in Rh.111.28

ἐπαπόλλυμι.definition: or kill in addition, Ael.NA10.48, Luc.Merc.Cond.42:—Med., die after, D.C.60.34: abs., Aristid.Or.25.22

ἐπαπόλογος.definition: in Arc. form requiring defence, SIG306.34

ἐπαπορητικός.definition: dubitative: a kind of rhetorical question, Stoic.2.61, cf. D.L.7.68; Gal.16.722. Adv. Phlp.inAPo.359.15, Eust.1114.30

ἐπαποστέλλω.definition: send to attack, Id.32.5.11; Id.2.8.12; D.S.12.24, cf. LXXJb.20.23

ἐπαράομαι.definition: Cret. part. Leg.Gort., Cyren; c. dat. only, curse solemnly, Pl.Lg.931b, Jul.Or.2.50b, Leg.Gort.2.40, etc

ἐπαράσσω.definition: Att. dash or clap to, Pl.Prt.314d, cf. Plu.Art.29; Hld.10.31; strike rods against the thin parts, Gal.10.998

ἐπαργυρόομαι.definition: to be overlaid with silver, IG22.1485.48: metaph., of costly dinners, . . Mnesim.3.2

ἐπάργυρος.definition: overlaid with silver, Hdt.1.50,9.80, cf. IG12.276, BMus.Inscr.4.481*.472; Onos.1.20

ἐπάρδευσις.definition: watering: hence, shower, of rain; irrigation, POxy. 1631.14 , al

ἐπάρδω.definition: irrigate, Arr.An.4.6.5: metaph., Luc.Am.45, cf. LXX4 Ma.1.29, Plot.6.7.33; Ph.2.345; Him.Ecl.32.6:—Pass., J.BJ4.8.3; of the body by nourishment, Ti.Locr.102b

ἐπαρέσκομαι.definition: to be satisfied, . . Eustr.in EN270.16: aor. Med., Hsch

ἐπαρηγών.definition: helper, A.R.1.1039, Milet.1.205a : c. gen., Orph.A.348, L.677

ἐπαριστερεύομαι.definition: to be awkward, clumsy, Hsch. s.v

ἐπαρίστερος.definition: towards the left, on the left hand; written from right to left, Tab.Defix.67a8

ἐπάρκεια.definition: help, support, Plb.1.48.5, al.: pl., Id.6.52.5; ib.49.7

ἐπαρκής.definition: helpful, Emp.22.4; of remedies; sufficient, Plu.Cic.7, cf. D.P.1101. Adv. IG4.491

ἐπαρχεία.definition: office of praefectus, IG12.336.22; = I SIG683.65 , IG14.951 , etc

ἐπαρχιώτης.definition: a provincial, Hadrian.Epist. ap. Justin. M.Apol.1.68, Jul.Ep.14, BGU1024vi24 :—also written Just.Nov.128.21, al., Cod.Just.1.33.4

ἐπαρωγός.definition: helper, aider, Od.11.498, E.Hec.164 , etc.: also fem., A.R.4.196: neut., AP6.219.21

ἐπασθμαίνω.definition: breathe hard, pant in working, LXX4 Ma.6.11; Philostr.Jun.Im.5

ἐπασπιδόομαι.definition: Pass., take as a shield, cj. in Ph.1.669 ; cf

ἐπαστράπτω.definition: lighten upon, Plu.2.594e: metaph., Lib.Or.61.10: abs., AP7.49 : c. acc. cogn., flash fire, APl.4.141 ; Nonn.D.18.74

ἐπασφαλίζω.definition: shore up, PLond.1.131r44; close up a wound, Paul.Aeg.6.67

ἐπαυδάω.definition: call to or say in addition, Hsch., Suid.:—Med., call upon, invoke, S.Ph.395

ἐπαύλιον.definition: Dim. of sq. 2, SIG344.98 (Teos, iv; or the day after the wedding, Id.3.49, Poll.3.39, Hsch., Suid.; also, presents given to the bride, Poll. l.c

ἐπαύξησις.definition: increase, increment, Pl.Lg.957d; PTeb. 27.47 ; Plu.Sol.15; to their profit, Plb.5.88.6

ἐπαύρεσις.definition: enjoyment of the fruit of a thing, fruition, . . Hdt.7.158; Th.2.53; Democr.278

ἐπαϋτέω.definition: make a noise or creak besides; = Call.Ap.102, Q.S.4.262; Theoc.22.91; of horses, Q.S.11.327: c. acc. cogn., Call.Dian.58

ἐπαφαίρεσις.definition: a fresh taking away of blood, Aret.CA1.1, Archig. ap. Gal.8.150, Philum. ap. Orib.45.29.1; of a beard, Mart.8.52

ἐπαφαυαίνομαι.definition: Pass., to be withered: hence I was quite spent with laughing, Ar.Ra.1089

ἐπαφάω.definition: touch on the surface, touch lightly, Hecat.22 J., A.Pr.849, Trag.Adesp.458.7, Pl.Cra.404d:—also in Med., abs., Hp.Mul.2.165: c. gen., Mosch.2.50; AP5.221.1 ; Alciphr.3.12: c. acc., IG14.2123

ἐπαφή.definition: touch, touching, handling; severe handling, punishment, ib.46d; esp. of Pythagorean treatment, Iamb.VP15.64 , 25.114

ἐπαφίημι.definition: throw at, discharge at, X.Cyr.4.1.3; let in upon, Thphr.CP2.5.5:— Pass., Jul.Or.1.30a

ἐπαφροδισία.definition: loveliness, elegance, Lync. ap. Ath.6.242c, Ptol.Tetr.86, Vett. Val.160.13; D.Chr.37.33; Artem.2.20; charm, PSI4.328.6 , UPZ33.9 , PMag. Osl.1.224, PMag.Lond.122.5, etc

ἐπαφρόδιτος.definition: lovely, fascinating; used to translate Sulla's epithet Felix, favoured by Venus, i.e. fortune's favourite , Plu.Sull.34, App.BC1.97

ἐπαχθής.definition: heavy, ponderous; metaph., burdensome, grievous, A.Pr.49; Pl.Phd.87a; Id.Lg.688d; not to say anything offensive, D.18.10; Arist.EN1127b8: Sup. Phalar.Ep.1; Ph.2.402; invidiousness, offence, Pl.Euthd.303e; Id.Prt.316d.…

ἐπαχθίζομαι.definition: to be burdened with . ., Ph.2.103, 113; ib.288: abs., ib.450

ἐπεγγελάω.definition: fut. Ep. iterative Q.S.14.397: —laugh at, exult over, S.Aj.989, X.An.2.4.27; S.Aj.969; J.AJ11.6.10: abs., S.Aj.454, Aeschin.2.182, Phld.Mort.20; Opp.H.2.303: c. acc. cogn., Aristaenet.2.6

ἐπεγγυάω.definition: = Lex ap.Lys.10.17; 3pl. impf. SIG 705.43 :—Pass., Dor. pres. part. Sophr.60

ἐπεγκαλέω.definition: bring a charge against, Lys.8.1; Procop.Arc.18; Gal.18.295; c. inf., Hierocl.in CA25p.477M.:—Med., Olymp.in Alc.p.155 C

ἐπεγκανάσσω.definition: drink or pour in besides, Hsch

ἐπεγκεράννυμαι.definition: Med., mix in with, Pl.Plt.273d, Nic.Al.166, etc.; Plu.2.1025b

ἐπεγκύκλιος.definition: circular, of bandages, Sor.Fasc.12.512,516 C., Gal.18.815

ἐπεγχέω.definition: poet. Nic.Fr.72.5:—pour in upon or besides, A.Ag.1137 , Philox.2.40; E.Cyc.423; pour in fresh water, Hp.Int.1

ἐπεγχυματίζω.definition: wash out the throat afterwards; give a clyster afterwards, Dsc.5.15

ἐπεικάζω.definition: surmise, guess, am I right in surmising that she is his wife? S.El.663; A.Ch.14, cf. 567; as one may read the riddle of their fates, ib.976; as far as one may guess, Hdt.9.32; S.OC152 ; Id.Tr.1220

ἐπείρομαι.definition: inf. v.l. in Hdt.7.101, al.: impf; c. acc. pers., ask or question him besides, about a thing, Ar.Lys.98, v.l. in Hdt.7.101; Id.1.158; with relat., Id.3.22; Id.4.161

ἐπειρωνεύομαι.definition: speak ironically, App.BC4.70, J.BJ5.13.1: c. dat., mock at, ib.1.3.6

ἐπεισάγω.definition: bring in besides or over, esp. of; bring in something new or strange, Aeschin.1.166, etc.; Plb.32.5.11; introduce, Jul.Or.2.88d:—Med., Plb.10.28.3

ἐπεισαγώγιμος.definition: brought in from abroad, imported wares, Pl.R.370e

ἐπεισβάλλω.definition: throw into besides, E.El.498; intr., invade again, Th.3.13; of a double attack of fever, Gal.7.352; simply, attack, Palaeph.1

ἐπεισβιάζομαι.definition: force one's way in besides, intrude, Inscrr. on grave- stones, CIG3996 , etc

ἐπείσειμι.definition: come in besides; come in after, Hp.Prorrh.2.1; Pl.Ti.81d

ἐπεισέρρω.definition: rush in with ill luck to one, Poll.9.158, Suid

ἐπεισέρχομαι.definition: come in besides, to one, Th.8.35; come in after, Hdt.1.37; Pl.Prt.316a; and freq. in Att.; D.H.Dem.8

ἐπεισκομίζω.definition: bring in besides, CIG 3882i , cf. Rev.Phil. 36.53

ἐπεισκρίνομαι.definition: Pass., to be overcharged with; replace losses, S.E.P.3.82

ἐπεισκυκλέω.definition: roll or bring in one upon another, 'pile up', Luc.Hist.Conscr.13; S.E.P.2.210; Gal.8.575; Longin.22.4:—Pass., Id.11.1; Luc.Deor.Conc.9, cf.Philops.29

ἐπεισκωμάζω.definition: rush in like disorderly revellers, Pl.R.500b; of tyrants, Stoic. 3.191: Metaph. of arguments, Pl.Tht.184a, cf. Luc.Pseudol.11: c. acc., Aristox.Fr.Hist.15: c. dat., make an inroad upon, Aristid.Or.22 .8

ἐπεισοδιάζω.definition: import, introduce from without, Ph.1.134:— Pass., ib.592

ἐπεισοδιόω.definition: vary by introducing episodes, Arist.Po.1455b1; Id.Rh.1418a33

ἐπείσοδος.definition: coming in besides, approach, S.OC730, Fr.273; entrance from without, Epicur.Nat.21 G., Placit.4.22.1; Orib.Fr.38; Ph.1.76

ἐπεισπαίω.definition: burst in, Ar.Pl.805; Com.Adesp.439: abs., Luc.DMeretr.15.1

ἐπεισπηδάω.definition: leap in upon, X.Cyr.3.3.64; usurp, Philostr.VA2.31, cf. Just.Nov.42 Pr.: abs., Ar.Eq.363, D.47.56, D.C.67.17

ἐπεισρέω.definition: flow in upon or besides, Trag.Adesp.89, Ph.Fr.73 H., Plu.Num.20, Luc.Alex.49

ἐπειστρέχω.definition: aor. Jul.Caes.309c:—run in upon or after, l.c.: abs., Ph.2.128

ἐπεισφέρω.definition: bring in besides or next, Hp.Art.4 ; A.Ag.864; Id.Ch.649 ; bring in a new argument, Ar.Th.1164; in Inscrr. on grave- stones, bring in another body, CIG3384 , al.:—Med., bring in for oneself, Th.3.53:—Pass., rush in be…

ἐπεισφοιτάω.definition: to be in the habit of coming in, Ph.1.615

ἐπεισφρέω.definition: bring in or introduce besides; intr., come in besides, Suid

ἐπεκβαίνω.definition: go out upon, disembark, Th.8.105: abs., Id.1.49: c. acc., of waves, go out over, AP7.393 , 9.276

ἐπεκδιδάσκω.definition: teach or explain besides, Pl.Prt.328e; . . Id.Euthphr.7a; . . Plu.Sol.25; Plb.15.35.7:—Pass., Gal.Libr.Propr.1

ἐπεκδίδωμι.definition: farm out a contract again, IG7.3073.38; publish again, Sch.Il.19.365

ἐπεκδρομή.definition: sally, sortie, Th.4.25, Procop.Vand.2.8, al.; raid, D.C.46.38

ἐπέκκρισις.definition: secretion or expulsion of bodies, cj. in Leucipp. ap. D.L.9.32

ἐπεκροφέω.definition: swallow up, dub. l. in Ar.Eq.701; v

ἐπεκτείνω.definition: stretch, Sor.1.10 , al.; extend; intr., extend, Id.APo.96a24; of a people or country, . . Str.8.3.11: c. dat., extend over, Olymp.in Mete.75.12

ἐπεκτίνω.definition: Cret. aor. inf. pay up, GDI 4993

ἐπεκφέρω.definition: carry out, f. l. for in; seek to enforce a contract, PEleph.1.14,16

ἐπεκχέω.definition: pour out upon, Anon. ap. Suid. s.v. rush upon, LXXJu.15.4, cf. PTeb.39.24 ; to be stretched upon, Q.S.10.481

ἐπέλασις.definition: charge, of cavalry, Arr.Tact.16.10 , al.; Plu.Tim.27, cf. Jul.Or.2.60b, Agath.1.14, al.; of elephants, Luc.Hist.Conscr.31

ἐπελαφρύνω.definition: lighten, Plu.2.165e; J.AJ18.1.1, cf. D.Chr.3.123, Max. Tyr.37.5, Hierocl.in CA15p.454M

ἐπεμβάλλω.definition: put on, Hes.Op.98; throw down upon, will throw them on [the inmates], E.HF864: c. acc. loci, that she may dash [her] upon it , Id.IT290

ἐπέμβασις.definition: attack, advance, D.H.3.19; Astrol., commencement of Man.5.80, Ptol.Tetr.141, al., Paul.Al.R.3

ἐπεμβαφίζω.definition: bathe again, Hsch. s.v. glossed by

ἐπεμβλέπω.definition: gaze at, prob. l. in D.Chr.4.95

ἐπεμβρίθω.definition: bear heavily on, c. acc., PFlor.93.14 :—Med., overcome, PMasp. 153.13

ἐπεμβριμάομαι.definition: to be indignant, rage against, Sch. rec.A.Pr.73

ἐπενδικάζω.definition: contest a claim in court, BGU1105.31

ἐπένδυμα.definition: upper garment, Aq.Ex.28.26, al., f.l. in Plu.Alex.32

ἐπενδύτης.definition: robe or garment worn over another, Ps.-Thesp.1, S.Fr.439, LXX1 Ki.18.4; Nicoch.5, cf. Ael.Dion.Fr.325, Poll.7.45

ἐπένθεσις.definition: insertion, as of a letter, A.D.Pron.82.4; of a word, Id.Synt.78.24, Phlp.in APo.186.26; application of a drug, Paul.Aeg.6.42

ἐπενθρῴσκω.definition: leap upon, Pi.Pae.6.115; A.Pers.359; S.Tr.917; leap forth after or upon one, as an enemy, Id.OT469

ἐπενθυμέομαι.definition: support, corroborate a conclusion by additional argument, Hermog.Inv.3.9

ἐπενθύμησις.definition: insertion of a corroborative argument, Id.Meth.5 , Greg. Cor. in Rh.7.1147 W

ἐπέντασις.definition: stretching, of the of an engine, Ph.Bel.67.24 , 25

ἐπεντίθημι.definition: insert a letter, A.D.Adv.148.8 ; a word, Id.Synt.88.5; a drug into a cavity, Paul.Aeg.6.14:—Pass., to be put in besides, CIG4429

ἐπεντρίβω.definition: rub in besides, Poll.5.102; inflict, Eust.219.18

ἐπεξαγωγή.definition: extension of a line of battle, Id.8.105

ἐπεξαμαρτάνω.definition: sin or err yet more, D.H.2.35; Ph.2.346; against one, J.AJ14.16.4

ἐπεξανίστημι.definition: Pass. with aor. 2 Act. rise up, stand up, Ph.2.582

ἐπεξελαύνω.definition: send on to the attack, X.HG5.3.6

ἐπεξέλευσις.definition: visitation, punishment, Ph.2.569; traversing of ground in argument, Eustr.in EN316.23

ἐπεξεργάζομαι.definition: slay over again, S.Ant.1288; work anew, Luc.Tim.37

ἐπεξεργασία.definition: investigation, Ptol.Tetr.117; elaboration, Eustr.in EN135.16, Sch.Il.11.226; carrying into effect of a law, Just.Nov.99Pr

ἐπεξέρχομαι.definition: march out, make a sally; proceed against, prosecute, Antipho1.1: generally, Th.3.38; attack, Pl.Prt.345d; proceed against one for murder, Id.Euthphr.4d; also Id.Lg.866b; follow it up, Lex ap. D.21.47; Antipho2.1.2: ab…

ἐπεξευρίσκω.definition: devise or discover besides, Hdt.2.160; J.AJ15.8.5:—Pass., Arist.Pol.1331a14

ἐπεξηγέομαι.definition: recount in detail, Plu.Art.8; explain besides, Asp.in EN48.20, Sch.Il.13.281

ἐπεξορκίζω.definition: compel to swear a second time, Plb.15.25.11

ἐπεργάζομαι.definition: cultivate besides, encroach upon; esp. encroach upon sacred ground, Lys.7.24, Aeschin.3.113; . . . . . . IG22.1126.15

ἐπεργασία.definition: cultivation of another's land; right of mutual tillage in each other's territory, X.Cyr.3.2.23

ἐπέρεισις.definition: pressure, Dsc.5.77, Sor.2.10, Heliod. ap. Orib.10.37.7, Gal.2.386; of the objects of sense, impact, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.233, al

ἐπερεύγομαι.definition: Pass., to be disgorged upon: of water, to be poured upon, A.R.4.631; D.P.95

ἐπερωτάω.definition: Ion. consult, inquire of, c; c. acc. rei, ask a question, Hdt.1.30,55, cf. Antipho1.10; also, ask about a thing, Hdt.7.100; call it in question, Pl.Prt.329a; inquire what . ., X.Oec.5.19; . . inquire about, LXX2 Ki.11…

ἐπιθερμαίνομαι.definition: Pass., become feverish, Hp.Epid.1.1; later in Act., warm up, PHolm.17.40

ἐπίθετος.definition: additional, D.H.3.71; esp. at; fictitious, Thphr.HP9.8.8; opp. D.H.4.70, cf. 68

ἐπιθεώρησις.definition: inspection, CPHerm.7 ii 23; Astrol., aspect, Ptol.Tetr.193

ἐπιθηματουργία.definition: making of lids or covers, Pl.Plt.280d

ἐπιθηραρχία.definition: contingent of four elephants, Ascl.Tact.9, Ael.Tact.23

ἐπιθιγγάνω.definition: aor.2 touch, Thphr.Od.11; reach as far as, Id.2.921d

ἐπιθλίβω.definition: press upon the surface, D.S.3.14; tread, Nonn.D.7.91; crowd round, App.BC4.45: metaph., repress, check, Plu.2.782d

ἐπιθολόω.definition: make turbid, Luc.Ind.7, Max.Tyr.33.5: metaph., Plu.in Hes.66; Philostr.V A6.11; Iamb.VP24.107; Agath.3.11:—Pass., become turbid, Placit.3.5.8, Gal.6.57, Luc.Lex.4: metaph., Artem.4Prooem.; Iamb.in Nic.p.4P., cf. Myst.…

ἐπιθόρνυμαι.definition: cover, of the male, Luc.Am.22, etc.; Philostr.V A5.29, cf. Im.2.3: abs., Ael.N.A.10.2, al

ἐπιθορυβέω.definition: in token of displeasure, X.HG1.7.13, Luc.Asin.54

ἐπιθρηνέω.definition: lament over, Babr.118.8: abs., Plu.2.123c, Diog.Oen.61: c. acc. cogn., Hld.10.37

ἐπιθρύπτω.definition: enfeeble, enervate, Philostr.V A1.37:—Pass., practise affectations, Aristaenet.1.28; effeminate, Plu.Dio17

ἐπιθυμέω.definition: set one's heart upon a thing, long for, covet, desire, c. gen. rei, Hdt.2.66, A.Ag.216, etc.: also c. gen. pers., Lys.3.5, X.An.4.1.14 ); of political attachments, And.4.28; Lys.20.3: c. inf., desire to do, Hdt.1.24; …

ἐπιθύμημα.definition: object of desire, Id.Lg.687c; yearning, desire, Hp.de Arte1, Antipho Soph.110, Epicur.Fr.141: pl., Philyll.30

ἐπιθυμία.definition: Ion. desire, yearning; c. gen., longing after a thing, desire of or for it, Th.2.52, 7.84, etc.; Democr.224; Antipho2.1.7; And.2.10; Pl.Cra.406b; Id.Criti.113d; Id.Prt.318a, Tht.143e; Id.Lg.841c; Id.Ti.19b; X.Cyr.1.1.…

ἐπιθυμιάω.definition: offer incense, Plu.Alex.25, CIG2715.6 : c.acc., prob. in Men.260 , cf. Plu.2.372d; Milet.3.145 , SIG694.43 , Artem.4.2:—Pass., Dsc.1.68

ἐπιθύνω.definition: = S.Ph.1059: Ep. Iterat. A.R.3.1325: c.dat., Man.2.340

ἐπίθυσις.definition: burning of incense, BMus.Inscr.789 , Ph.Bybl. ap. Eus.PE1.10 codd.; OGI383.142

ἐπιθωρακίζομαι.definition: put on one's armour, v.l. for

ἐπικαγχαλάω.definition: exult in, Q.S.1.161; exult over, ib.643: abs., Id.2.374

ἐπικαθαιρέω.definition: pull down or destroy besides, Th.8.20

ἐπικαθαίρω.definition: purge yet more, Hp.Judic.11, Ruf. ap. Orib.7.26.169 ; of supplementary menstruation, Sor.1.28

ἐπικαθέζομαι.definition: sit down upon, Ar.Pl.185; to be supported, rest on, HeroBel.83.11, cf. J.AJ8.3.5

ἐπικαθεύδω.definition: sleep upon, Luc.Ind.4; sit on eggs, Arist.HA542b20: metaph., go to sleep over, i.e.neglect, Just.Nov.88.2.1

ἐπικάθημαι.definition: Ion. sit upon, Hdt.6.72; sit at his counter, of a banker's clerk or money-changer, D.49.17, cf. 33: abs., Id.36.7

ἐπικαθίζω.definition: set upon, Hp.Art.78: abs., (sc; Intr., sit upon, Eup.94.5; light upon, Plu.Them.12, cf. Thphr.CP6.10.5

ἐπικαθικνέομαι.definition: Dor.3sg. fut. impose a surcharge or penalty, IG5.1421.15

ἐπικαθίστημι.definition: set upon, establish, D.C.41.50; set over, Pl.Ti.72b

ἐπικαθυγραίνομαι.definition: to be kept moist, Sor.1.44, Orib.Fr.144, Paul.Aeg.3.63

ἐπικαίνυμαι.definition: Pass., to be adorned or furnished with, 20.35 ; Q.S.12.145

ἐπικαιρία.definition: opportunity, Hp.Gland.4; title of work by Democr., D.L.9.48

ἐπικαίριος.definition: important, X.Oec.15.11; of persons, the most important persons of the army, Id.Cyr.3.3.12, cf. HG3.3.11: c.inf., those whose cure is all- important, Id.Cyr.8.2.25

ἐπικαίω.definition: light up or kindle on a place, h.Ap.491; burn on the surface, scorch, Hp.Aër.17 ; Pl.Ep.340d; Plb.38.8.7, cf. Apollon.Mir.23; Antipho Soph.26; of lightning, Arist.Mete.371b14; of hot iron, Id.HA631b26; of cold, Hp.Aër…

ἐπικαλέω.definition: summon a god to a sacrifice or as witness to; pray for, PLond.5.1676.24

ἐπικαμπή.definition: bend, return or angle of a building; draw up their army angular-wise, i.e. with the wings thrown forward at an angle with the centre, so as to take the enemy in flank, X.Cyr.7.1.6; Arr.An.2.9.2, cf. 3.12.2

ἐπικαμπής.definition: curved, curling, BGU781 ii4 ; Luc.Gall.28; Plu.Cam.32; convex, Pall.in Hp.Fract.12.284C.; of hammer-toes, Heph.Astr.1.1. Adv. Sch.rec.A.Th.384

ἐπικάμπιος.definition: Subst. = Arr.Tact.26.7; Ael.Tact.31.4; opp. Polyaen.4.3.22, cf. Plb.5.82.9; also of fleets in naval warfare, Id.1.27.4

ἐπικάμπτω.definition: bend into an angle; Act., move to pity, Lib.Decl.46.13:—Pass., abs., Ctes.Fr.29.56, Lib.Or.6.38; Id.Loc.1.31

ἐπικαμπύλος.definition: crooked, curved, in the shoulders, h.Merc.90; Hes.Op.427

ἐπικαρπία.definition: produce, crop, Pl.Lg.955d; harvest-rights, Tab.Heracl.1.108, BGU101.19 ; usufruct, D.H.3.58

ἐπικαρπίζομαι.definition: draw the nutriment from, exhaust, of crops, Thphr.HP8.9.3

ἐπικαταβαίνω.definition: go down to a place; go down after or against an enemy, Hdt.8.38, Th.4.11, 7.84

ἐπικαταβάλλω.definition: let fall down or droop at a thing, X.Cyn.4.3; impose a fine, Tab.Heracl.1.134, where for Ahrens corrected

ἐπικατάγνυμαι.definition: to be broken upon, of eggs; pf. part. Pass. perh. = weak, Cat.Cod. Astr.8.188

ἐπικατάγω.definition: work out a calculation; usu. in Pass., of ships or persons at sea, come to land along with or afterwards, Th.3.49, 8.28, J.AJ18.7.2, D.Chr.37.4, D.C.42.7, etc

ἐπικαταδαρθάνω.definition: aor. 2 fall asleep afterwards, Th.4.133, Pl.R.534d

ἐπικαταδέω.definition: bind upon or to, Hp.Epid.5.58, Luc.Asin.16,34

ἐπικαταδύνω.definition: dive after, Poll.1.108; of stars, set after, Procl.Hyp.5.52; Gem.9.1:—also Med., Cleom.1.3, Theo Sm.p.138 H

ἐπικατάδυσις.definition: setting of a star just after; Astrol., name of eighth Antioch. Astr.inCat.Cod.Astr.8.117.11

ἐπικατακλίνω.definition: make bend down upon; introduce as a concubine, J.AJ1.10.4

ἐπικατακολουθέω.definition: attend to, Sch.Pi.O.6.108: abs., comply, PLille4.6

ἐπικαταλαμβάνω.definition: follow and catch up, overtake; of fruit which forms before the last year's fruit is ripe, overtakes it, Thphr.HP2.6.10

ἐπικαταλείπω.definition: bequeath in addition, Ramsay Studies in the Eastern Rom.Emp.345

ἐπικαταπίπτω.definition: fall upon, Luc.Anach.1; Q.S.3.399; metaph., fall to the lot of, Id.7.78

ἐπικαταπλάσσω.definition: put on a plaster as well, Hp.Fract.25

ἐπικαταπλέω.definition: bear down upon, of ships, D.S.16.66, Charito8.6

ἐπικαταράομαι.definition: bring curses, LXXNu.5.19,22; call down; curse , ib.Ma.2.2

ἐπικαταράσσομαι.definition: Pass., fall with a crash, D.H.10.16, 11.26

ἐπικαταρρήγνυμι.definition: tear, rend, J.AJ2.6.7:—Pass; Pass., to be violently purged, Gal.16.691

ἐπικατασκάπτω.definition: destroy, D.H.1.39; throw down upon, Id.4.48; J.AJ13.13.3; destroy as well, App.Ill.8, al

ἐπικατασκευάζω.definition: bring about in addition, J.BJ4.3.3; Med., establish by additional arguments, Arg.D.46

ἐπικατασπάω.definition: draw down after, Arist.Pr.901a2:—Pass., to be drawn in afterwards, Hp.Vict.3.70

ἐπικατασπένδω.definition: pour besides as a libation over, J.BJ1.3.6

ἐπικατάστασις.definition: in Tactics, wheeling through four right angles and return to original point, Ascl.Tact.10.1, 9

ἐπικαταστρέφω.definition: invert and put over, Gp.10.56.6, cf. Dsc.5.79; Sch.S.Ant.134

ἐπικατασφάζω.definition: later Phld.Ir.p.36; slay in succession or after, D.H.3.20, App.Hann.59, al

ἐπικατατέμνω.definition: carry the workings of a mine beyond one's boundaries, D.37.36

ἐπικαταφέρω.definition: fell, knock down on top of; Pass., of stars, follow the sun, Nech. ap. Vett.Val.279.22, Anon. in Ptol.Tetr.22; name of eighth Thrasyll.inCat.Cod.Astr.8.101

ἐπικαταφορά.definition: Astrol., name of eighth Firm.2.19.9, 7.6.8, al.; cf. II

ἐπικατάφορος.definition: prone to, or Terpsicles ap.Ath.9.391e, Ath.13.608d

ἐπικαταχρίω.definition: in Med., smear oneself with, Orib.Fr.85

ἐπικαταψεύδομαι.definition: tell lies besides, Hdt.3.63, Th.8.74; accuse falsely, J.AJ17.5.5

ἐπικάτειμι.definition: go down into, Th.2.49: abs., of persons, J.AJ1.19.3: metaph., descend in the scale, Dam.Pr.87

ἐπικατέχω.definition: detain, D.H.9.60, Luc.Herm.23, Arg. Cratin. in POxy.663.39; restrain, D.Chr.3.34

ἐπικατηγορέω.definition: predicate of a thing besides, S.E.M.9.334; attribute to . . , Plu.2.1113b; D.H.1.66 :—Pass., to be added to the predicate, Arist.APr.49a25; to be predicated of, c. dat., Iamb.in Nic.p.34P

ἐπικατηγορία.definition: further predication or characterization, Demetr.Lac.Herc.1012.41 F., al., cf. S.E.M.10.297

ἐπικατορύσσομαι.definition: Pass., to be buried after, Antipho3.2.10

ἐπικαττύω.definition: mend shoes, Poll.7.82; metaph., vamp up old plays, Com.Adesp.46

ἐπικελαδέω.definition: shout at or to, esp.in applause, cheer, Il.8.542

ἐπικελεύω.definition: exhort, encourage, cheer on, c. dat; give consent or authorization, PPetr.3p.133 , PTeb.201

ἐπικέλομαι.definition: call upon, Il.9.454; A.Supp.40 : c. dat., A.R.3.85

ἐπικεντρίζω.definition: apply the spur, AP9.777; graft vines, Gp.5.17.11

ἐπικεντρόομαι.definition: Astron., occupy a cardinal point, cj. for Antioch.Astr.inCat.Cod.Astr.8.115

ἐπίκεντρος.definition: Astron., occupying a cardinal point, Vett.Val.9.19, Man.1.34, Doroth.ap.Heph.Astr.2.5, S.E.M.5.40: Comp., Ptol.Tetr.79

ἐπικέντρωσις.definition: occupation of a cardinal point, Paul.Al.P.1

ἐπικερδής.definition: profitable, advantageous, TAM2.245 , Aesop.137, Vett.Val.189.30, al., Heph.Astr.2.30, App.BC1.57

ἐπικεφάλαιος.definition: of or for the head, Suid; Subst. = Arist.Oec.1346a4, POxy.1157.14 ; SIG1009.4

ἐπικεφαλαιόω.definition: add up, Vett.Val.260.21:— Med., sum up; Pass., to be summed up, D.C.52.28

ἐπικεφάλιον.definition: poll-tax, IGRom.4.181 , IG12.724.11, POxy.1438.14 , : more freq. in pl., Cic.Att.5.16.2, BGU833, Wilcken Chr.28 , POxy.2131.10 , etc

ἐπικέφαλον.definition: head of battering-ram, Ath.Mech.23.8; money distributed at so much a head, head-money, IG12.946.22 ; = Hsch

ἐπικηδεύω.definition: form connexions by; bury, Hsch. s.v

ἐπικηραίνω.definition: to be hostile to one, Hsch

ἐπικηρυκεία.definition: sending an embassy to treat for peace, entering into negotiation, D.5.18, cf. Plb.14.2.13, Theopomp.Hist.209

ἐπικηρυκεύομαι.definition: send ambassadors to treat for peace, make proposals for a treaty of peace, to one, Ar.Th.336, Th.4.27; Hdt.4.80,6.97; Ar.Th.1163

ἐπικηρύσσω.definition: esp. of penalties, . . proclaim death as the penalty, X.HG1.1.15; set a price on his head, Hdt.7.214 ; D.I.c.; issue letters of marque, Plb.4.26.7:—Pass., . . Hdt.7.213; the price set upon one's head, Nymphod.12, cf. …

ἐπικίνδυνος.definition: in danger, insecure; dangerous, Gorg.Pal.4 ; Pl.R.467d; Phld.Ir.p.29 W.; Pl.Lg.736c, cf. X.Mem.4.6.10; Id.An.1.3.19; to one, Hp.Aph.4.16, Th.3.54; there is danger, Arist.HA588a10

ἐπικινέω.definition: Act.only as f.l. for or , Iamb.VP 3.17:—Pass., to be moved, Luc.Asin.6; gesticulate at a thing. v.l. Epict.Ench.33.10: metaph., to be moved, zealous, LXX1 Es.8.69; also, to be moved to passion, Phld.Piet.21

ἐπικίρνημι.definition: Ion. for Heraclit.All.35, Philum. ap. Orib.45.29.8:—Pass., Hdt.1.51, Plu.2.270a, cf. Heraclit.All.40

ἐπικλείω.definition: Ep. Att. shut to, close, Ar.Pax101 ; Tryph.200:-Med., Luc.Tox.50:-Pass., to be shut to, opp. X.Eq.12.6: c. dat., to be covered by . . , Gal.18.429

ἐπικλῄζω.definition: = 3, Orph.A.1359, cf. Poet.deherb.154:—Pass., Poet. ap. D.L.6.100, App.Syr.17

ἐπικλήρωσις.definition: assignment by lot, SIG333.29 , Milet.3 No. 143.31

ἐπίκλησις.definition: surname, additional name; used by; after Hom., in other cases, surname, name, Th.1.3, etc

ἐπίκλητος.definition: called upon, called in as ally; specially summoned, held a privy council, Hdt.7.8 ; privy councillors, among the Persians, Hdt.8.101, 9.42; committee of a council, SIG353.2 , Str.14.1.21

ἐπικλίνεια.definition: inclination, bend, Heliod. ap; tendency, Gal.17 .726

ἐπικλινής.definition: prone, inclined, Them.Or.15.187b; Ph.1.252. Adv. ib.37,al

ἐπίκλιντρον.definition: couch, arm-chair, Ar.Ec.907; back of a couch or chair, IG11 .144 A 66, B 8 , Gp.13.14.9

ἐπίκλισις.definition: slope, Str.1.3.7; inclination towards, Antip. ap.Stob.4.22.25, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.175

ἐπικλονέω.definition: urge violently on, A.R.3.687; Q.S.8.426:— Pass., rush like a tide upon, of persons, A.R.1.783; of storms, Q.S.14.501

ἐπικλύζω.definition: Aeschin.3.173:—overflow, flood; metaph., deluge, swamp, E.Tr.1327 , cf. Theoc.25.201; A.R.3.695; Ph.1.91; Luc.Pseudol.25; Lib.Decl.50.44; Jul.Or.1.8b:—Pass., Id.ad Them.257c

ἐπίκλυσις.definition: overflow, flood, Th.3.89; Thphr.Fr.171.11: pl., Them.Or.13.167b

ἐπίκοιλος.definition: porous, spongy, Hp.VC1 ; cj. for in Sor.1.122

ἐπικοιμάομαι.definition: fall asleep after a thing, Hp.Aph.5.27; overlay, LXX3 Ki.3.19; J.AJ8.2.2

ἐπίκοινος.definition: common to many, promiscuous; Gramm., common, of gender, D.T.634.19, Gell.13.7.3. Adv. A.D.Conj.253.20

ἐπικοινόω.definition: Med., share, ib.1.4:— Pass., to be shared with, Pl.Lg.631d

ἐπικοινωνέω.definition: communicate with, Hp.Prog.7; share in a thing with one, what letters has it in common? Pl.Cra.394c; having nothing in common with . . , Aeschin.3.44: generally, share in, c.gen., Ph.1.561

ἐπικοίτιος.definition: at bedtime, of self- examination, Hierocl.in CA19p.460M

ἐπικομίζω.definition: bring or carry to, Str.11.2.17, cf. Arist. ap. D.L.5.14 :—Med., bring with one, J.AJ2.15.2; D.C.50.11, cf. PLips.41.10

ἐπικομπάζω.definition: add boastingly, E.HF981; Plu.Cam.22: abs., boast, Ph.1.550

ἐπικόπανον.definition: chopping-block, billet, Men.33, IG11.199 B89 , Poll.10.101

ἐπίκοπος.definition: of coins, re-stamped, EM360.41, Hsch; Act., for cutting: as Subst., = Luc.DMort.10.9, Eust.1476.33; support for cutting upon, in surgery, Heliod. ap. Orib.44.23.66, Antyll.ib.18, Gal.2.685

ἐπικορύφωσις.definition: culmination, terminal number of an arithmetical series, Nicom.Ar.2.3

ἐπικοσμέω.definition: add ornaments to, decorate after or besides, Hdt.1.184; adorn, Hyp.Eux.24,25; IG22.1277; Arist.PA658a32; honour them with . . , Hdt.7.228; honour, celebrate, Ar.Ra.385; of funeral honours, X.Cyr.7.3.11: abs., Demetr.E…

ἐπίκοτος.definition: wrathful, vengeful, Pi.Fr.109.4; Pass., hateful, S.Fr.428

ἐπικοτταβίζω.definition: throw the cottabus on or at, Poll.6.110, prob.f.l. for

ἐπικούρημα.definition: protection, X.An.4.5.13; remedy, Gal.6.171: pl., aids, succours, Iamb.Protr.20

ἐπικούρησις.definition: succour, protection, Antipho Soph.Oxy.1364.158; Euryph. ap. Stob.4.39.27; against evils, E.Andr.28; Pl.Lg.919b

ἐπίκουρος.definition: helper, ally, Hom. only in Il., mostly; mercenary troops, opp. citizen-soldiers, Th.2.33, cf. Hdt.1.154, 2.163, 3.145, Lys.12.94, X.HG7.1.12, etc.; Hermipp.63.18; used as body-guard by tyrants, Hdt.1.64, 6.39, Th.6.55,58

ἐπικραδαίνω.definition: wave on high, Hld.3.1; quiver, Poll.5.61

ἐπικρανῖτις.definition: pl. top course of a wall, IG12.372.16, al

ἐπικράτεια.definition: predominance, in heredity, Placit.5.7.6; S.E.P.1.80; named from its dominant element, opp. Gal.15.74, cf. 5.672, 17.216; Placit.4.9.9: Gramm., prevalence, authority, A.D.Synt.256.26, al.; numerical superiority, ib.326.14

ἐπικρατής.definition: master of a thing: only Comp. superior in . . , Th.6.88; having the upper hand of . . , D.C.55.30; Memn.34.3; with success, D.S.37.2.—Hom. only in Adv. with overwhelming might, impetuously, Il.16.67,81,23.863 ; so Hes…

ἐπικράτησις.definition: mastering, conquest of; supreme power, D.C.47.21

ἐπικρατήτωρ.definition: ruling star, Ps.-Ptol.Centil.25, cf. Vett.Val.132.15, etc

ἐπικραυγάζω.definition: cry out to or at, Arr.Epict.1.21.3,4.1.19

ἐπικρεμάννυμι.definition: Pass., aor. overhang, of a rock, h.Ap.284; Plu.Publ.10: metaph., hang over, threaten, Simon.39.3; Pi.I.8.14 ; Th.2.53; impending danger, Id.7.75, cf.3.40: c.dat.pers., A.R.3.483; Ep.3pl. impf. Nonn.D.20.173

ἐπίκριμα.definition: = Lat. decretum, OGI453.23 , 669.28 ; Epist. ap. J.AJ19.6.3

ἐπίκρισις.definition: verification, Gal.17.354, cf. 1.117; in Egypt, revision of lists and selection of privileged persons, POxy.288.35 , PFay.27.24 , BGU324.2,19 , etc

ἐπικριτής.definition: adjudicator, arbiter; in Egypt, examining magistrate , PFay.27.3 , PTeb.320.2

ἐπικροτέω.definition: rattle on or over; c. acc., strike with a rattling sound, clash, Alciphr.1.12; Luc.Syr.D.44; Opp.C.2.244

ἐπίκροτος.definition: beaten or trodden hard, esp. of ground, X.Eq.Mag.3.14; Arist.HA558a6: metaph., their sonorousness, Philostr.VS1.25.7

ἐπικρούστιον.definition: a surgical instrument, perh. slasher, Hermes 38.282

ἐπικρύπτω.definition: poet. aor. 2 Q.S.7.235 :—throw a cloak over, conceal, A.Eu.317 ; Pl.Cra.421b; f.l.for E.Supp.296:—freq. in Med., disguise, S.Fr.88.12 ; . . E.Fr.553; Pl.La.196b, cf. Prt.346b; D.17.17: abs., with concealment or secrec…

ἐπίκρυφος.definition: unknown, inglorious, Pi.O.8.69, Max.21; concealed, Plu.Arat.10

ἐπίκρυψις.definition: concealment, Str.2.3.8, Plu.Nic.23; latencies, quiescences, Aret.CD1.5

ἐπικτάομαι.definition: gain or win besides, A.Eu.901; Hdt.2.79; extend one's empire, Th.1.144; Id.4.61; add to those you have, X.HG7.1.3; as an ally, A.Eu.671; S.Ant.846 ; acquire additional property, PGiss.108.3 , etc.:—late in Pass., Agat…

ἐπίκτησις.definition: further acquisition, fresh gain, S.Ph.1344; Arist.HA522a18: pl., D.H.9.53

ἐπίκτητος.definition: gained besides or in addition, acquired land, which was formerly under water, as the Delta of Egypt, Hdt.2.5, cf. 10; property added to one's hereditary property, Pl.Lg.924a, cf. Lycurg.48; a foreign wife , or newly a…

ἐπικτυπέω.definition: aor. 1 : aor. 2 A.R.1.1136:—make a noise upon, stamp on the ground with the feet, Ar.Ec.483; clashed on their shields with . ., A.R. l.c.; Id.2.1081; strike, Nonn.D.38.397: abs., re-echo, respond, Ar.Av.780; of a chor…

ἐπικυδής.definition: only in Comp. , glorious, distinguished, X.HG5.1.36; brilliant, successful, Isoc.4.139; Plb.16.4.3; and of persons, more sanguine, Id.5.69.11, cf. Ph.1.252, al., Onos.23.2. Adv. Comp. Plb.5.23.2

ἐπικυΐσκομαι.definition: become doubly pregnant, i.e. pregnant again before the first foetus is born, Hdt.3.108, Hp.Superf.1, Arist.GA773b28

ἐπικύκλησις.definition: return in a cycle, Alex.Aphr.de An.30.26

ἐπίκυκλος.definition: Astron., epicycle, Plu.2.1028b, Theo Sm.p.162H., Ptol.Alm.3.3, Iamb.VP6.31 , etc

ἐπικυλινδέω.definition: Pass., to be applied by rolling, Gal.11.757; Pass., degenerate, Id.19.560: metaph., Dam.Pr.88

ἐπικυλινδρόομαι.definition: Pass., to be flattened by rollers, Thphr.CP5.6.7

ἐπικυλλόω.definition: mould a cake of dough, prob. for Hsch

ἐπικυματίζω.definition: float upon the waves, Ph.1.455, Ael.Ep.18: metaph., , Ph.1.553; also of persons, Id.2.300; of a runner, Philostr.Her.2.3:— Pass., Phld.Mort.33; opp. Id.Rh.2.55S

ἐπικύπτω.definition: pf. :—bend oneself over, stoop over, bow down, Hp.Art.52, Ar.Th.239; Arist.HA522b18; of the horn of the moon, Thphr.Sign.27; stoop down to get something, X.Cyr.2.3.18; pore over a book, Luc.Herm.2; lean upon, Id.DMort…

ἐπικυρόω.definition: confirm, sanction, ratify, Th.3.71, cf.S.El.793, X.An.3.2.32, D.15.34, SIG167.20, etc.: c.inf., . . E.Or.862:—Pass., Th.5.45; Arist.Ath.37.1, cf. Sammelb. 1161.17

ἐπικύρω.definition: Ep. impf. Ep. aor. 1 and :—light upon, fall in with, c. dat., Il.3.23; Hes.Op.755; kept always touching his neck with . . , Il.23.821; let his sword touch her neck, Q.S.13.394; Pi.P.10.21: c. gen., meet with, obtain, …

ἐπικύρωσις.definition: ratification, confirmation, Arist.Ath.41.3, cf. D.H.9.51, Just.Nov.42.1.1

ἐπικωκύω.definition: lament over, S.El.283; ib.805: abs., Hld.1.13

ἐπικωλύω.definition: hinder, check, X.Oec.8.4; . . S.Ph.1242; IG7.3073.35 ; ib.45: abs., to be a hindrance, Th.6.17:—Pass., PPetr.3p.109 , etc

ἐπικωμάζω.definition: rush on or in with a party of revellers, Plb.26.1.4, Call.Epigr.43: generally, make a riotous assault, Ar.Ach.982; Men.881; go careering about, Pl.Lg.950a; Plu.2.772f: metaph., Chor.in Jahrb.9.177:—Pass., to be visite…

ἐπικώμιος.definition: of, at, or for a or festal procession, Pi.P.10.6, N.8.50; epith. of Apollo, IGRom.4.1539 ; = praises, Pi.N.6.32: sg., revel, Gloss

ἐπικωμῳδέω.definition: make a jest of, caricature, Pl.Ap.31d

ἐπίκωπος.definition: at the oar, rower, Men.Eph. ap; of a boat, furnished with oars, Moschio ap.Ath.5.208f, cf. D.H.3.44, D.S.3.40; phaselus epicopus, dispatch-boat, Cic. Att.14.16.1, cf. 5.11.4

ἐπιλαλέω.definition: interrupt in speaking, Sm.Ps.122.4; charm , LXXJe.8.17

ἐπιλαμβάνω.definition: take or get besides; simply, take, receive, PEleph.10.1 , OGI179.18 , etc

ἐπιλαμπρύνω.definition: make splendid, adorn; of sound, make loud and clear, raise high, Id.Comp.14; of frogs, Plu.2.912c

ἐπίλαμψις.definition: shining, of heavenly bodies, Ph.1.24, al.; Id.2.7 ; illumination, Iamb.Myst.5.26, also cj. for in Hp.Epid.6.1.4

ἐπιλεαίνω.definition: smooth over, Plu.2.74d; chew, Ph.1.63, al.: metaph., ib.180

ἐπιλείπω.definition: leave untouched, Pl.Prt.310e: c.part., Id.Phlb.26b, cf. 52d; of things, fail one, c.acc. pers., . ., Thgn.1131; Hdt.7.21, cf. 2.174; so Id.2.25; Ar.Av.1106; Th.5.103: c.inf., Antipho5.17; time would fail me, Isoc.1.11…

ἐπιλεκτάρχης.definition: commander of a picked band, Plu.Arat.32:— hence SIG421.18

ἐπίλεκτος.definition: chosen, Ph.1.242; esp. of soldiers, X.An.3.4.43, HG5.3.23, IG22.680.12, IPE12.352.39 ; in Egypt, OGI731 , UPZ110.21

ἐπιλεπτύνω.definition: smear over with a thin coat; sift finely, Hsch. s.v

ἐπιλευκαίνω.definition: to be whitish. Arist.PA676a32; of a plant, Thphr.HP3.12.9, etc

ἐπιλήγω.definition: end in or at, J.BJ3.9.3, cf. 3.10.7; prob.l., ib.3.3.4

ἐπίληθος.definition: causing to forget, c.gen., . ., Od.4.221 ; Ael.NA15.19, cf.4.41

ἐπιληπτίζω.definition: have an epileptic fit, Plu.2.290b:—Pass., Alex.Trall.1.15

ἐπίληπτος.definition: Ion. caught or detected in; culpable, censurable, Ph.2.348; Id.2.4, al., cf. Porph.Chr.23; of errors in metre, Heph.4.6

ἐπιλησμονή.definition: forgetfulness, Cratin.410 ap.Sch.Ar.Nu.788, LXXSi.11.27; Ep.Jac.1.25:—also , Hsch., and Alex.315

ἐπιλησμοσύνη.definition: = foreg., Cratin.410 ap.Suid. , IG12.561 , Archig. ap. Gal.8.149, D.C.56.41

ἐπιλήψιμος.definition: reprehensible, Luc.Rh.Pr.22; liable to seizure, Polem.Call.34

ἐπιλιμπάνω.definition: = Gramm., to be wanting, of a tense, An. Ox.4.393, etc

ἐπιλινευτής.definition: one who catches with nets, prob. in AP6.93

ἐπιλιχμάω.definition: lick up, Babr.48.6:—Med., lick up, devour, Ph.1.550: metaph., ib.305, cf. 527

ἐπιλόγευσις.definition: levying of arrears of taxation, PRev.Laws 19.12 . etc

ἐπιλογεύω.definition: levy arrears of taxation, ib.6.1 , PPetr. 3p.69 , etc

ἐπιλογίζομαι.definition: Att. fut. Pl.Ax.365b: aor; address the peroration, Theodect. ap.Rh.7.33 W

ἐπιλογισμός.definition: reckoning, calculation; description, account, Apollod.Poliorc.138.13 , Erasistr. ap. Gal.8.317

ἐπίλογος.definition: reasoning, inference, only Ion; peroration of a speech, Arist.Rh.1414b12, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.96, Phld.Rh.1.202 S., Longin.12.5, etc

ἐπιλοιδορέω.definition: cast reproaches on, cj. in Plb.15.33.4:—Med., Suid. s.v

ἐπιλυπέω.definition: trouble, annoy, offend besides, v.l. in Hdt.9.50, LXX2 Ma.8.32:—Pass., to be troubled at, . . S.E.M.11.127

ἐπίλυπος.definition: sad, Ph.2.29; in low; painful, Arist.EN1117a34; a thing that causes pain, ib.1110b19; Plu.2.13a. Adv. D.S.17.118

ἐπίλυσις.definition: solution, S.E.P.2.246; explanation, 2 Ep.Pet.1.20, Vett. Val.172.3 , Hld.1.18, 4.9, Iamb.Protr.21

ἐπιλύω.definition: loose, untie, Theoc.Adon.42; let; solve, explain, Ev.Marc.4.34:—Pass.,S.E.P.2.246, Sch.Od.9.106:—Med., J.AJ8.6.5, Vett.Val.259.4, Ath.10.45of, al.: pf. part. Pass. lucid, of writings, Vett.Val.329.25

ἐπιμαίνω.definition: make madly in love with, Anon. ap; Pass., with aor. 2. but also aor.1 Med. Il.6.160, AP6.309 , Luc.Syr.D.21: pf. be mad after, c.dat., Il. l.c., cf. Anacr.3, Mosch.Fr.2.2,Plu.Brut.5; Call.Cer.30; Ar.V.744 , cf. 1469 ,…

ἐπιμανθάνω.definition: learn besides or after, opp. Th.1.138: c.inf., Hdt.1.131; . . Id.2.160

ἐπιμαντεύομαι.definition: prophesy, c. acc. et inf., App.BC4.127; ib.138, Philostr.VA5.19

ἐπιμαρτύρησις.definition: confirmation, corroboration; Astrol., supporting by aspect, Paul.Al.O.4, Ptol.Tetr.200

ἐπιμαρτυρητής.definition: one who calls to witness, Gloss

ἐπιμαρτυρία.definition: a calling to witness; supporting by aspect, Man.2.400 , cf. 3.314 , al

ἐπιμαρτύρομαι.definition: call to witness, appeal to, in case; call on earnestly, conjure, Th.6.29

ἐπιμασάομαι.definition: chew, Alciphr.3.51; chew after other food, Gp.12.30.9:—Pass., Dsc.3.45

ἐπιμάχομαι.definition: fight after, act as a reserve, Ael.Tact.17, Arr.Tact.15.5

ἐπιμείγνυμι.definition: and add by mixing; intr., mingle with others, have intercourse or dealings, Th.1.2; X.An.3.5.16; Hld.6.13; come to it, Id.5.33; Philostr.VA5.24:—Pass., Hp.Morb.1.11; X.Cyr.7.4.5; Th.2.1: abs., Id.1.146; also join them…

ἐπιμειλίσσομαι.definition: placate, J.BJ1.20.3:—Act., aor. 1 inf. prob. for Hsch

ἐπιμείρομαι.definition: to be assigned by fate, Vett.Val.346.6

ἐπιμελαίνομαι.definition: to become black on the surface, a; of fruit, blacken in ripening, Thphr.HP3.15.6

ἐπιμέλεια.definition: written IG22.483.24; a commission or charge, Aeschin.3.13, Arist.Pol.1299a20 ; ib.1322b18, cf. ib.30 ; a special office at Athens, Din.3.15; so = POxy.281.2

ἐπιμελέομαι.definition: also Hdt.1.98, 2.2,174,al; of public commissions, have charge of, be inspector or curator of, Lys.7.29; X.Cyr.8.1.14; Id.An.4.8.25; CIG4011 : c.acc. cogn., Pl.Lg.812e:—in Att. Inscrr., is usual of a definite commissio…

ἐπιμελής.definition: careful or anxious about; abs., careful, attentive, Ar.Nu.501, X.Mem.2.6.38, etc.: Comp. S.Fr.472, cf. X.An.3.2.30: Sup., Isoc.4.142; Men.223.9. Adv. carefully, X.Mem.2.4.2, Pl.Ti.88c, Men.Pk.32, etc.; Ion. Hp.Art.55;…

ἐπιμελητεία.definition: office of IG22.1338.30 ; term of such office, SIG825 A5

ἐπιμελητεύω.definition: to be an PTeb.61.71 , IG3.393, SIG829 A 7 , 855.6 , etc

ἐπιμελῳδέω.definition: sing over or at a person, Aristid.Or.29.30

ἐπίμεμπτος.definition: = sq., of persons or actions; blaming, Sch.S.Tr.446. Adv. Arg.Aeschin.3

ἐπιμερισμός.definition: distribution, Hsch.s.v; Astrol., assignment, Vett. Val. 97.9, Critodem.inCat.Cod.Astr.8.102.4

ἐπιμετρέω.definition: add to the measure, give over and above, Plu.Lys.4, cf. Alex.42; Luc.DMort.5.1; prolong one's magistracy, Plu.Comp.Ages.Pomp.3, etc.; add, in speaking, Plb.28.17.2, etc.: c. gen. partit., add some jests, Luc.Nav.19; a…

ἐπίμετρον.definition: something added to make good measure excess, Theoc.12.26, PTeb.91.11 ; make an increase, Thphr.CP4.13.7, Plu.2.676b; ib.503d; into the bargain, Plb.6.46.6; S.E.P.2.47, cf. Gal.8.493

ἐπιμηθεύομαι.definition: think of afterwards or too late, Eust.67.27:— also Corn.ND18

ἐπιμηνιεύω.definition: hold the office of ib.241.90 , 495.180 , BCH17.555 , Test.Epict. 4.15,35, etc.; hold monthly chairmanship, SIG708.2

ἐπιμήνιος.definition: monthly, HondiusNovae; priests who offered the Hsch.; . . SIG1106.63 , cf. 1044.24 , Test.Epict.2.33

ἐπιμηρύομαι.definition: wind a layer of gut on top of others, Ph.Bel.65.43

ἐπιμηχανάομαι.definition: devise plans against, take; devise besides, X.Cyr.8.8.16; D.Chr.6.11, cf. App.BC4.120

ἐπιμηχάνημα.definition: Dor. a means towards a thing, Hippod. ap. Stob.4.1.94

ἐπιμηχάνησις.definition: device, contrivance, on purpose, artificially, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.153

ἐπιμίσθιος.definition: engaged for hire, Dam. ap. Suid. s.v. cf. Hsch.s.v. :—pecul. fem. AP7.403

ἐπιμισθόω.definition: contract for, in Pass. of bricks, Michel1512 , cf. IG12.189.30 , 11.165.36, 199A106 , PPetr.3p.109 ; v.l. in Ael.VH3.14

ἐπιμοιράομαι.definition: receive by lot, receive as one's share, c. acc., get earth enough for a grave, Moschio Trag.6.31, cf. Ps.-Phoc.99 : c. gen., have a share of, Ph.2.178

ἐπίμοιρος.definition: partaking in, c. gen., B.1.48, cf. Euryph. ap. Stob.4.39.27

ἐπίμομφος.definition: inclined to blame, E.Rh.327; blameable, unlucky, A.Ag.553; dub.l., Id.Ch.830

ἐπιμονή.definition: tarrying, delay, Th.2.18; residence; steadfastness, Pl.Cra.395b, Plu.Sert.16; persistence, Sor.2.16,40; of fruit, Thphr.CP2.9.8

ἐπίμονος.definition: staying on, lasting long, Plb.6.43.2; continue him in his command, ib.15.6; delay their payment, Id.38.11.10; Hermes 17.5 ; Sor.1.43; or persevering in it, Plb.29.26.2, Plu.Flam.1; Stoic.3.32. Adv. constantly, permane…

ἐπιμόριος.definition: containing a whole + a fraction with 1 for its numerator , superparticular, Arist.Pr.921b5; Ph.2.183 , Plu.in Hes.59; of the rhythm of the pulse, Gal.8.516; also Arist.Metaph.1021a2. Adv. Nicom.Ar.2.20; opp. , ib.1.20…

ἐπιμορφάζω.definition: pretend, c. inf., Ph.1.387; c.acc., simulate, ib.340,698:—Med., Hsch

ἐπίμοχθος.definition: toilsome, B.1.71, cf. Man.4.248: gloss on Sch.Ar.Pax383; Hp.Ep.17. Adv. with toil, App.Pun.72; so neut., LXXWi.15.7

ἐπιμυθεύομαι.definition: to be added fabulously, Arist.HA605a5, Ant.Diog.5

ἐπιμυκτηρίζω.definition: turn up the nose, mock at, Men.562.4

ἐπιμύλιος.definition: at or in the mill, epith. of Artemis; of a millstone, LXXJd.9.53

ἐπιμύρομαι.definition: to be washed by the sea, A.R.1.938; but dribbles, An.Ox. 3.220

ἐπιμύσσω.definition: laugh at, cj. in Luc.DMort.6.3: aor. 1 Hsch

ἐπιμωκάομαι.definition: mock at, Sch.S.OT970, Sch.A.R.1.486:—also v.l. in Luc.JTr.16

ἐπίμωμος.definition: blameworthy, Hld.7.2; blemished, Artem.5.67: opp. Herm. ap. Stob.1.41.1

ἐπινάσσω.definition: fut. stuff up, close up, Hsch.; cf; pour, heap over, Gp.6.6.2

ἐπιναυπηγέω.definition: build upon the ship, Poll.1.92; build in addition, Anon.Argent.p.75 Keil

ἐπινεανιεύομαι.definition: behave like a youth, in good sense; commit further outrages, Lib.Decl.13.9,56

ἐπινέμησις.definition: appropriate apportioning of; spreading, Plu.Lys.12, Epicur.Ep.2p.40U.; of disease, Antyll. ap. Orib.50.8.3

ἐπινέφελος.definition: clouded, overcast, Hp.Epid.3.2; bringing clouds, Arist.Pr.947b5

ἐπίνικος.definition: = foreg., Pi.O.8.75, cf. Stratt.40 : Subst. , Aristid.Or.28.34, 61

ἐπινίσσομαι.definition: go over, c. gen., S.OC689; c. acc., come upon, visit, A.R.4.817, Nic.Th.470, Pae.Delph.6: abs., Theoc.8.43, A.R.4.281

ἐπινοέω.definition: think on or of, contrive, Hdt.1.48; have in one's mind, intend, purpose, Th.2.8, cf. X.An.2.5.4, etc.: c. pres. inf., Hdt.1.27, Ar.Th.338, X.An.6.4.9, etc.: fut., Hdt.3.134: aor., Id.2.152, 5.24,65, E.Rh.195 , Pl.Ti.3…

ἐπινομή.definition: a grazing over the; right of pasturage, Schwyzer 197.33

ἐπινομία.definition: a grazing over the boundaries: right of pasture, X.Cyr.3.2.23 , Berl.Sitzb.1927.7 , IG9.61.7 , 5.511 ; SIG534.15

ἐπινοσέω.definition: to be ill after, Hp.Epid.1.16, cf. Phryn.PSp.120B

ἐπινοσσοποιέομαι.definition: Med., build their nests upon, Ps.-Democr.Symp. Ant.p.6G

ἐπινυκτερεύω.definition: pass the night at or in, Heraclit.All.9; of water, stand for a night, Plu.2.690c

ἐπινύμφειος.definition: bridal, prob. in S.Ant.814 : fem. Supp.Epigr.2.874

ἐπινυμφεύομαι.definition: contract a second marriage, of a woman, GDI3721.5

ἐπινύσσω.definition: prick on the surface, Antyll. ap. Orib.10.19.5; stabbing pains, Arching. ap. Gal.8.110:—Pass., Sor.Fract.24, f.l. in Luc.Lex.11

ἐπινυστάζω.definition: drop asleep over, Plu.Brut.36: abs., Luc.Bis Acc.2, Agath.4.18

ἐπινωτίζω.definition: attack from behind, E.HF362 ; = Archipp.5:—Med., take on one's back, Paus.Gr.Fr.143

ἐπινώτιος.definition: on the back, Batr.80, Luc.Am.26; shoulder-blades, Poll.2.133

ἐπίξανθος.definition: inclining to yellow, tawny, of hares, X.Cyn.5.22; of deer, Poll.5.76; of the open lime- flower, Thphr.HP3.10.4, cf.4.2.7

ἐπιξεναγός.definition: officer attached to an Ascl.Tact.6.3, Ael.Tact.16.4, Arr.Tact.14.6

ἐπιξενόομαι.definition: have hospitable relations with, be intimate with, D.50.56, cf. D.S.1.23; lent to or communicated with, Heraclit. ap. S.E.M.7.130

ἐπιξηραίνω.definition: dry on the surface, Hp.Fract.33, Arist.Pr.928a9:— Pass., to be so dried, Hp.Prorrh.2.6; have an interval of dryness, Id.Acut.28: generally, to be dried up, Ruf.Ren.Ves.6.5; to be constipated, Aret.CA1.1

ἐπιορκία.definition: false swearing, perjury, X.An.3.2.4, etc.; D.19.220: pl., Pl.Grg.525a; X.An.2.5.21

ἐπίορκος.definition: sworn falsely, of oaths; of persons, forsworn, perjured, Hes.Op.804, Schwyzer179a , E.El.1355 , Ar.Nu.399,al.: Antipho6.48. Adv. Hdn.6.9.2

ἐπιόψομαι.definition: fut. , I will choose, Il.9.167, Od.2.294: aor. I ind. chose, IG2.948.1 , cf. Pl.Lg.947c , Hsch., Suid.: aor. 1 Pass., IG2.949.2

ἐπιπαιανίζω.definition: sing a paean over, D.S.5.29: c.acc.cogn., Plu.Marc.22

ἐπιπαίζω.definition: mock at, Hld.10.13: abs., Alex.172.16; sport upon, Philostr.Im.2.17

ἐπιπαραγίγνομαι.definition: arrive on the scene, Satyr.Vit.Eur.Fr.39xxi 25, Mitteis Chr.8.3 , etc.; of generals, succeed in a command, Plb.1.31.4; of troops, come up, Id.4.12.7; of events, come also upon, Junc. ap. Stob.4.50.27

ἐπιπαράκειμαι.definition: to be adjacent, Steph.in Hp.1.209 D

ἐπιπαρανέω.definition: heap up still more besides, Th.2.77

ἐπιπαρεμβάλλω.definition: re-form, Plb.12.19.6; intr., fall into line with others, Id.3.115.10, 11.23.5

ἐπιπαρέξειμι.definition: pass farther along, of the sun , Arist.Pr.912a11

ἐπιπαρέρχομαι.definition: go past on the way to a place; Astrol., intervene as well, Vett. Val.291.9

ἐπιπαροινέω.definition: in Pass., to be further intoxicated , prob. in Phld.Ir.p.33 W

ἐπιπαροξύνω.definition: incite still more, D.C.44.35, Ach.Tat.1.8:—Pass., of persons in fever, suffer from successive accesses, v.l. in Hp.Epid.1.2, cf. Gal.7.306; of a sore, become more inflamed, Hp.Prorrh.1.162

ἐπίπασμα.definition: powder for sprinkling, Aret.CA2.2; Sch.Theoc.15.114, cf. Alex.Trall.Febr.3

ἐπιπάσσω.definition: Att. Dor. inf. IG4.951.119 , cf. upon or over, Il.4.218, cf. 5.401, IGl.c., Euphro11.10; Hdt.4.172; Orph.L.455, Luc.DMar.15.3: c. partit. gen., Id.Pisc.22: abs., Theoc.2.18:—Pass., Pl.R.405e, cf. PTeb.1.19

ἐπίπαστος.definition: a kind of cake with comfits upon it, Ar.Eq.103, 1089, Pherecr.130.3; but , = Hp.Hum.5, Theoc.11.2, Aret.CA2.2

ἐπίπεδος.definition: on the ground, on the ground-floor; level, flat, Pl.Criti.112a; X.HG7.1.29, etc.; not on a level, but . . , ib.6.4.14; PThead.20i3 ; = Lat. de plano, J.AJ19.5.3: irreg. Comp. X.HG7.4.13

ἐπιπειράομαι.definition: do violence to a woman, c. acc., Leg.Gort.2.17, cf. Hsch

ἐπιπέμπω.definition: pf. POxy.743.30 :—send after; send to, IG12.94; of the gods, send upon or to, Hdt.7.15; Pi.Fr.75.2 ; Pl.Phdr.245b ; esp. by way of punishment, send upon or against, let loose upon, generally of the gods, . . E.Ph.811 …

ἐπιπεριελίσσω.definition: wrap round a second time, Hp.Art.38

ἐπίπερκνος.definition: somewhat dark, of grapes ripening: hence, of the colour of certain hares, X.Cyn.5.22, Poll.5.67

ἐπιπέσσω.definition: Att. bake, SIG57.36; Pass., to be concocted, Gal.UP14.11

ἐπιπετάννυμι.definition: spread over, X.Cyn.5.10, cf.Aret.CA1.10:—Pass., Q.S.14.25; Aret.SD2.9

ἐπιστρατοπεδεία.definition: encamping over against, Plb.1.77.7; the fact that the enemy was encamped near, Id.5.76.9

ἐπιστρατοπεδεύω.definition: encamp over against, Id.1.19.5; Id.5.30.4, etc

ἐπίστρεμμα.definition: turn or return of a boundary line, IG14.352i28

ἐπίστρεπτος.definition: or to be turned; that can be turned round, reversible, HeroAut.15.3, Spir.1.28

ἐπιστρεφής.definition: turning one's eyes or mind to a thing; exact, strict, severe, D.H.10.33 ; Hdn.7.8.7; Id.5.2.5. Adv. Ion. earnestly, vehemently, Hdt.1.30; Aeschin.1.71; D.H.7.34: Comp. UPZ 24.24 , Phleg.Olymp.Fr.1, etc.; cf. is v.l. f…

ἐπιστροφίς.definition: dislocation, Hsch; in pl., curls, Eust.1561.38

ἐπιστρώφησις.definition: going to and fro, Onat. ap. Stob.1.1.39

ἐπιστύλιον.definition: architrave, IG12.372; shelf with pigeon-holes, Arist.Ath.47.5

ἐπισυγκροτέω.definition: weld together, combine in one body, J.BJ1.1.6

ἐπισυγκρούω.definition: meet with a check or reverse, D.C.Fr.50.2

ἐπισυγχέω.definition: in Pass., to be in confusion, .. Ph.1.320 codd

ἐπισυκοφαντέω.definition: harass yet more with frivolous accusations, Hyp.Fr.243, Plu.Ant.21

ἐπισυλλέγω.definition: collect besides or after, Hp.Off.11 ; J.BJ1.6.3:—Pass., v.l. in Dsc.4.153, cf. Gal.18.781

ἐπισυλλογίζομαι.definition: draw a subsequent inference, A.D.Conj.252.5 : c. acc. et inf., Iamb.VP3.16

ἐπισυμπάρειμι.definition: Astrol., of planets, to be present as well, Nech. ap. Vett.Val.280.5

ἐπισυμπίπτω.definition: collapse, decay, Ph.2.221; happen besides or in addition to, J.AJ15.10.3; casual distortions, Ptol.Tetr.108

ἐπισυμπλέκω.definition: add a drug to a mixture, Paul.Aeg.4.4:—Pass., to be combined, A.D.Synt.124.27

ἐπισύμπτωσις.definition: falling together, Anon.Lond.27.29; incidence, Andronic.Rhod.p.570 M

ἐπισυναλοιφή.definition: elision at the close of a verse; coalescence of two syllables in one, Isid.Etym.1.35.5

ἐπισυνάρχομαι.definition: begin together with, Hippodam. ap. Stob.4.39.26

ἐπισυνδίδωμι.definition: rush in together, of streams, Plu.Aem.14

ἐπισυνέμπτωσις.definition: succession of words with like terminations and containing the same vowels , Eust.1291.43

ἐπισυνεργέω.definition: contribute, Euryph. ap; restrict still further, Sor.1.56

ἐπισύνθεσις.definition: addition, Vett.Val.280.13, Herm.in Phdr.p.107 A.; combination, S.E.M.1.22; Longin.40.1; complexity, Marcellin.Puls.464

ἐπισύνθετος.definition: compound: hence , metre composed of of different Heph.15.10

ἐπισυνθήκη.definition: additional article to a treaty, Schwyzer631.4 , ii B. C.) : pl., Plb.3.27.7

ἐπισυνίστημι.definition: band together, J.l.c.; Id.BJ2.3.4; simply, incite to conspiracy against, Str.13.4.2

ἐπισυνοικίζω.definition: bring in new colonists, Str.5.1.6:—Pass., of a place,to be colonized anew, Paus.6.22.5

ἐπισυντάσσω.definition: contrive against; bring in as well, PMasp.6ii136

ἐπισυντείνω.definition: intensify effort, Poll.3.121:—Pass., have a feeling of tightness, Hp.Acut.44

ἐπισυντίθημι.definition: add successively, Archim.Sph.Cyl.1.2; close the edges of a wound, Orib.46.25.6

ἐπισυντρέχω.definition: run together to a place, Ev.Marc.9.25

ἐπισυρρέω.definition: flow together, Str.5.3.13, Dsc.4.153; of a crowd, Ph.2.365 : c. dat., D.H.4.55,Placit.3.7.3

ἐπισύστασις.definition: gathering, riotous meeting; collection, S.E.M.11.127; Sor.1.58

ἐπισυστέλλομαι.definition: Pass., to be drawn together, contracted, of a wasp's waist, Sch.Ar.Pl.301: metaph., of style, to be lowered in tone, Arist.Rh.1404b17

ἐπισυστρέφω.definition: collect together, LXXNu.16.42; compress into unity, Longin.24.1

ἐπισφάλλω.definition: trip up, make to fall, J.BJ3.7.29, Onos.42.6

ἐπισφηκόω.definition: bind on or to, Nonn.D.9.123:—Med., ib.2.111

ἐπισφίγγω.definition: bind tight, tighten, Ph.1.698; Gal.18.398; Luc.Am.41; in the arms, AP5.242 ; tie the shoe- strings tight, Ath.12.543f; Gp.10.12.3: metaph.,shut up tightly, Ph.1.108; complicate it, opp. S.E.M.2.96; also screw it tight…

ἐπισφοδρύνω.definition: make rigid, intensify, Plu.Cleom.10; corroborate, confirm, Phld.Sign.28

ἐπισφραγίζω.definition: confirm, ratify, APl.5.366, cf.Vett.Val.354.19:— Med., get it sanctioned, Plb.32.6.3; give one's sanction to, Hierocl.in CA10p.437M

ἐπισφράγισις.definition: = sq., Greg.Cor.in Hermog.in; cadence of a verse, Sch.Heph.p.118C

ἐπισφραγιστής.definition: one who seals or signs, Luc.Alex.23

ἐπισχεδιάζω.definition: say or do off-hand, make a suitable impromptu, Philostr.VS1.2:— Pass., Id.Gym.54

ἐπίσχεσις.definition: checking, stoppage; delay, reluctance, Od.17.451; delay or lingering there, Th.2.18, cf. PCair.Zen.283.5

ἐπισχίζω.definition: cleave at top, A.R.2.662; Str.16.2.41; split the end of a bandage, Sor.Fasc.12.514C., cf. 510C.:— Pass., Dsc.3.147

ἐπισχύω.definition: make strong or powerful; intr., to be or grow strong, Thphr.CP2.1.4; prevail, D.S.5.59, Corn.ND7; to be urgent, Ev.Luc.23.5; Vett.Val.48.6

ἐπισωματόομαι.definition: Pass., to be condensed into a mass, Dsc.5.74

ἐπισωρεύω.definition: heap upon, Ath.3.123e; heap up, accumulate, 2 Ep.Ti.4.3; Arr.Epict.1.10.5; Plu.2.830a:—Pass., Id.in Hes.34, Vett.Val.344.12

ἐπιταγή.definition: = Plb.13.4.3, LXX1; esp. of oracles or divine commands, SIG1153 ; JHS26.28, etc.; Ep.Rom.16.26, cf. 1 Ep.Cor.7.6

ἐπιτάκτης.definition: commander, Gp.17.2.4 : used to transl. Lat. Imperiosus, the surname of Manlius Torquatus, Plu.2.308e

ἐπιταλαιπωρέω.definition: suffer or labour at, Th.1.123; labour yet further, D.H.9.35

ἐπιταράσσω.definition: Att. trouble or disquiet yet more, Hdt.2.139; Hp.Epid.1.15; Plu.2.788e; Luc.DMort.2.1:—Pass., to be disarranged, Sor.1.38

ἐπιταφέω.definition: to be present at a funeral, SIG1109.161

ἐπιτάφιος.definition: over or at a tomb; = IG22.1006.22, 12.946.16

ἐπιταχύνω.definition: hasten on, urge forward, Th.4.47; Plu.Per.29, Hdn.2.11.1; making it rapid, Plu.2.1011e; D.H.Comp.20; Paus.8.51.4:—Pass., Plu.Ant.68

ἐπιτέγγω.definition: pour liquid upon, moisten, Hp.Fract.29, cf. Gal.UP14.11, al.; Philostr.VS2.5.3; Gal.6.122; = Anacreont.53.41

ἐπιτείνω.definition: Ion. iterat. Hdt.1.186 : pf; stretch as on a frame, tighten, screw up, esp. of musical strings, Pl.Ly.209b; Macho2.9:— Pass., Arist.Pr.920b3, cf. GA787b13, Pl.Phd.98c

ἐπιτειχίζω.definition: build a fort or stronghold on the frontier of the enemy's country to serve as the basis of operations against him, abs., Th.1.142,7.47; And.1.101, cf. Lys.14.30, Plu.Alc.23; add.codd.] .. X.HG7.2.1, cf.5.1.2; and in P…

ἐπιτείχισις.definition: building a fort on the enemy's frontier, Th.1.142; Id.6.93

ἐπιτείχισμα.definition: fort or stronghold placed on; metaph., a barrier or obstacle to.., Id.15.12; J.BJ1.23.1; a barrier against, or a bulwark in defence of, the laws, Alcid. ap. Arist.Rh.1406b11; S.E.M.1.298

ἐπιτειχισμός.definition: = Th.7.18, X.HG5.1.2; against it, Th.1.122 : metaph., D.18.87

ἐπιτεκμαίρομαι.definition: detect a star by means of, Arat.229; so Id.457; predict, c. gen., Id.1038, cf. 1129 ; infer, conjecture, .. Id.142

ἐπιτέλεια.definition: oversight, command, prob. f.l. for; fulfilment, Aristeas18; Id.272

ἐπιτέλειος.definition: bringing to fulfilment, epith. of Aphrodite, BCH49.79 ; of Zeus, SIG961 note 2

ἐπιτελειόω.definition: complete, esp. a sacrifice, Lycurg.Fr.36 ; Plu.Mar.22; cf

ἐπιτελείωσις.definition: after-offering, esp. in; accomplishment, completion, Plu.Num.14, cf. 2.961c; of the Censorship at Rome, Id.Cat. Ma.16, Flam.18

ἐπιτελέω.definition: bring to perfection, Arist.GA741b5, cf. HA539a33:—Pass., Id.GA758b26

ἐπιτέρμιος.definition: at the limits, Hsch.; esp. as epith. of Hermes, Id

ἐπιτερπής.definition: pleasing, delightful, h.Ap.413; devoted to pleasure , Id.Alc.23

ἐπιτετραέβδομος.definition: containing one plus four- sevenths, v.l. for Nicom.Ar.1.23

ἐπιτετραμερής.definition: containing one plus four-fifths, ib.20, al

ἐπιτεχνάζω.definition: scheme against, App.BC3.39; Med., = sq., Opp.H.3.194

ἐπιτεχνάομαι.definition: contrive for a purpose or to meet an; contrive against, Id.6.20, cf. Luc.Bis Acc.1

ἐπιτέχνημα.definition: contrivance, Ael.NA12.16 : pl., devices, Ptol.Alm.13.2, Jul.Or.2.91c

ἐπιτέχνησις.definition: contrivance for a purpose, invention, Th.1.71, Arist.Mu.398b10, Ph.1.296; Paus.1.6.6; artifice, in speaking, D.H.Is.3; artificial preparation, Ath.3.124e, cf. Antyll. ap. Orib.10.2.2; Ath.13.568a

ἐπιτηδειόομαι.definition: to be made fit or capable, Iamb.VP32.228

ἐπιτηδειότης.definition: fitness, suitableness; all material, etc., for carrying on war, Plb.2.23.11

ἐπιτήδευσις.definition: devotion or attention to a pursuit or business, Th.2.36, Pl.Ax.369b, etc.; cultivation of a habit or character, Th.7.86; Pl.Lg.853b; scrupulous refinements, E.Hipp.261 ; of a studied style, D.H.Lys.8; of baths, opp. A…

ἐπιτηδευτής.definition: one who practises, J.AJ19.1.5, cf. Ptol.Tetr.163

ἐπιτηδεύω.definition: impf. Pl.Phd.64a : aor; c. inf.. take care to do, use to do, Hdt.3.18, 4.170, Pl.Grg.524c, Jul.Or.1.3d, etc.; also .. Hdt.3.102

ἐπιτηρέω.definition: look out or watch for, h.Cer.244; keep an eye on, App.BC4.39:—Pass., to be kept under surveillance, POxy.1413.10

ἐπιτηρητής.definition: watcher, scout, Sch. rec.A.Th.36; superintendent of taxes, Ostr.144 , cf. 1020, al.; BGU 478.4 , Arch.Pap.4.143 ; POxy.2116.1

ἐπιτίκτω.definition: bring forth after, Hp.Superf.1; Sor. ap.Orib.22.7.2, cf. Plu.Phil.1
