ἐπιτιμέω.definition: Hdt.6.39, Schwyzer 346.11 :—lay a; show honour to, Hdt.l.c

ἐπιτίμημα.definition: legal penalty, IG12.75; censure, criticism, Arist.Po.1461b22 , Plu.2.1110e

ἐπιτιμία.definition: the condition of an enjoyment; punishment, penalty, LXXWi.3.10, OGI 669.43

ἐπιτιτράω.definition: aor. I inf. pierce, cut holes in stones, IG11.161 A55 ; trepan, Heliod. ap. Orib.46.15.3

ἐπιτομή.definition: cutting on the surface; epitome, abridgement, Arist.Pr.891a7; Epicur.Ep.1p.4 U.; title of works by Chrysippus, etc., Stoic.2.5, etc.; D.H.1.5, cf. LXX2 Ma.2.28; briefly, Cic.Att.5.20.1; of Rome, Ath.1.20b

ἐπίτομος.definition: cut off, timber cut in short; short, compendious, D.H.1.68, Ph.2.25; Paus.10.31.7; D.Chr.18.4; Hld.10.4

ἐπιτόνιον.definition: peg or key by which the strings of an; pitch-pipe for giving the note to a choir, Et.Gud.d. s.v

ἐπιτοξίς.definition: dub. sens. in IG22.1357; = sq., Vitr.10.10.4 codd

ἐπιτοξῖτις.definition: groove or slot for the arrow in a catapult, Ph.Bel.73.51, 75.2, HeroBel.77.10, cj. in Vitr.10.10.4

ἐπιτραγηματίζω.definition: serve up as dessert, Arist. ap. Jul.Ep.180

ἐπιτραγία.definition: epith. of Aphrodite, from a she-goat, which was changed into a he-goat , Plu.Thes.18, IG3.335

ἐπιτραγῳδέω.definition: make a tragic story of a thing, exaggerate, Thphr.HP9.8.5, D.H.Th.28, Plu.Art.18 , Luc.Tox.12; Ph.2.105; descant solemnly upon, Plu.Per.28, Demetr.Eloc.122; lament tragically, Hld.1.3; add to a tragedy, Id.7.6, cf. 2.29

ἐπιτραπέζιος.definition: on or at table, Luc.Herm.68; = foreg., Hsch. s.v

ἐπιτραπέζωμα.definition: a dish set on table, Pl.Com.74, cf. Ath.4.170e

ἐπιτρέφω.definition: fut. Hdt.8.142 : pf. AP7.536; rear upon, APl.c

ἐπιτρίβω.definition: metaph., afflict, destroy, Hdt.4.184; Ar.Nu.438, cf. 243; Id.Lys.888; X.Mem.1.3.12; D.18.104; opp. Men.Epit.550; of an actor, murder a part, D.18.180; Plu.2.531b:—Pass., to be utterly destroyed or undone, Sol.33.7, Ar…

ἐπιτριηραρχέω.definition: to be trierarch beyond the legal time, D.50.24,54: ib.36:—Pass., two months beyond my term of office having elapsed, and my successor not having relieved me, ib.20

ἐπιτριηράρχημα.definition: burden of a trierarchy continued beyond the legal term, ib.50.1, 54

ἐπιτριήραρχος.definition: trierarch subject to this burden, IG22.1612.136

ἐπιτρομέω.definition: to be in fear of, Q.S.2.474

ἐπιτροπαῖος.definition: entrusted to one, delegated, Hdt.3.142; Id.4.147

ἐπιτροπεία.definition: charge, guardianship, over one; office of a Roman procurator, PFay.20.17 ; Them.Or.8.117a

ἐπιτροπεύω.definition: to be an administrator, guardian, etc; abs., Hdt.1.134, X.Oec.12.8, 13.1, IG3.392, etc.; for one, Pl.Lg.849b

ἐπιτροπή.definition: reference, esp. to an arbiter in decision; generally, power to decide, Hp.Decent.17, cf. Schwyzer 195.10 , ii B.C.); Plb.18.39.5; or Lat. dedere se in fidem, to surrender absolutely, Id.2.11.8,15.8.14, etc.; to receiv…

ἐπίτροπος.definition: one to whom the charge of; = Lat. procurator, Str.3.4.20, Plu.2.813e, etc.; OG1502.10 , 501.2 ; Arr.Epict.3.4.1; OG1678.5 , etc

ἐπιτρόχαλος.definition: quickly passing, 'tripping', D.H.Comp.18: metaph., glib, flowing, Id.Dem.40

ἐπιτροχασμός.definition: rapid succession of statements, as a figure of speech, Phld.Herc.862.14 , Alex.Fig.1.17, Phoeb.Fig.2.1

ἐπίτροχος.definition: running easily, easily inclined, Hp.Art.14; walks which break into a run, Aret.CD1.3; not very mobile, Id.SD1.7: metaph., tripping, Hld.4.17; Aristid.Quint.2.15; voluble, glib, Luc.DDeor.7.3; Id.Nec.7. Adv. Ael.NA7.7

ἐπιτρύζω.definition: squeak beside or over, Euph.134; mutter, Call.Aet.Oxy.2079 Fr.1.1, cf. Hsch.; Babr.112.8: abs., chirps, AP6.54

ἐπιτρυφάω.definition: luxuriate, revel in, v.l. for in Ph.2.392

ἐπιτρώγω.definition: eat with or after, Luc.Sat.21,28: c. gen; generally, eat, POxy.1185.11

ἐπιτυλίσσω.definition: turn over or open a book, D.L.9.114

ἐπιτυμβίδιος.definition: at or over a tomb; frequenting tombs, or with tomb-like crests, or with tombs in their heads , Theoc.7.23, cf. Sch.ad loc

ἐπιτύφομαι.definition: Pass., aor. 2 Ar.Lys.221:—to be burnt up, esp. by lightning, Philostr.VS1.21.2, cf. Im.2.29: metaph., to be inflamed by love, for one, Ar.l.c.; furious, Pl.Phdr.230a

ἐπιτυχία.definition: success, opp. Democr.275; Plb.1.6.4; D.H.3.70; OG1678.2 : pl., Phld.Po.2.33; advantage, Ph.2.326

ἐπιτωθάζω.definition: mock, jest, Pl.Ax.364c, Hp.Ep.17; mock at, jeer, App.BC2.67, 5.125, cf. Hieronym.Hist.7; Men. Rh.p.420S

ἐπιφαιδρύνω.definition: make bright or clean, A.R.4.663:—Pass., Hld.8.9

ἐπιφάνεια.definition: appearance, coming into light or; esp. of deities appearing to a worshipper, manifestation, D.H.2.68, Plu.Them.30; advent, D.S.2.47; SIG867.35 ; a manifestation of divine power, Klio16.204 , cf.LXX2 Ma.15.27, D.S.1.25

ἐπιφαυλίζω.definition: make of small account, v.l. for in LXXLa.1.22, 2.20

ἐπίφημι.definition: agree, assent, Emp.9.5: Aeol. aor. inf. Act. = Hsch

ἐπιφθάνω.definition: reach first, aor. 2 part. Batr.213: generally, reach, attain, Suid. s.v. PLond.5.1676.43 ; arrive, D.C.65.18:— Med., see before others, Anon. ap. Suid

ἐπιφθέγγομαι.definition: utter after or in accordance, A.Ch.457; attach a name to, predicate a quality of, Pl.Phlb.18d, cf. Plu.2.1110e

ἐπίφθεγξις.definition: charm, invocation, Philagr. ap. Aët.12.51; cry addressed to dogs, Sch.Ar.V.702

ἐπίφθονος.definition: liable to envy or jealousy, looked on; Act., bearing a grudge against, A.Ag.133 : abs., malignant, hostile, Id.Eu.376 , Sammelb.3924.35 ; .. App.Pun.59; Hld.4.5

ἐπιφιλοπονέομαι.definition: Dep., labour willingly and earnestly at, X.Oec.5.5

ἐπιφλεγμαίνω.definition: suffer from supervening inflammation, Hp.Fract.38, Aret.SA1.9, etc

ἐπιφλυκταινόομαι.definition: Pass., have pustules on the top, Hp.Epid.4.20

ἐπιφοινίσσω.definition: make red on the surface, Luc.Am.41; intr., incline to be red, be reddish, Arist.Phgn.812a33; Thphr.Sign.10:—Pass., Arist.Phgn.812a32; ib.37

ἐπιφοιτάω.definition: Ion. come habitually or in; c. dat. pers., visits them rarely, of the Phoenix, Hdt.2.73, cf. Ph.1.265, Palaeph.37, Luc.Am.9, etc

ἐπίφορος.definition: carrying towards; leaning or prone to a thing, gloss in Hp.Art.14 ; Plu.2.703d; well-suited, Longin.5, Plu.2.623d. Adv. Str.12.3.26

ἐπιφορτίζω.definition: load heavily, overload, J.Ap.2.9; Gp.9.14.6: metaph., Phld.Po.5.2; Gal.8.785; lay a heavier burden upon, Aët.7.91:—Med., X.Eph.5.2: metaph., levy blackmail on, Sch.Ar.Pl.379:—Pass., have excessive burdens laid on one,…

ἐπίφραξις.definition: obstruction of the earth, in eclipses, Plu.2.891f, Anaximand.11

ἐπιφράσσω.definition: Att. block up, Thphr.HP9.3.2; Nic.Al.285: metaph., Ph.1.299, al.:—Med., stop one's ears, Luc.Im.14:—Pass., to be obstructed, Placit.2.29.1; Ph.2.165

ἐπιφρίσσω.definition: Att. to be rough or bristling on the surface, Emp.83.2; D.P.443; cj. in Nonn.D.35.55; esp. of water, .. make a ripple on the calm sea, Opp.C.1.384, cf. Orph.A.1149, Poll.1.106

ἐπιφροσύνη.definition: thoughtfulness, wisdom, .. Od.5.437: in pl., 19.22, cf. Hes.Th.658, A.R.4.1115; observation, Arat.762; prudent reserve, A.R.3.659: also in late Prose, Ph.1.203, al. ; J.AJ15.11.3; Onos.Praef.1

ἐπιφυλλίς.definition: small grapes left for gleaners, AP6.191 , LXXLa.2.20; interpol. in Dsc.4.142: metaph., of poetasters, Ar.Ra.92, cf. Sch. ad loc., D.H.Rh.10.18

ἐπίφυσις.definition: ongrowth, excrescence; Anat., epiphysis, Hp.Art.27, Fract.12; opp. , Gal.2.733

ἐπιφυτεύω.definition: plant over or upon a thing, Ar.Pax168 : metaph., in Pass., LXX4 Ma.15.6

ἐπιφύω.definition: make to grow, produce on or besides; Pass., with aor. 2 and pf. Act., upon, Hdt.4.34; esp. as an excrescence, Arist.HA605a3; Plb.1.81.7; with or without the conjunctiva, Gal.7.101, Steph.in Hp.1.88 D.: hence, adhere, …

ἐπιφώνημα.definition: a witty saying, Plu.Alex.3; Rhet., phrase added by way of ornament or as a finishing touch, Phld.Rh.1.173 S. , D.H.Rh.10.18, Demetr.Eloc.106, 109, Quint.8.5.11, Hermog.Inv.4.9, S.E.M.2.57

ἐπιχαίνω.definition: gape at, Luc.Tim.18,Sacr.9,al; desire greedily, Ph.1.211, cf. 2.202

ἐπιχαιρεκακέω.definition: rejoice at another's misfortune, Phld.D. 1.11, cf. Ph.1.314

ἐπιχαιρεκακία.definition: joy over one's neighbour's misfortune, spite, malignity, Arist.EN1107a10, Ph.2.394, Plu.2.91b, etc

ἐπιχαιρέκακος.definition: rejoicing over one's neighbour's misfortune, Anaxandr.59, Alex.51, Arist.EN1108b5, Ph.2.269, Gal.4.817

ἐπιχαλεπαίνω.definition: to be angry at, Hsch. and Apollon.Lex. s.v

ἐπιχαλκεύω.definition: forge upon an anvil, A.Fr.307; Pass., to be wrought upon, J.AJ3.6.3

ἐπίχαλκος.definition: covered with copper or brass, brazen, Hdt.4.200, Ar.V.18; of a flute-player, Alc.Com.20; , Amips.17

ἐπιχαράσσω.definition: slash through, Heliod. ap. Orib.47.14.3; impress upon, Plu.Publ.11:—Pass., to be branded, Sch.Il.Oxy.1086.30

ἐπιχαριεντίζομαι.definition: quote as a good joke, Luc.Symp.12

ἐπιχαρίζομαι.definition: make a present of, X.Eq.6.12; intr., be civil to him, Ar.Ach.884

ἐπίχαρις.definition: neut. pleasing, charming, A.Th.910 , etc.; X.Cyr.1.4.4; Pl.Lg.853d; Id.R.474d; of the hare, X.Cyn.5.33; pleasantness of manner, Id.An.2.6.12; elegance, of mathematical study, Pl.R.528d: Comp. and Sup. , X.Smp.7.5, Oec…

ἐπιχάρτης.definition: one who rejoices malignantly, Philonid.II : condemned by Poll.3.101

ἐπίχαρτος.definition: wherein one feels joy, S.Tr.1262; more freq., wherein one feels malignant joy, Id.Pr.159 ; Th.3.67, cf. D.45.85; Pl.Ep.356b

ἐπιχέζω.definition: fut. ease oneself upon, Ar.Lys.440,Ec.640: pf., Id.Av.68

ἐπιχείρησις.definition: an attempt upon, attack; dialectical reasoning , Arist.Top.111b16, al.; Plb.12.7.4, cf. Phld.Sign.29 , D.H.Amm.1.8, Plu.2.698a, S.E.P.2.192 ; things capable of proof or disproof, Hermog.Prog.5

ἐπιχειρητής.definition: an enterprising person, opp. Th.8.96, cf. D.C.59.17: c. gen., ready to attempt, Pl.Ti.69d

ἐπιχειρίζω.definition: set upon, attack, Hsch.s.v; while at his post of basilicogrammateus, POxy.1274.7 , cf. Sammelb.4472

ἐπιχειρογραφέω.definition: add an attestation to, PSI5.509.18 , cf.515.8

ἐπιχειρονομέω.definition: gesticulate, Ph.1.298,2.485: metaph., grasp at, ib.371 ; = Hsch

ἐπιχειροτονέω.definition: sanction or confirm by vote, of the; confirm in office, Arist.Ath.43.4, cf.37.1; the shall confirm the appointment, Lex ap.D.24.39: hence, of a Roman Tribune, got the Praetorship for him, Plu.Mar.35

ἐπιχειροτονία.definition: voting by show of hands, Pl.Lg.755e; confirmation of the powers of magistrates, D.58.27 , Arist.Ath.55.4; .. ib.61.2

ἐπιχερρονησιάζω.definition: approach a peninsular form, dub. in Str.6.3.1

ἐπιχλευάζω.definition: jeer, abs., Ph.1.193,426, al.: c. acc., make a mock of, Plu.Num.22; App.Syr.53; mock at, .. Plu.2.93b; say scornfully, .. Babr.82.4, cf. Ph.2.436

ἐπιχορηγέω.definition: supply, furnish, HeroDioptr.31; 2 Ep.Cor.9.10; Ep.Gal.3.5; Dam.Pr.341; esp. of a husband, provide for a wife, POxy.905.10 , cf. 282.6 ; conversely, LXXSi.25.22:—Pass., Peripl.M.Rubr.60; D.H.1.42; .. Ep.Col.2.19

ἐπιχρεία.definition: use, need, PFlor.207 ; equipment, stores, of a ship, PLond.3.948.12

ἐπιχρηματίζω.definition: enact a subsequent measure, SIG704 H 24

ἐπιχρησμῳδέω.definition: make an oracular pronouncement upon, Philostr.VS1.8.2: c. acc., Id.VA5.14

ἐπίχρισις.definition: smearing over, Str.4.4.6 , cf. Sever. ap.Aët.7.96

ἐπίχριστος.definition: smeared on, Luc.Am.41; rouged, painted, Max.Tyr.37.4: metaph., Id.31.6; Luc.Tim.28

ἐπιχρονίζω.definition: last long, Thphr.Ign.61; Arist.Pr.936a20; inveterate, chronic, Gal.11.103:— Pass., when cooled in course of time, Arist.Pr.942a33

ἐπιχρώννυμι.definition: and fut. pf. Plu. : —rub or smear over, colour on the surface, tinge, Ruf.Anat.30, Plu.2.395e, cf. Plot.4.5.7; with a thing, Luc.Dom.8; .. .. Id.Im.16: metaph., Plot.5.6.4:— Pass., merely tinged with.., Pl.Ep.340d

ἐπίχυμα.definition: an eye-disease, =; extra amount of oil, PRyl.97.5

ἐπίχυτος.definition: poured over: as Subst; coin or cast of silver or lead, Hsch

ἐπιχωνεύω.definition: remould, PSI4.441.7 ; cast, PLeid. X.21,84; cast upon, on top, Ph.Byz.Mir.4.3

ἐπιχώννυμι.definition: and heap up, 1923.39; fill up, Thphr.HP9.3.2; X.Eph.4.6; D.S.13.107 codd

ἐπιχώομαι.definition: Dep. to be angry at, A.R.3.367

ἐπιχωρέω.definition: yield, give way, S.Ant.219; surrender, concede, PStrassb.114.1, cf. Arr.An.1.27.5, Plu.2.422a: c.inf., IG22.1012.24: abs., give one's consent, SIG546B3 , BCH6.26

ἐπιχώρησις.definition: concession, permission, LXX2 Es.3.7, J.AJ19.3.3, Arr.An.6.25.2; PHib.1.151

ἐπιχωριάζω.definition: of persons, to be in the habit of visiting, Pl.Phd.57a; live much with, Luc.Pseudol.19; to be occupied with, Id.Cont.1

ἐπιψάλλω.definition: play the lyre, S.Fr.60, Poll.4.58 ; Plu.2.713b; sing, LXX2 Ma.1.30:—Pass., Ph.1.626

ἐπιψεύδομαι.definition: lie still more, X.Hier.2.16; attribute falsely, A.R.3.381, cf.Ph.2.319, Plu.Mar.16, Luc.Tox.42

ἐπιψηφίζω.definition: put to the vote, in Senate or Assembly; abs., put the question, Th.6.14, etc.; of Socrates, X.Mem.1.1.18; in the preface to decrees, IG22.44, al., cf. Decr. ap. And.1.77; Th.1.87; Luc.Tim.44

ἐπιψύχω.definition: cool, A.R.2.525, Ph.2.345, Plu.Sert.8; Pass., take a chill afterwards, Hp.Mul.1.54; but to be cooled still more, Gal.11.567

ἐποίγνυμι.definition: or v. but Aeol. for Hdn.Gr.2.436

ἐποικίδιος.definition: presiding over the house, of; gloss on Sch.Pi.P.1.188

ἐποικίζω.definition: settle in a colony, App.BC1.96; = Paus.4.26.6:—Pass., ib.28.1

ἐποίκιον.definition: outhouse, farmstead, etc., IG9.47; village, LXX1 Ch.27.25, PTeb.382.6 , POxy.2137.12, 2142.3

ἐποικοδομέω.definition: build upon, X.An.3.4.11; Pl.Lg.736e; OGI483.117 : metaph., Pl.Lg.793c ; Ph.1.610; Arr.Epict.2.15.8 ; or 1 Ep.Cor.3.12, Ep.Eph.2.20; Sor.1.47 ; Paus.8.2.6, cf. Dam.Pr.87

ἐποικοδόμησις.definition: building up : metaph., piling up of expressions, climax, Arist.GA724a29; Longin.39.3

ἐποικοδομία.definition: = foreg., Haussoullier Cinquantenaire de l'école des hautes études p.89 , SIG799 ii 4 , prob. in J.AJ19.1.15

ἐποικονομία.definition: apportionment, rhetorical arrangement of them, Longin.11.2

ἐποικτείρω.definition: or have compassion on, Xenoph.7.3, S.Aj.121, OT671, etc.: abs., A.Ag.1069

ἐποικτίζω.definition: compassionate, c. acc., S.OT1296:—Med., bewail, lament, J.BJ1.27.3

ἐποιχνέω.definition: ply, practise, Aristonous1.11; visit, AP12.131 , cf. PBodl.ined.32471, prob. l. in B.9.1

ἐποκέλλω.definition: of the ship, run aground, be wrecked, Id.8.102, Plb.1.20.15; put in, Arr.An.2.23.3; of tunnies, Arist.Mir.844a30

ἐπολισθάνω.definition: slip or glide upon, J.BJ3.7.29; AP10.15.3 : metaph., ib.5.277

ἐπολολύζω.definition: shout for joy, triumph at, abs., A.Ag.1236 , Ar.Eq.616 ; at or to one, A.Th.825 ; over or at a thing, Id.Ch.942

ἔπομβρος.definition: very rainy, Hp.Aph.3.11, Epid.3.2; Arist.HA601b26 ; Thphr.HP8.7.6

ἐπονομάζω.definition: apply a word as a name to a thing; call by a name, ib.397d; called the Muses by this name , ib.406a; Id.Phd.103b; with pleon., Id.Prm.133d:—Pass., to be named, after one, Th.6.2, etc. ; also to be named the temple of.…

ἐποξίζω.definition: turn acid, Erot. and Suid. s.v

ἐποξύνω.definition: hasten, LXX2 Ma.9.7; stimulate, excite, Hierocl.in CA8p.431M

ἐποποιός.definition: epic poet, Hdt.2.120, Arist.Po.1447b14, Neanth.26J.: generally, verse-maker, Luc.JTr.6

ἐποπτεία.definition: highest grade of initiation at the Eleusinian mysteries, Plu.Demetr.26, Sch.Ar.Ra.757; initiation into.., Mich.in EN603.34; Hierocl.in CA26p.481M

ἐπόπτειρα.definition: fem. of 1, cj. for in Herm. ap. Stob.1.49.44

ἐποργίζομαι.definition: to be wroth at, LXXDa.11.40: abs., ib.2 Ma.7.33

ἐπορθιάζω.definition: set upright, prick the ears, v.l. in Ph.2.4: but mostly of the voice, lift up at or over, A.Ag.29; ib.1120: abs., lift up the voice in wailing, Id.Pers.1050

ἐπορθρεύω.definition: rise early, Hsch.,EM368.1:—Med., D.Chr.12.3, Luc.Gall.1, Poll.1.71

ἐπορίνω.definition: urge on, v.l. in Nic.Th.671, Man.6.597

ἐπορχέομαι.definition: dance over or at, dancing to the tune of.., D.18.260: abs., dance, Ph.2.485: metaph., triumph over, App.Pun.66

ἐποστρακίζω.definition: send potsherds skimming over the water, play at ducks and drakes, EM368.3: hence, Poll.9.119

ἔπουρος.definition: blowing favourably, S.Tr.954; a kind of fish, Hsch

ἐπούρωσις.definition: dub. in Licymn. ap. Arist.Rh.1414b17, prob. a speeding onward, as by a gale: v.l. ap.Sch. ad loc

ἐποφείλω.definition: owe still, Th.8.5, cf. D.C.51.21:—Pass., Id.42.51

ἐποφθαλμιάω.definition: cast longing glances at, ogle, Ael.NA3.44, cf. Fr.81; Plu.Caes.2; Id.Dem.25; eye jealously, POxy.1630.6 ; v.l. in Hyp.Fr.258

ἐποφλισκάνω.definition: owe still more, Them.Or.6.83a, cf. Men.Prot.p.34 D.:—Pass., aor. part. PMasp.168.63

ἐποχετεύω.definition: carry water by sluices or courses, Pl.Grg.493e; .. Id.Criti.117b; Ph.1.398; Longus4.4: metaph., Ph.2.359; .. Plu.2.660c, cf. Jul.Or.4.137d, Dam.Pr.35, etc.:—Pass., to be so brought, Arist.PA666a6; are conducted one in…

ἐπόψιος.definition: also Arat.258: :—full in; Act., overlooking all things, epith. of gods, S.Ph.1040; esp. of Zeus, SIG1264 , A.R.2.1123, 1133, Call.Jov.82, Ant.Lib.6.2

ἑπταβόειος.definition: of seven bulls'-hides, Il.7.220,222, etc.; comically, Ar.Ra.1017

ἑπταεικοσαπλασίων.definition: gen. twenty-seven times as great, Hipparch. ap. Theo Sm.p.197H

ἑπτάζωνος.definition: seven-zoned, of the planetary system, Vett. Val.144.14, Paul.Al.I.3, Nonn.D.1.241; PMag. Leid.W.6.5

ἑπτακαιεικοσιμόριος.definition: containing a twenty-seventh part, Theol. Ar.4

ἑπτάκλινος.definition: with seven couches or beds, Phryn.Com.66, X.Smp.2.18; Callix. I; and without Tim.Com.I ; place seven seats, Eub.121; provides sitting-room for seven, Arist.HA630a22: hence, as a measure of area, Ph.Bel.80.48

ἑπτάλοφος.definition: seven-hilled, of Rome, Cic.Att. 6.5.2, AP14.121 , cf. Plu.2.280d

ἑπταμερής.definition: having seven parts, Ph.1.45, cf. Procl.in Ti.2.209D

ἑπταμηνιαῖος.definition: born in the seventh month, Cic.Att.10.18.1, J.AJ5.11.4, Placit.5.18.5:—also Theol.Ar.48

ἑπτάμηνος.definition: a space of seven months, Placit.5.18.1, cf. IG12.53

ἑπταμήτωρ.definition: mother of seven children, LXX4 Ma.16.24

ἑπτάνευρον.definition: prob. f.l. for II, Paul.Aeg.7.17, Apul.Herb.I

ἑπταπάλαιστος.definition: seven palms long, S.E.M.9.321:—early Att. IG12.373.237

ἑπταπλασιάζω.definition: multiply seven times, Dam.Pr.98, HeroGeom.17.7: hence, ib.33

ἑπταπλάσιος.definition: sevenfold, Pl.Ep.332a, cf. Iamb.in Nic.p.102 P. Adv. LXXPs.11.6,al

ἑπτάπορος.definition: with seven tracks or paths, of the planets, h.Hom.8.7; or E.IA7, Or.1005 ; Epigr.Gr.223.4 ; seven-mouthed, of the Nile, Mosch.2.51, D.P.264

ἑπτάπυλος.definition: with seven gates, epith. of Boeotian; stairway symbolizing the ascent of the soul through the seven planetary spheres, Cels. ap. OrigenesCels.6.22

ἑπτάπυργος.definition: seven-towered, of Boeotian Thebes, E.Ph.245 , etc.: metaph., LXX4 Ma.13.7

ἑπτάσημος.definition: of seven times, in metre, Heph.11.5, cf. 12.1, Aristid.Quint.1.14

ἑπταστάδιος.definition: seven stades long, Scymn.649; Str.2.5.19; J.AJ12.2.13: Subst., space of seven stades, Str.2.5.22

ἑπτάστομος.definition: seven-mouthed, of Boeotian Thebes, E.Supp.401; Id.Ph.287, Ba.919; S.Fr.773; of rivers, Str.4.1.8, 7.3.15

ἑπτάτονος.definition: seven-toned, Terp.5; B.Scol.Oxy.1361 Fr. 1.2; Ion Eleg.3.3; E.Alc.446

ἑπταφάρμακον.definition: drug compounded of seven ingredients, Aët.15.26

ἑπτάφωνος.definition: seven-voiced, of a colonnade with a sevenfold echo at Olympia, Plu.2.502d, Luc.Peregr.40, Plin.HN36.100

ἑπτετηρίς.definition: festival celebrated every seven years, Arist.Ath.54.7

ἐπώδυνος.definition: painful, Hp.VM22, Prog.7; Ar.Ach.1205 ; Ph.2.579; Plu.2.114c: irreg. Comp. Hp.Art.49. Adv. Ph.1.136

ἐπωμάδιος.definition: on the shoulders, Theoc.29.29 , cf. APl.4.108

ἐπωμίζομαι.definition: Med., put on one's shoulder, Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.4

ἐπωνυμία.definition: Ion. derived or; generally, name, title, Id.2.4, cf. Pl.R.394a, PHal.1.251 , etc.; Sor.Vit.Hippocr.13

ἐπωνύμιον.definition: surname, Plu.2.560e; Id.Pyrrh.1; = Lat. cognomen, D.H.5.19

ἐπωνύμιος.definition: poet. for sq. I.3, called after or by the name of, Pi.P.1.30, v.l. in Hdt.2.112; Pi.O.10.78

ἐπωπετής.definition: epith. of Zeus at Athens, Hsch

ἐπωπίς.definition: epith. of Demeter at Sicyon, Id

ἐπωτειλόομαι.definition: Pass., to be scarred over, Aret.SD2.4

ἐπωφελέω.definition: aid, succour, S.El.578,Ph.905; Id.El.1005, E.Or.955, cf. Ar.Nu.1442; S.OC441, E.Andr.677: abs., Pl.Lg.843c; Seleuc. ap. Ath.15.697d:—Pass., receive aid, Phalar.Ep.137. —In S.OC541 , .. the Sch. takes as, = would that …

ἐπωφελής.definition: helpful, useful, Sever.Clyst.p.17 D., Poll.5.136, Cod.Just.1.2.17.1; Hierocl.in CA11p.441M. Adv. Poll.5.135, Vett. Val.165.18, Them.Or.21.252a,22.278c

ἐρανάρχης.definition: president of an collector of contributions to it, BGU1133.5 , D.L.6.63, Artem.1.35 , Harp. s.v. —hence hold this office, IG11.1223

ἐρανίζω.definition: lay under contribution, c. acc. pers; collect by way of contribution, Aeschin.3.45; Pl.Lg.915e: abs., Thphr.Char.1.5; for their benefit, IG7.411.7 : metaph., bring together, combine, AP9.13b , cf.11 , Ael.VH12.1; art …

ἐρανιστής.definition: member of or contributor to an I, Pherecyd.11 J. ; to give a club-dinner, Ar.Fr.408, Arist.EN1123a22; member of an III, IG22.1265 , 11.1223 , etc

ἐρασίμολπος.definition: delighting in song, of Thalia, Pi.O.14.15

ἐραστής.definition: lover, prop. c. gen. pers; admirer, Pl.Men.70b, Ly.222a, Prt.317c

ἐράστρια.definition: fem. of lover, Eup.414; Perict. ap. Stob.4.28.19, cf.Ael.NA3.40

ἐρατώνυμος.definition: of gracious fame, B.16.31; cj. in Stes.44

ἐρατῶπις.definition: of lovely look, IG14.1356.8, v.l. in Hom.Epigr.1.2

ἐργασείω.definition: Desiderat. of long to do. be about to do, S.Tr.1232; Id.Ph.1001

ἐργαστηριάρχης.definition: foreman of a workshop, CIG4968 , Anatolian Studies 30

ἐργαστήριον.definition: any place in which work is done; metaph., X.HG3.4.17; Lib.Or.55.34

ἐργαστής.definition: = A.D.Adv.135.4, IGRom.4.1209 ; = Lat.negotiator, SIG1229.1 ; v.l. in J.AJ18.1.1, Gal.Thras.33

ἐργατεία.definition: labour, work, handicraft, in pl; gang of workmen, ibid., POxy.1450.6

ἐργατεύομαι.definition: work hard, labour, LXXTo.5.5, D.S.20.92:— Act., UPZ110.102

ἐργάτης.definition: workman, Hermes 17.5; in the religious sense, 2 Ep.Ti.2.15, 2 Ep.Cor.11.13

ἐργεπιστατέω.definition: to be superintendent of works, OGI510.12 , IGRom.4.1352 , 818 , Sch.Ar.Pax605

ἐργεπιστάτης.definition: superintendent of works, Epich.212, Artem.4.31, IG3.486 , 12.253

ἐργοδιωκτέω.definition: to be a taskmaster, LXX2 Ch.8.10

ἐργοδοτέω.definition: let out work, opp. Apollod.Com.20, CIG 2826.5

ἐργοδότης.definition: one who farms out work, X.Cyr.8.2.5, CIG3467.22 ; un-Attic, acc. to Phryn.326; incorrectly used of workmen, Aret.SD1.6

ἐργολάβεια.definition: = II, making profit out of them, Alciphr.1.34

ἐργολαβέω.definition: contract for the execution of work, opp; make profit out of, Phld.Rh.1.329S.; so of Sophists, Alciphr.3.55: so abs., freq. in Oratt., Aeschin.2.112, cf. D.22.49; in a matter, Aeschin.3.33; for one, D.25.47; or against…

ἐργολάβος.definition: Adj.for gain, gainful, v.l. in Plb.20.12.1

ἐργοπόνος.definition: husbandman, AP11.9 ; hunter, Opp.C.1.148; fisher, Nic.Th.831; a worker in.., Man.1.298: as Adj., laborious, Coluth.195 ; in bad sense , Rhetor.inCat.Cod.Astr.7.198

ἐργωνέω.definition: contract for a work, Hermes 17.4 , IG11.150 A14 , 7.3073.92

ἐργώνης.definition: a contractor, Hermes 17.4 , IG11.150 A9 , 7.3073.4 , SIG495.135 : Dor. IG 4.1508

ἐρεβινθιαῖος.definition: of the size of an Dsc.5.137, 152

ἐρέγμινος.definition: made of bruised beans, Dsc.3.80.3, Orib.4.8.7

ἐρεγμός.definition: = Gal.6.533, Archig. ap; = Mim.Oxy.413.19, Moer.p.158 P., EM371.20

ἐρέθισμα.definition: provocation, App.Sam.3; Ar.Nu.312 ; of Anacreon, Critias1 D.; i.e. by purging, Aret.CA2.5

ἐρεθισμός.definition: irritation, Hp.Acut.43; provocation, Phld.Ir.p.54 W. , D.H.10.33

ἐρεθιστής.definition: rebellious or perverse person, LXXDe.21.18, Ph.1.359, Hsch. s.v

ἐρείκη.definition: heath, Erica arborea, A.Ag.295, Eup.14.4, Theoc.5.64, Thphr.HP1.14.2, Dsc.1.88.—The Inscr. quoted s.v. proves that is correct ; is the later spelling, v

ἐρεικίς.definition: pounded barley, groats, mostly in pl., written Gal.19.100:—Cret. Hsch

ἐρείκω.definition: bruise, pound, of pulse, Ar.Fr.22, cf. Dieuch. ap. Orib.4.6.4; Hp.Morb.2.67, Mul.2.113, Superf.34; Id.Nat.Mul.103; Arist.HA595b7; Diocl.Fr.140; shattered them, A.Ag.655; of pain, S.Fr.152

ἐρείπιον.definition: fallen ruin, wreck, Arist.Rh.1413a6, Aristid.Or.49.42, Opp.H.5.324: generally in pl., wreckage, A.Ag.660, Fr.274, E.Hel.1080; A.Pers.425; ruins, Hdt.2.154,4.124; E.Ba.7; alone, Cratin.151; fragments of garments, Trag.…

ἔρεισμα.definition: prop, stay, support; metaph., of a person, pillar of Agrigentum, Pi.O.2.6; Id.Fr.76, cf. Luc.Dem.Enc.10, Tim.50; of the tomb of Oedipus, S.OC58

ἐρεσχελία.definition: = EM371.1, Suid. s.v. , Gloss.; quarrel, PMonac.1.23

ἐρεσχηλέω.definition: trans., quiz, banter, Pl.Phdr.236b; Ath.6.223e, etc.; tease, worry, Ael.NA3.37, 15.22, Luc.Musc.Enc.10: c. dat. pers., Pl.Phlb.53e

ἐρετμίον.definition: Dim. of sq., cj. in Com.Adesp.607

ἐρευθέδανον.definition: madder, Rubia tinctorum, Hdt.4.189; of the wild form, Rubia tinctorum, Thphr.HP9.13.6, Dsc.3.143 : hence, dye made therefrom, PHolm.26.36

ἐρευνητής.definition: searcher, inquirer, Clearch.25, Parth.1.1: c. gen., J.AJ17.5.5, BJ1.30.7; spies, D.C.78.14; inspector, customs-officer, UPZ149.15 ; cf

ἐρεύω.definition: = Eust.670.65, Hsch.:—hence = exactor, collector of stale- debts, SIG527.132 , GDI5073.18 . .)

ἐρημαῖος.definition: poet. for desolate, solitary, Mosch.3.21, A.R.2.672, etc. ; silent, Emp.49; deserted, A.R.4.1298: c. gen., reft of, AP9.439

ἐρημία.definition: of places, a solitude, desert, wilderness, Hdt.3.98, A.Pr.2, etc.; Ar.Ach.704; Id.Lys.787; to solitary places, Arist.HA610b24, etc

ἐρημονόμος.definition: haunting the wilds, A.R.4.1333; desolate, Nonn.D.37.12, 47.510

ἐρημοπλάνος.definition: wandering alone, Orph.H.39.4 ; noted as by Demetr.Eloc.116

ἐρημοσκόπος.definition: one who keeps watch negligently, Anon. ap. Suid

ἐρημοτελωνία.definition: tax for maintenance of desert-police, PLond.2.88 , etc

ἐρημοφύλαξ.definition: desert-policeman, PCair.Zen.172.25 , etc.:— hence maintenance of this force, PFay.68 , etc

ἐρημόω.definition: strip bare, desolate, lay waste; bereave one of a thing, c. dupl. acc., Pi.P.3.97: c. acc. et gen., Id.I.4.17; to leave the oars without men, E.Hel.1609; Pl.Alc.39:—Pass., to be bereft of, Hdt.1.164; Id.7.174; Id.6.22…

ἐρήμωσις.definition: making desolate, LXXLe.26.34, al., Heph.Astr.1.21; Arr.An.1.9.7; LXXDa.9.27, cf. Ev.Matt.24.15

ἐριβρεμέτης.definition: Ep. loud-thundering, Il.13.624; of Aeschylus, Ar.Ra.814 ; D.P.578, etc.; loud-roaring, Pi.I.4.46; loud-sounding, AP6.195

ἐρίβρομος.definition: loud-shouting, of Bacchus, h.Bacch.56, Anacr.11, Panyas.13.2; loud-roaring, Pi.O.11.21; Id.P.6.3,11

ἐρίγδουπος.definition: = , loud-sounding, thundering, in Hom. epith. of Zeus, Il.5.672; Od.15.112; exc. in Il.11.152 so after Hom., Pi.Dith.Oxy.2.12; APl.4.74; Nonn.D.18.105

ἐριδάντης.definition: wrangler, Timo28.2: Ion.gen. pl. Democr.150: Dor. epith. of Heracles at Tarentum, Hsch

ἐρίδουπος.definition: = in Hom. always of things and places, Il.20.50, Od.10.515; Il.24.323, Od.20.176; resounding, Emp.4.11

ἐρίηρος.definition: as epith. of perh. faithful, trusty , in sg., only in Il.4.266: elsewh. always in heterocl. pl. acc. or Od.9.100, Il.3.47, etc.; parodied by Cratin.143; loyal to his master's house, Od.1.346, al

ἐριθαλής.definition: = Limen.6, Hsch; Subst. stone-crop, Sedum altissimum, Plin.HN25.160; cf. Hsch.; dub. l. in Ps.-Dsc.4.88

ἐριθεία.definition: labour for wages, Hsch. , Suid; canvassing for public office, intriguing, Arist.Pol.1302b4, 1303a14

ἐρικυδής.definition: very famous, glorious, of gods and their descendants, Il.14.327, Od.11.576,631; of their gifts, Il.3.65, 20.265; 11.225, Hes.Th.988; B.12.190: generally, a splendid banquet, Il.24.802, Od.3.66, al.; of places and men,…

ἐρινάζω.definition: aor. I inf. and; gather wild figs, Poll.7.143

ἐρινεόν.definition: fruit of the Hp.Loc.Hom.47: pl., PCair.Zen.33.12 , v.l. in Arist.HA557b28

ἐριοκάρτης.definition: shearer, PFlor.71.438, al. ; perh. cf. PTeb.401.1,16

ἐριοπλύτης.definition: wool-cleaner, fuller, Dsc.2.163, BGU118 iii 7 ; IGRom.4.821

ἐριοπωλέω.definition: sell or deal in wool, Poll.7.28

ἐριοπώλης.definition: a dealer in wool, Critias70 D., Poll.7.28, PLips.14.6 ; cf

ἐριοπώλιον.definition: wool-shop, in pl., Zeno Stoic.1.58, J.BJ5.8.1

ἐριουργέω.definition: work in wool, X.HG5.4.7, Lac.1.3, etc

ἐριστάφυλος.definition: of wine, made of fine grapes; rich in grapes, of Lesbos, Archestr.Fr.56.9; of Bacchus, AP9.580.6, Nonn.D.12.251

ἐριστέφανος.definition: eminently crowned, epith. of Rhea, Rev.Ét. Gr.19.268

ἐρισφάραγος.definition: loud-roaring, of Poseidon, h.Merc.187; of Zeus, Pi.Fr.15, B.5.20; loud-voiced, of men, Plu.2.698e

Ἑρμαθήνη.definition: terminal bust with head of Athena, Cic.Att.1.1.5, 1.4.3; so of busts with heads of other divinities, of Eros, Plin.HN36.33 ; of Heracles, Cic.Att.1.10.3, Milet.1 No.305; of Pan, cf

ἑρμαῖος.definition: called after Hermes, in; of Hermes, the constellation Lyra, Arat.674; , month at Argos, etc., Polyaen.8.33; in Boeotia, IG7.289, al.; in the Aetolian league, GDI 1745, al.; cf

ἑρμαιών.definition: name of a month at Halicarnassus, SIG45.4 ; in Ceos, IG22.1128

Ἑρμαφρόδιτος.definition: Hermaphrodite, or person partaking; as Adj., Leonid. ap. Paul.Aeg.6.69

ἑρμηνεύς.definition: interpreter, esp. of foreign; court interpreter, POxy.237 vii 37 , etc

ἑρμηνεύω.definition: Dor. SIG1168.88 , interpret; explain, expound, S.OC398, E.Fr.636.5, etc.; Antipho3.2.1; Philyll.11; Pl.Ion535a:—Med., Id.Epin.985b:— Pass., Arist.SE166b11

ἑρμογλυφεύς.definition: carver of Hermae : generally, statuary, Luc.Somn.2, Plu.2.580e

Ἑρμοδάκτυλον.definition: a plant, in two varieties, Colchicum luteum and autumnale, [Gal.]14.760, Alex.Trall.11

ἑρμομαχέω.definition: fight with I.4, as a game, Hsch. s.v

ἑρπετόδηκτος.definition: bitten by a reptile, Dsc.3.68, CrateuasFr.5

ἑρπηστής.definition: = Nic.Th.9, etc.; of a; guinea-worm, Hippiatr.58

ἑρπύλλινος.definition: made of tufted thyme, Eub.99; Antiph.106.7, cf. Gal.12.512

ἕρπυλλος.definition: poet. also Theoc.Ep.1, AP4.1.54 , Pancr. ap. Ath.15.677f:—tufted thyme, Thymus Sibthorpii, Cratin.98, Ar.Pax168, Thphr.HP1.9.4, al., CP2.18.2, Dsc.3.38

ἐρυγγάνω.definition: Prose and Att. form of , belch, Hp.Vict.3.76, Cratin.58: c. acc., E.Cyc.523, cf. Eup.198; Luc.Alex.39: metaph., Diph.43.21:—also in Med., c. acc., Hp.Vict.3.75

ἐρυθαίνω.definition: aor. A.R.1.791, LXXWi.13.14:—Pass., Hom. , etc.:—poet. and later Prose word for dye red, A.R.4.474; LXX l.c. ; make to blush, A.R.1.791:—Pass., to be dyed red, Il.10.484, cf. 21.21: c. gen., Nonn.D.11.92 ; blush scarl…

ἐρυθραῖος.definition: of or from Erythrae, Hdt.1.18, etc

ἐρυθρίας.definition: of ruddy complexion, opp. Arist.Cat.9b31, PPetr.3p.30

ἐρυθρίασις.definition: Ion. ruddiness, blushing, Hp.Decent.5, Hsch. s.v

ἐρυθριάω.definition: Ep. part. Musae.161: impf; to be inflamed, Aret.SA1.8

ἐρυθρόγραμμος.definition: with red lines, Arist.Fr.294, cf. Ath.7.321e

ἐρυθροδανόω.definition: dye with madder, dye red, LXXEx.25.5, 26.14

ἐρυθροπρόσωπος.definition: of a ruddy look, Anon. ap. Suid. s.v

ἐρυμνάομαι.definition: Pass., to be defended, Anon. ap. Suid

ἐρυμνότης.definition: strength or security of a place, X.Cyr.6.1.23; Arist.Pol.1330b37; the difficulties of passing them, Plb.3.47.9, etc

ἐρυμνόω.definition: fortify, make strong, Agath.2.4, EM378.31:—Pass., Nonn.D.6.386

ἐρυσίβη.definition: Orph.L.600], rust, in corn; title of Demeter in Lydia, Et.Gud.210.25

ἐρυσίβιος.definition: averting rust, epith. of Apollo at Rhodes, Str.13.1.64

ἐρυσίπελας.definition: erysipelas, Hp.VM19 , Prog.23, Aph.5.23, Gal.10.949, Orib.45.1.3 , Gp.12.23.5 , etc

ἐρυσίπτολις.definition: protecting the city, epith. of Athena, Il.6.305 codd. , h.Hom.11.1, 28.3

ἐρυσίσκηπτρον.definition: a plant, = Thphr.Od.57, Dsc.1.20; = ib.4; also, = Ps.-Dsc.3.12; = ib.4.60; cf

ἐρυσίχαιος.definition: expl. as, = carrying a shepherd's staff, Alcm.24.4; but prob. = inhabitant of in Acarnania, cf. Hdn.Gr. ap. Bgk.ad lcc

ἐρωμανέω.definition: to be mad for love, Opp.C.3.368, Nonn.D.1.136, al., AP5.266.10

ἐρώτιον.definition: = IG11.161 B 118 (Delos; charming, sweet child, Aristaenet.1.19

ἐρωτοδιδάσκαλος.definition: teacher of the art of love, Ath.5.219d

ἐρωτομανής.definition: = cj. in Stoic. ap. Stob.2.7.5b9, Orph.H.55.14 codd., Ath.13.599e, Aristaenet.1.27, etc. Adv. Zonar

ἐρωτοπαίγνιον.definition: in pl., title of amatory poems by Laevius, Gell.2.24.8

ἐρωτοτόκος.definition: producing love, Musae.159; Nonn.D.4.129; Procl.H.2.13:—fem. PMag.Par.1.2557

ἐσθέω.definition: clothe : only pf. and plpf. Pass., mostly in part. Ion. clothed or clad, in a thing, Hdt.6.112: c. dat., Id.3.129; E.Hel.1539; Pythaen.6: 3pl. pf. Ael.Fr.121: 3sg. plpf. Id.VH12.32; Id.NA16.34

ἔσθημα.definition: garment, always in pl. in Trag., clothes, raiment, as A.Pers.836, Ag.562, S.El.268, cf. Th.3.58, etc. : later in sg., Ael.VH1.2, Jul.Or.2.85a

Ἑσπερία.definition: the Western land, of Italy, Agathyll. ap. D.H.1.49; of Spain, Suid. s.v

ἑσπέριος.definition: of Time, towards evening, Hom., esp. in Od., usu. with Verbs, .. Od.15.505; 2.385; 9.452; Pi.N.6.38; at eventide, Opp.C.1.138, cf. Man.2.422; Arist.HA619b21 ; songs sung at even, Pi.P.3.19: in late Prose, Vett.Val.72.21

ἑστιάρχης.definition: the master of a feast, Plu.2.643d, prob. in CIG2052.4

ἑστιατορία.definition: allowance of food, LXX4 Ki.25.30; feast, ib.Da.5.23; PTeb.584

ἑστιατόριον.definition: later = IG11.144 A 68 , Theopomp.Hist.32, Bull.Soc.Alex.5.126 , Sammelb.6596 , D.H.2.23, SIG1109.141 : Ion. Hdt.4.35: Rhod. IG12.677

ἑστιοῦχος.definition: guarding the house; having an altar or hearth, A.Pers.511, S.Ant.1083, E.Andr.283

ἐσχάρα.definition: Ion. Ep. gen. and dat; pan of coals, brazier, Ar.Ach.888, V.938, cf. Poll.10.94, 95

ἐσχαρεών.definition: = I, Theoc.24.48, AP7.648; forge, Nonn.D.14.22, al

ἐσχάριον.definition: pan of coals, Ar.Fr.516; stand, platform, Plb.9.41.4 , D.S.20.91

ἐσχάριος.definition: of or on the hearth, AP7.210

ἐσχαρίς.definition: brazier, Alex.250, Plu.Crass.16, etc. ; CIG2859 ; IG12.51.22 ; used in fishing by night. Ael.NA2.8

ἐσχαρίτης.definition: bread baked over the fire, Antidot.3, Crobyl.2, LXX2 Ki.6.19, J.AJ7.4.2

ἐσχάρωσις.definition: formation of an eschar, Arist.Pr.863a14, Heliod. ap. Orib.45.19.1, Sor.2.41

ἐσχατιά.definition: Ion. farthest part, edge; border of a country, Od.3.294; Il.9 484; alone, Od.14.104; Archil.89.4: pl., the extremities of the world, Hdt.3.106; also, borders, frontier-land, Id.6.127: abs., Id.3.115,116, X.HG2.4.4, et…

ἑταιρεία.definition: at Athens and elsewhere, political club or union for party purposes, Eup.8.6 D., Com.Adesp.22.31 D., Th.3.82, Lys.12.55, Isoc.4.79 ; Pl.R.365d; Id.Tht.173d;at Carthage, compared to the at Sparta, Arist.Pol.1272b34, cf…

ἑταιρεῖος.definition: amorous, h.Merc.58; AP9.415; house of a Sch. Ar.Eq.873

ἑταιρεύομαι.definition: Pass., prostitute oneself, D.S.12.21, Theopomp. Hist.217c

ἑταιριστής.definition: lewd man, Poll.6.188:— fem. = Pl.Smp.191e, Luc.DMeretr.5.2, Tim.Lex

ἑτεράλκεια.definition: varying fortune of battle, coined by Eust.662.46

ἑτεραλκής.definition: giving strength to the other side; Act., a body of men which decides the victory, Il.15.738; Nic.Th.2; of a lame man, Nonn.D.9.230

ἑτερεγκεφαλάω.definition: or to suffer in half the brain, to be half-mad, crazy, Ar.Fr.778

ἑτερήμερος.definition: on alternate days, day and day about, of the Dioscuri, Od.11.303, cf. Ph.2.189, Jul.Or.4.147a; Ph.1.643; of an intermittent fever, Orph.L.633

ἑτεροβάρεια.definition: weighing down to one side, Hsch., Suid. s.v

ἑτερογάστριος.definition: by another mother, opp. Tz.ad Hes.Op.374

ἑτερογενής.definition: of different kinds; of different kind or race, Demetr.Lac.1012.36 F., D.T.635.7; Dam.Pr.308; simply, different, D.S.1.9. Adv. S.E.M.7.361, cf. Nicom.Ar.1.10

ἑτερόγλωσσος.definition: Att. of other (i.e; of diverse tongues, Ph.1.406

ἑτερόγναθος.definition: with one side of the mouth harder than the other, X.Eq.1.9, al.; glossed by Phot

ἑτερογνωμοσύνη.definition: difference of opinion, J.AJ10.11.7, Hsch. s.v

ἑτεροδίδακτος.definition: taught by another, opp. Olymp.in Alc.p.11 C

ἑτεροδιδασκαλέω.definition: teach differently, teach false doctrine, 1 Ep.Ti.1.3

ἑτεροδοξέω.definition: hold an erroneous opinion, Pl.Tht.190e; differ in opinion, Ph.1.508

ἑτερόδοξος.definition: differing in opinion, Luc.Eun.2; holding opinions other than the right, heterodox, Ph.1.403, al., Arr.Epict.2.9.19, J.BJ2.8.5; Sor.1.52, cf. Gal.9.670. Adv. in heterodox manner, Philostr.VS2.1.11

ἑτεροδύναμος.definition: of different power or faculty, Porph.Sent.33

ἑτεροεθνής.definition: of another tribe, foreign, Str.8.1.2, Ph.2.400

ἑτεροζυγία.definition: inclination to one side, of the balance, Sch.Luc.Lex.3

ἑτεροθαλής.definition: flourishing on one side: of children of the same father, but different mothers, Cat.Cod.Astr.8.110, Eust.1283.2, Tz.ad Hes.Op.374

ἑτερόθρησκος.definition: practising a false religion, interpol. in Suid. s.v

ἑτεροῖος.definition: Ep. D.P.1180:—of a; diversified, differentiated, Dam.Pr.194, 204

ἑτεροιότης.definition: difference in kind, Pl.Prm.160d, Ph.1.5; Dam.Pr.440

ἑτεροίωσις.definition: alteration, Diog.Apoll.5 ; opp. Arist.Ph.217b26, cf. Mu.400a24 ; Epicur.Ep.2p.43U. ; of sensation, Chrysipp.Stoic.2.23; Plu.2.430c, A.D.Pron.18.15, M.Ant.4.39: mythological transformations, title of work by Nicander, …

ἑτερόκαρπος.definition: bearing different fruit, of grafts, Hp.Nat.Puer.26

ἑτεροκίνητος.definition: moved by external force, incapable of self-motion, opp. Id.Inst.14, Simp.in Epict.p.10 D., Dam.Pr.18,al., Syrian.in Metaph.23.21. Adv. Simp.in Epict.p.4 D

ἑτεροκλινέω.definition: lean on one side, Anon.Intr. Arat.p.98 M., Sm.Ps.16 .11, Phryn.PSp.68 B.; cf

ἑτεροκλινής.definition: leaning to one side, uneven, Hp.Art.24; of a building, D.C.57.21; sloping ground, X.Cyn.2.7. Adv. one-sidedly, Sor.2.62; to have a propensity to it, Arr.Epict.3.12.7

ἑτερόκλιτος.definition: irregularly inflected, of nouns, as A.D.Synt.102.12, etc.; of Verbs, as Id.Pron.13.2. Adv. Eust.113.41

ἑτεροκρανία.definition: pain on one side of the head , Archig. ap. Gal.8.94, Aret.CD1.2, etc. . Adj. liable to such pain, Antyll. ap. Orib.10.19.1

ἑτεροκωφέω.definition: to be deaf of one ear, LXXSi.19.27

ἑτερόκωφος.definition: deaf on one side, Cyrill. ap. Valck.Animadv. ad Ammon.p.65

ἑτερόμαλλος.definition: woolly, shaggy on one side, Str.5.1.12: also Hsch. s.v

ἑτερομάσχαλος χιτών.definition: a frock with only one hole for the arm, i.e. only coming over one shoulder, worn by slaves, opp. Poll.7.47, Sch.Ar.Eq.878

ἑτερομέρεια.definition: inclination to one side, Suid., Phot. s.v

ἑτερόμορφος.definition: of different or diverse form, Ael.NA12.16, Ph.1.655; opp. Ptol.Tetr.145; so of monstrosities, Alex.Aphr.Pr.2.47: hence monstrosity, of the Minotaur, Isid.Etym.11.3.9

ἑτεροούσιος.definition: differing in substance, Porph.Sent.35. Adv. ib.37:—also in form ib.32, cf. Iamb.Myst.1.19

ἑτεροπλατής.definition: with unequal sides, of beams, Apollod.Poliorc.161.12

ἑτερόπλευρος.definition: with two visible faces, SIG247; with unequal sides, Scymn.267

ἑτερόπλοος.definition: contr. lent on bottomry with the risk of the outward, but not of the homeward, voyage, D.34.30; Id.56.29; Id.34.8

ἑτεροποδέω.definition: go lame of one foot, Hippiatr.109

ἑτερόπους.definition: gen. with uneven feet, halting, Alciphr.3.27, Philostr.VS1.21.1, Hippiatr.13

ἑτεροπρόσωπος.definition: of another person: when a statement is made in the words of another, Phoeb.Fig.1.5, cf. Choerob.Rh.p.256S. Adv. Proll.Hermog. in Rh.7.7 W

ἑτερόπτολις.definition: of another city, Erinn.5; of various cities, Nonn.D.26.41

ἑτερόρρυθμος.definition: of different rhythm: hence, of the pulse, having a false rhythm, i.e. unsuitable to the patient's age, Gal.8.516, al

ἑτεροσήμαντος.definition: of different signification, Eust.1411.43. Adv. Sch.Hes.Sc.354

ἑτεροσκελής.definition: with uneven legs, Hippiatr.13; of a triangle, scalene, Poll.4.161

ἑτερόστοιχος.definition: belonging to the other series, Hsch., Phot

ἑτερόστομος.definition: one-edged, Poll.1.137; a marching formation in which the of the leading are on the r., those of the rear on the l., or vice versa, Ascl.Tact.10.22, etc. Adv. ib.11.4

ἑτερόστροφος.definition: consisting of two different strophes, Heph.Poëm.5.3, Sch.Ar.Nu.263

ἑτερόσφυκτος.definition: having one wrist-pulse different from the other, Marcellin.Puls.147:—hence Gal.18.301

ἑτεροσχημάτιστος.definition: differently formed: change of grammatical form, as a figure of speech, Phoeb.Fig.1.5

ἑτεροσχήμων.definition: of varying shape, Thphr.HP1.10.1; altered in shape, distorted, Luc.Hist.Conscr.51. Adv. Vett.Val.333.20:— later irregular, Heliod. ap. Orib.48.20.15

ἑτεροτράχηλος.definition: with neck turned to one side, of Alexander, Tz.H.11 No.368 tit

ἑτερότροπος.definition: of different sort or fashion, Ar.Th.724; Opp.H.1.379; various, AP9.768 , cf. Nonn.D.2.669, 7.7

ἑτεροφθαλμία.definition: difference of the two eyes, Hippiatr.13, Dem. Ophth. ap. Simon. Jan. s.v. ethereoftalmia

ἑτερόφθαλμος.definition: one-eyed, D.24.141; with different-coloured eyes, Gp.16.2.1

ἑτερόφρων.definition: gen. thinking strangely, raving, Tryph.439; AP1.19 , cf. Nonn.D.9.49

ἑτερόφυλος.definition: of another race or breed, Ael.NA16.27, Scymn.101; opp. Iamb.VP16.69: generally, differing in kind, Dam.Pr.74; of different kinds, Simp.in Ph.890.16

ἑτεροφωνέομαι.definition: to be different in sound, Eust.1626.3

ἑτεροφωνία.definition: diversity of note, Pl.Lg.812d; title of work, Thphr.Fr.181

ἑτεροχροέω.definition: to be of different colour, AB386; to be discoloured, of bones, Orib.46.11.7

ἑτερόχροια.definition: difference of colour, Hierocl.p.21 A., Xenocr.28, Gal.14.325

ἐτήσιος.definition: and in Hp. :— lasting a; annual, Plu.2.993e; Th.5.11, etc., cf. SIG1024.24 ; IG7.2227 ; Cratin.23; = Arist.Pr.940a35; Arr.Ind.21.1. Adv. Sch.Lyc.107: neut. as Adv., AP5.226

ἐτητυμία.definition: poet. truth, Call.Aet.3.1.76, AP9.771 , Max.462, Orph.Fr.280.7

ἑτοιμασία.definition: preparation, Aen.Tact.21.1, cf. LXXPs.9.38 ; ib.Wi.13.12; equipment, Ep.Eph.6.15

ἑτοιμοκόλλιξ.definition: one who gives rolls freely, Com.Adesp.1094

ἑτοιμόπτωτος.definition: inclined to fall, gloss on AB367

ἑτοιμοπωλεῖον.definition: cook-shop where dressed meats are sold, BGU 1647.6

ἐτυμολογέω.definition: argue from etymology, Diogenian; analyse a word and find its origin, Ath.2.35b, cf. Corn.ND32; ib.1, Str.1.2.34; An.Ox.3.220; EM220.37; Phlp.in de An.92.4:—Pass., Str.13.1.52

ἐτυμολογία.definition: etymology, Id.16.4.29, D.H.Comp.16, A.D.Adv.153.13, Ph.1.354, etc

ἐτυμόλογος.definition: studying etymology: as Subst., etymologist, EM199.24, Varro LL6.39

εὐαγγελίζομαι.definition: impf., Paus.4.19.5: fut. part; preach or proclaim as glad tidings, Ev.Luc.4.43, etc.; Ep.Eph.2.17, etc

εὐαγγέλιον.definition: reward of good tidings, given to the; good tidings, good news, in pl., LXX2 Ki.4.10, Cic.Att.2.3.1, 13.40.1, Inscr.Prien.105.40 : sg., J.BJ2.17.4, Luc.Asin.26, App.BC3.93, Sammelb.421

εὐαγγελιστής.definition: bringer of good tidings: hence; proclaimer of oracular messages, IG12.675

εὐάγγελος.definition: bringing good news, A.Ag.21; ib.262, etc.; ib.646; IG14.1120; Opp.H.5.237; title of Hermes, Hsch

εὔαγρος.definition: lucky in the chase, S.OC1088 , AP6.34 ; affording good sport, ib.9.555 ; epith. of Pan, Sammelb.4031, 4053; of Ares, BMus.Inscr.1064

εὐαγωγία.definition: easiness of being led, Pl.Def.413b, cf. Them.Or.13.175c: abs., docility, Arist.VV1250b32; Philostr.V A6.13

εὐαερία.definition: freshness of air, prob. in Callix.1, cf. Ptol.Tetr.86; fineness of weather, Plu.2.787e, Eust.1505.19: Ion. v

εὐάζω.definition: cry in honour of Bacchus, S.Ant.1134 , E.Ba.1034 ; AP9.363.11 , cf. D.S.4.3, Callistr.Stat.2: c. acc. cogn., Sopat.10:—Med., E.Ba.68

εὐαιμορράγητος.definition: easily bleeding, Id.19.457, Leonid. ap. Aët.15.5, Paul.Aeg.6.30

εὐαισθησία.definition: quick sensibility, vigorous capacity of sensation, Pl.Ti.76d, Arist.PA656a16, Stoic.3.32, Aristeas259, Ph.1.104, al., Gal.UP8.6, Iamb.Protr.2

εὐανάγνωστος.definition: easy to read aloud, Arist.Rh.1407b11, Phld. Rh.1.199 S

εὐανάδοτος.definition: easy to digest, Ath.1.26a, Diph.Siph. ap. eund.8.356b , Dsc.2.85, Iamb.VP3.13

εὐανάκλητος.definition: easy to call out, of the names of; easy to recall, Plu.Cim.17; Id.TG2. Adv. M.Ant.1.7

εὐανακόμιστος.definition: easy to bring back, Plu.2.458e; easily restored, of health, Gal.6.297

εὐανάληπτος.definition: easy to recover, Str.1.2.16; easily; Act., easily taking in, of good capacity for, Stob.2.7.11m

εὐανάλυτος.definition: easily analysed, Simp.in Cat.217.18. Adv. ib.212.16

εὐανάπνευστος.definition: easy to repeat in a breath, Arist.Rh.1409b14

εὐανάστροφος.definition: ready to turn back, cautious, Ptol.Tetr.159

εὐανάσφαλτος.definition: quickly recovering, Hp.Alim.28; from which one wakes easily, Ruf. ap. Orib.inc.4.55

εὐανάτρεπτος.definition: easy to upset, actiones; Medic., 'shaky', Gal.18.605; but mobility, Id.UP1.7

εὐανδρέω.definition: abound in men, Aristeas108, Str.1.2.40; to be in full vigour, Plu.Cam.8, App.Syr.37

εὐανδρία.definition: abundance of men, esp. of good men and; physical fitness, as a subject of a contest, Din.Fr.16.2, IG22.956.48, al.; And.4.42: so in pl., Ath.13.565f; by the crews being able-bodied men, Plu.Pomp.24

εὐανθής.definition: blooming, downy; rich in flowers, flowery, Thgn.1200; Ar.Ra.373 ; Pl.Smp.196b; decked with flowers, Pi.P.2.62, cf. Sapph.78; freely flowering, Thphr.HP6.2.3

εὐάντητος.definition: accessible, gracious; acceptable, Opp.C.2.488, cf. H.2.149

εὐαπόβλητος.definition: easily lost, Alex.Aphr.Quaest.122.8, Simp.in Epict.p.52 D., in Ph.274.29

εὐαπόκριτος.definition: easy to expound by answers, Sor.1.1; Act., in Adv. to have an easy answer . . , Artem.4.63

εὐαπολόγητος.definition: easy to excuse, Str.10.3.1, Plu.Agis17, Hierocl.in CA19p.461M

εὐαπόλυτος.definition: easy to be separated from; easily solved, of a question, Phld.Sign.11, Demetr.Lac.1055.23 F., A.D.Pron.30.13

εὐαπόνιπτος.definition: easy to wash off, Sch.D.T.p.204 H

εὐαπόρρυτος.definition: easily flowing away, Hp.Fract.28; easily slipping off, of bandages, Id.18.765

εὐαπόσπαστος.definition: easy to be torn from, Arist.HA550a12

εὐαποτείχιστος.definition: easy to wall off, blockade, Th.6.75, X.HG2.4.31

εὐαρέστημα.definition: individual taste, preference, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.5.27.6

εὐαρέστησις.definition: being well pleased; satisfaction, Aq., Sm., Thd.Ex.29.18

εὐαρμοστέω.definition: to be well tempered or composed, Hp.Praec.9; to be of convenient size, Ph.Bel.53.29; suit, agree with, c. dat., Dieuch. ap. Orib.4.7.25

εὐαρμοστία.definition: happy adaptation, suitableness; of men's dispositions and tempers , Pl.R.400d, Prt.326b, etc.; D.61.19; Pl.Pomp.1; of political concord, Ecphant. ap. Stob.4.7.64

εὐάρμοστος.definition: well-joined, harmonious; of men, well-tempered, Hp.Epid.2.6.1; accommodating, harmonious, Isoc.12.32; Pl.R.413e: Comp. and Sup., Id.Prt.326b, R.412a; = Ph.1.5. Adv. Isoc.11.12, cf. Ruf. ap. Orib.7.26.135; Ph.1.33

εὐάροτος.definition: well-ploughed or easy to be ploughed, A.R.2.810; AP6.41 ; ib.9.347 :—also EM141.2

εὐαρχία.definition: good government, PMasp.2iii9 , EM390.38; gloss on Sch.Od.19.114

εὐαρχίζω.definition: in fut. = Hsch.: also aor. 1 Med. Id

εὐασμός.definition: the cry of Hermesian.7.18, Str.4.4.6, Plu.Marc.22, Ant.75

εὔβολος.definition: throwing luckily , Eub.58, cf. Poll.9.94, Suid. s.v. generally, lucky, Opp.H.3.71, Hld.5.18. Adv., he was in luck, cj. Pors. for A.Ch.696: Comp., Aristaenet.1.23

εὐβουλεύς.definition: like he of good counsel, epith. of Zeus, D.S.5.72; of Dionysus, Orph.H.30.6: acc. Plu.2.714c: alone, = Nic.Al.14, Orph.Fr.237, Hsch

εὔβουλος.definition: well-advised, prudent, Thgn.329, Hdt.8.110, Pi.O.13.8, B.14.37, Th.1.84, Pl.R.428b, Arist.EN1141b13: Comp., Ar.Pax689: Sup., And.1.140. Adv. : Comp. D.C.43.16: Sup. Gp.5.16.1

εὐγένειος.definition: Ep. of a lion, well-maned, . . Od.4.456; Il.15.275; of Pan, well-bearded, h.Hom.19.39; of men, Pl.Euthphr.2b, Luc.Icar.10

εὐγενέτης.definition: Dor. = sq., used by E. in lyr., Ion1060, al., cf. Tim.Pers.219, AP12.195 :—fem. ib.9.788, IG14.192 ; also prob. in IG 5.259

εὐγενία.definition: = E.HF696 , AP7.337.6; eugenia, a kind of vine, Plin. HN 14.25

εὐγηρία.definition: green old age, Arist.Rh.1361b26, Stoic.3.24, Plu.2.111b, Cat.Cod.Astr.8.167; Ph.2.163

εὐγλαγής.definition: Nic.Th.617; and Lyc.307:—abounding in milk: metapl. dat. AP9.744

εὔγλωσσος.definition: Att. Cret. GDI 5112; sweet-sounding, of the Attic dialect, AP9.188, cf. Gal.8.586; that which is pleasant to the ear, D.H.Comp.1

εὐγνωμονέω.definition: have good sense or feeling, show a; reward, repay, Lib.Decl.34.26, cf. PAmh.2.142.17 ; make a return gift in token of gratitude, Him.Or.8.7

εὐγνώμων.definition: gen. of good feeling; sensible, prudent, Aeschin.3.170, etc.; Democr.231; Plu.2.42of

εὐγονία.definition: fruitfulness, Pl.R.546a, X.Lac.1.6, Ph.2.390, etc.; opp. Iamb.Comm. Math.15

εὔγραμμος.definition: well-designed, D.H.Is.4; well-; well-defined, D.H.Dem.40; so Id.Comp.23

εὐγώνιος.definition: with regular angles, X.Oec.4.21, Arist.Pr.912b15; with perfect angles, four square, of blocks, IG22.1666A64, etc.; right-angled, Gal.18.856

εὐδαιμονέω.definition: pf. Arist.Metaph.1048b26; to be truly happy, Democr.40, cf. Arist.Pol.1339b19, Diog.Oen.25, etc

εὐδαιμόνημα.definition: piece of good luck, Luc.Im.22, Stoic.3.136

εὐδαιμονία.definition: Ion. prosperity, good; true, full happiness, Democr.171; opp. Id.170, cf. Pl.Def.412d, Arist.EN1095a18, Zeno Stoic.1.46, etc

εὐδαιμονίζω.definition: call or account happy, E.Tr.268, cf. X.Mem.2.7.7, Arist.EN1096a2, etc.; Isoc.8.83: c. gen. rei, . . for his eminent fortune, S.OC144, cf. Pl.R.516c, al.; D.21.109, cf. 19.67; X.An.1.7.3 ; D.18.260; Luc.Nigr.23:—Pass.,…

εὐδαιμόνισμα.definition: that which is thought to be a; congratulation, App.BC4.16

εὐδαιμονισμός.definition: thinking or calling happy, predication of happiness, Arist.Rh.1367b34, EN1127b18, Plu.Pel.34, etc.: pl., Ph.1.312.al

εὐδαιμοσύνη.definition: = Archyt. ap. Stob.3.1.112, 114, Perict. ib.4.28.19, X.Eph.1.16

εὐδαίμων.definition: gen. blessed with a good genius; of outward prosperity, wealthy, Hdt.1.133, cf. 196,5.8, Th.1.6, etc.; Lys.32.17; Pl.R.406c; Id.Prt.316b; Hdt.8.111; Id.5.31; Pi.P.4.276, etc.; Gorg.Fr.10 D.; Peripl.M.Rubr.26; Philostr…

εὔδειπνος.definition: with goodly feasts, well-; epith. of departed souls to whom offerings were made , A.Ch.484; taken by some Gramm. as applied to the festival itself, Hsch., Phot.,EM42.3

εὐδιάβατος.definition: easy to cross, X.HG4.2.11, Colot. ap. Plu.2.1117d, cf. Polyaen.2.2.1

εὐδιάβλητος.definition: = Arist.EE1237b23, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.77, S.E.M.3.160, Ptol.Tetr.2: Sup., Eus.Mynd.47

εὐδιάβολος.definition: easy to misrepresent, Pl.Lg.944b; Id.Euthphr.3b. Adv. D.61.17

εὐδιάκριτος.definition: easy to distinguish, A.D.Adv.164.12; easy to explain, clear, Just.Nov.166Pr., cf. Sch.Il.24.23

εὐδιάλυτος.definition: easy to undo or open, of traps; easy to dissolve or break up, gloss on Gal.16.762: metaph., Arist.EN1156a19, cf. Ph.1.379; Plu.Phil.8

εὐδιάπνευστος.definition: = sq, Thphr.Od.39, Ath.1.26e; Act., perspiring freely, ib.9.5.3, Gal.6.407

εὐδιάσειστος.definition: easily shaken, EM104.5, cf; easy to disprove, A.D.Pron.4.23

εὐδιασκέδαστος.definition: easily spread, of a plaster; easily dispersed, Eus.Mynd.63

εὐδιάφθορος.definition: easily destroyed; easily corrupted, Arist.Ath.41.2 ; easily going bad, of food, Xenocr. ap. Orib.2.58.145, Dsc.1.105

εὐδιαφόρητος.definition: easily carried off by perspiration; easily distributed or digested, of foods, Gal.6.661, Xenocr.2, PGoodsp.Cair.2i11

εὐδιαχώρητος.definition: of food, easy to digest and pass, Xenocr.31, cf. Ruf.Interrog.40: Comp., Arist.Pr.927b22

εὐδικία.definition: Ion. righteous dealing, righteousness, Od.19.111; righteously, A.R.4.343; IG3.1151; . . Epigr.Gr.915, cf. BCH50.444 : also in late Prose, Phld.Hom.p.43 O., Ph.1.664, Plu.2.781f

εὔδικος.definition: righteous, BCH23.302 : as pr.n., IG12.393 , etc

εὐδίοπτος.definition: easy to see through, Arist.PA658a5, Pr.932b8 , cf. Thphr.Sens.80; Arist.GA779b31

εὐδιόριστος.definition: easy to define, Arist.de An.421a7; easy to distinguish, Gal.7.778

εὔδμητος.definition: Dor. well-built, Il.1.448; Hes.Sc.242; Pi.P.12.3; A.R.1.317

εὐδοκέω.definition: to be well pleased or content, Plb.2.49.2; consent, approve, c. dat., PLond.3.1168.15 , al.; POxy.1273.40 ; also PTeb.317.33 , al.: freq. abs. in legal documents, PRyl.120.24 , etc

εὐδόκησις.definition: satisfaction, approval, Plb.16.20.4, D.S.15.6, D.H.3.13, S.E.M.7.200; consent, concurrence, POxy.1273.39 ; SIG685.108

εὐδοκία.definition: = esp. of God, LXX1 Ch.16.10; object of desire, LXXPs.144.16, Si.18.31

εὐδοκιμέω.definition: impf. Pl.Grg.515e: aor; of wine, meats, etc., to be highly esteemed, popular, Alex.282, cf. Philem.122; i.e. their flesh, Arist.HA618a3; so of things generally, Isoc.4.45, cf. 9.11; D.21.50, cf. Arist.EN1181a16; of po…

εὐδοκίμησις.definition: good repute, reputation, credit, mostly in pl., Pl.R.358a, 363a, Luc.Pisc.25: sg., Them.Or.29.347c

εὐδόκιμος.definition: in good repute, honoured, famous, glorious, A.Pers.858 ; E.Heracl.621 ; in Sup., Pl.Ap.29d, Lg.878a; Plu.Lys.22; Pl.Lg.631b; X.Mem.3.7.1

εὐδοξέω.definition: to be in good repute, to be honoured, famous, E.Rh.496, X.Mem.3.6.16, D.20.142, Ph.2.61, etc.; X.HG1.1.31

εὔδοξος.definition: of good repute, honoured, Thgn.195, Pi.P.12.5, Th.1.84 , etc.; Simon.145, cf. Pi.P.6.17; Pl.Lg.773a; 'crack' ships, Hdt.7.99. Adv. remarkably, 'famously', Pl.Hp.Ma.287e; with distinction, Man.1.102

εὐδράνεια.definition: bodily strength and health, LXXWi.13.19, Hsch

εὐδρομέω.definition: to be fleet of foot, Men.681, Plu.Phil.18: metaph., go off well, Philostr.Im.1.30; to be successful, S.E.M.10.36

εὔδρομος.definition: running well, swift, AP6.160; easily traversed, Id.26.2 , cf. Poll.1.186

εὐειδής.definition: well-shaped, comely, Il.3.48; prop. of female beauty , cf. Hes.Th.250, Thgn.1002, Pi.I.8.31, B.12.102, Hdt.1.196 , al., Pl.Cri.44a, X.Mem.3.11.4; of males, Hdt.1.112, 6.32 , A.Pers.324, E.Hel.1540, X.HG5.3.9: generall…

εὐειματέω.definition: to be well-dressed, Antiph.54, Arist.Rh.Al.1420a17, Gerhard Phoinix p.6, Sotad.9.3

εὐέκβατος.definition: easy to get out of, Hp.Acut.65

εὐεκκάθαρτος.definition: easily cleared up, prob. in Phld. Herc.1251.4

εὐεκκαρτέρητος.definition: easy to endure, Id.D.1.12: written for

εὐέκκριτος.definition: of food, easy to excrete, Hp.Acut.10, Diph.Siph. ap. Ath.2.62f, Dsc.2.9, Xenocr.33, Gal.6.503

εὐέκνιπτος.definition: easy to wash out, of a colour, Poll.1.44

εὐεκπλήρωτος.definition: easily fulfilled or realized, Phld. D.1.13

εὐέκπλυτος.definition: Act.,purging, relaxing, v.l. for in Hp.Acut.10

εὐεκτέω.definition: to be in good condition, Ceb.16, cf. Ph.1.611, Gal.UP1.21, Aesop.185, etc.; Plu.2.919c

εὐέκτης.definition: of a good habit of body, opp. Plb.3.88.2, D.L.2.22: as Adj., Ph.1.583

εὐεκχόλωτος.definition: easily made bilious, Philagr. ap. Paul.Aeg.7.6

εὔελπις.definition: neut. gen. hopeful; c. acc. et fut. inf., A.Pr.509; in good hope to be saved, Th.6.24: c. acc. et pres. inf., Pl.Phd.63c; hopefulness, Plu.2.1101d, D.C.42.1, etc.; cheerful talk, Plb.1.32.6

εὐελπιστία.definition: hopefulness, sanguine temper, confidence, Epicur.Sent.Vat.39, cf.Plb.11.3.6, Phld.Oec.p.73J., Cic.Att.2.17.2; Ph.1.502, Perict. ap. Stob.4.28.19; Procl.in Cra.p.88P

εὐέμβατος.definition: easy to get into, Hp.Acut.65; ChioEp.16.2; ib.15.3

εὐέμβλητος.definition: easy to put in, of dislocated joints, Hp.Art.71

εὐέμετος.definition: or vomiting readily, Hp.Art.40 :—also or Id.Mul.2.125, Aph.4.6, Dsc.2.169 ; that vomiting may be easy, Thphr.HP9.10.2

εὐέμπρηστος.definition: easily set on fire, dub. in Diog.Oen.8

εὐεμπτωσία.definition: liability, proneness to a thing: hence, evil proclivity, Stoic.3.102: in Medic., an illness to which people are commonly liable, such as colds, Posidon. ap. Gal.5.434, Stoic.3.103

εὐέμπτωτος.definition: easily falling into: hence, prone, liable, Posidon. ap. Gal.5.434; Stoic.3.110: Comp., Phld.Ir.p.97 W.; Id.Rh.Supp.p.26S.: abs., Ptol.Tetr.164. Adv. Gal.5.448, Dsc.Ther.Praef.; Phlp.in de An.53.15

εὐένδοτος.definition: easily yielding, Str.16.1.9; morally weak, Ph.2.269, al.; Id.1.153

εὐεξάλειπτος.definition: easy to wipe out, X.HG2.3.53 , Sch.D.T.p.505 H

εὐεξαπάτητος.definition: easily deceived, Pl.R.409a, cf. X.Eq.Mag.7.15, Corn.ND25

εὐέξαπτος.definition: easily kindled or lighted, M.Ant.9.9, Gal.7.342, al

εὐεπακολούθητος.definition: easy to follow, of a train of argument, Arist.Rh.1357a11

εὐεπηρέαστος.definition: exposed to harm, Arr.Epict.4.1.111 , Vett. Val.49.4; Gal.6.124; Sor.1.109; liable to wanton damage, prob. in SIG888.16

εὐεπίβατος.definition: easy to ascend, Str.5.3.7; easy of attack, Ph.Bel.94.40: metaph., Id.1.459, Luc.Cal.19

εὐεπίβλεπτος.definition: easily seen, manifest, Poll.1.172, dub. in Epicur.Nat.2.6, Phld.D.3 Fr. 36

εὐεπίβολος.definition: hilling the mark: hence, shrewd, intelligent, Vett.Val.38.1, al., Ptol.Tetr.57, v.l. in S.E.M.7.322: also spelt Adv. Sch.Ptol.Tetr.99, Simp.in Ph.738.4

εὐεπιβούλευτος.definition: exposed to treachery or stratagem, Str.2.3.4, cf. Ph.2.552, Vett. Val.236.27: Comp., X.Cyr.8.4.3, Onos.36.6, D.C.38.31

εὐεπίβουλος.definition: fond of plotting or intriguing, Ptol.Tetr.162

εὐεπίγνωστος.definition: or easy to recognize or understand, Sor.1.58, Artem.4.84, Cat.Cod.Astr.1.114; Corn.ND9: Comp., a more skilled recognizer, cj. in Hp.Ep.22

εὐεπίδρομος.definition: easily scaled, Agath.2.2; assailable, Id.5.14: metaph., Them.Or.20.235d

εὐεπίθετος.definition: easy to set upon or attack, Th.6.34, D.C.50.32 ; Plb.4.19.12; . . was easy for them to make an attack, X.An.3.4.20 ; Arist.Pol.1314b34; . . Pl.Plt.306a. Adv. to be exposed, Aen.Tact.23.4

εὐεπίμεικτος.definition: accessible, Str.11.2.2; of men, Id.11.4.6, cf. Poll.5.138. Adv. ib.139

εὐεπινόητος.definition: fertile in devices, 'sharp' in business, Vett. Val.44.22

εὐεπιπόλαστος.definition: tending to return or be vomited, Sor.1.109

εὐεπίστροφος.definition: easily twisted, EM616.7; beautifully curved, of a dome, Agath.5.9

εὐεπίτευκτος.definition: easily hitting the mark, successful, Vett.Val.39.20,40.36, 45.10; Malch.p.391 D.; opportune, Sever.Clyst.p.34D

εὐεπιτήδευμα.definition: act embodying good conduct, cj. in Stoic. ap. Stob.2.7.11e

εὐεπίφορος.definition: inclined, prone, Corn.ND35; leading easily, D.H.10.46

εὐεπιχείρητος.definition: easy to be attacked, Str.5.3.7; easy to be attempted or proven, Arist.APr.42b29, cf. Top.111a11

εὐέργεια.definition: Ion. = sq.I, AP15.34; ease of a surgical operation, Orib.45.18.14

εὐεργεσία.definition: Ion. well-doing, opp; a good deed, kindness, Od.22.235, cf. Hes.Th.503 ; done by him, Hdt.5.11; Id.3.47 ; ib.67; Th.1.128; Hdt.4.165; X.An.7.7.47; Pl.Grg.513e; opp. Isoc.14.57; Th.1.137, cf. 32; for service done, Simo…

εὐεργέτημα.definition: service done, kindness, X.Cyr.8.2.2, cf. Hp.Ep.25 , etc.: pl., X.Cyr.5.5.34, Isoc.4.34, Arist.EN1161a16, IG22.808, etc

εὐερμέω.definition: to be favoured by Hermes, to be fortunate, Poll.5.135 . fortunate, Vett.Val.14.24, Hsch

εὐζωΐα.definition: well-living, Arist.EN1098b21, Hierocl.in CA Praef.p.416M., al.; civil well-being, PMasp.19.28, al. ; also, means of subsistence, PLond.5.1708.20 : trisyll., metri gr., Pi.P.4.131: opp. Herm.in Phdr.p.179 A

εὐήκοος.definition: Dor. . 2. hearing willingly, obedient, Arist.EN1102b27 . 3. inclined to give ear, of the gods, AP9.316.5 , cf. IG12.101, 105 ; written Sammelb.4607.5: generally, inclined, Thphr.CP2.14.5 . Adv. Plb.27.7.7. II. Pass., …

εὐημερέω.definition: spend one's days cheerfully; to be successful in a thing, Aeschin.2.63; Thphr.Char.21.11; Macho ap.Ath.13.577d; of physicians, to be successful with a remedy, Gal.12.749: c.acc., of a dramatist, Ath.13.584d; of an act…

εὐημέρημα.definition: a success, usu. in the military sense, Plb.3.72.2, OGI299.7 , Cic. Att.5.21.2, D.S.13.13, Ph.2.120: pl., successes, Inscr.Prien.109.90 , 111.130 : generally, strokes of good fortune, Epicur.Fr.488; bodily excellencies…

εὐημερία.definition: Dor. fine weather; prosperity, health and wealth, E.El.197 ; Arist.EN1178b33; happiness, Pherecr.213; joy of living, Arist.Pol.1278b29; personified, Alex.161, Schwyzer462 A6 ; to keep a day of rejoicing, Alciphr.1.21;…

εὐήμερος.definition: Dor. of a fine; bright, happy, E.Fr.773.47 ; Id.Hyps.Fr.41.62 ; Ar.Av.1322 ; Pl.Ti.71d ; a prosperous life, Ph.1.515

εὔηχος.definition: = euphonious, Phld.Po.994.24, v.l. in D.H.Comp.14, cf. Longin.24.2; melodious, of the voice, Ath.3.80d; Ph.1.511; Dsc.2.27; LXXPs.150.5: neut. pl. as Adv., Ps.-Luc.Philopatr.3: regul. Adv. Thom.Mag.p.223 R

εὐθαλέω.definition: bloom, thrive, Nic.Fr.74.16, Plu.2.28e, POxy.729.22 , Q.S.4.423: metaph., Them.Or.27.339c

εὐθαλής.definition: blooming, flourishing, thriving, A.Fr.300.5; Men.Mon.388; Mosch.3.100, cf. AP9.3 , Orph.A.912; AP7.600 : later in Prose, SIG889.9 ; Sabin. ap. Orib.9.17.3; POxy.902.15 : metaph., Ph.1.512; Them.Or.21.251b

εὐθανατέω.definition: die a noble death, Stoic.3.156, Plb.5.38.9, J.AJ9.4.5

εὐθάνατος.definition: dying easily or happily: = Men.23, cf. Paul. Al.M.3. Adv. Cratin.413, Men.481.16

εὐθαρσέω.definition: to be of good courage, And.2.16: prob. to be written divisim in A.Th.34, Supp.1015

εὐθενέω.definition: thrive, flourish, of animals and plants; Pass. in same sense, Hdt.1.66 codd. ; D.19.231 . is freq. v.l.; is required by metre in A.Eu.895 , Cratin.327, and is found in best codd. of D., Arist. , cod. Urb. of Thphr.CP5…

εὐθεραπευσία.definition: ease of treatment, Heliod. ap. Orib.46.22.11

εὐθεράπευτος.definition: easy to cure, Hp.Coac.501; easy to help or remedy, D.C.38.24

εὐθετέω.definition: to be suitable, convenient; trans., set in order, Luc.DDeor.24.1 , cf. SIG1240 ; Ar.Fr.782; adorn, D.C.51.13; lay out a corpse, Id.40.49, cf. Phryn.PSp.71 B

εὐθετισμός.definition: convenience, propriety, Id.Adv.144.19, Synt.309.12; orderly arrangement, Simp.in Ph.487.29, in Cat.336.38

εὔθετος.definition: well-arranged, conveniently; of persons, well-adapted, Philem.105.5; Phld.Ir.p.46 W., Lib.p.45 O.; Ev.Luc.9.62; for a business, Nicol. ap. Stob.3.1.40; Plb.25.3.6, etc.; quick, able, D.S.33.22: abs., fit and proper pe…

εὐθηλέομαι.definition: Pass., to be well-suckled, fatted up, A.Fr.309.1:—also in Act., = Democr.276

εὔθηλος.definition: with distended udder, E.IA579 , Ba.737, AP9.224 ; Lyc.1328

εὐθημονέομαι.definition: Dep. keep in order, manage, Pl.Lg.758b:—Act., intr., to be in good order, Simp.in Ph.1067.24; trans. in Tz.H.1.367

εὐθηνέω.definition: thrive, flourish, Hdt.2.91, 124 codd., cf. X.Ath.2.6 codd.; h.Hom.30.10; may their sheep thrive, SIG526.42 ; prob. in Hp.Aër.12 , cf. Epid.6.4.20 ; freq. in LXX , cf. BGU1118.30 , al., Ph.1.211, 2.429:—Pass., POxy.138…

εὐθηνιάρχης.definition: commissioner of food- supply, BGU556ii12, POxy.1412.1 :—hence ib.908.19 , 2108.3 , BCH12.84

εὐθήρατος.definition: easy to catch or win, A.Supp.87; AP12.105 , cf. Corn.ND28; Plb.31.25.3; v.l. Opp.H.5.426

εὔθικτος.definition: touching the point, clever, quick, Arist.HA616b22; quick in repartee, Ath.13.583f; Ph.1.54, 240, 286; witty, Plb.18.4.4, AP6.322 : f.l. for Heraclit.All.51 codd. Adv. LXX2 Ma.15.38, Hdn.4.7.2

εὐθυβολέω.definition: intr., dart or go right forward, Placit.5.14.2; metaph., hit the mark, Anon. ap. Suid.s.v. cf. Ph.2.176

εὐθύβολος.definition: throwing straight: hence, hitting the mark, accurate, exact, prob. for in Aristox. ap. Stob.1.7.18; Ph.1.617, 2.126; the exact name, Id.1.73 , al.: Comp., Id.1.618: Sup., Id.1.300; = foreg., Id.2.465. Adv. Id.1.99, al…

εὐθύγλωσσος.definition: Att. straightforward, plain-spoken, Pi.P.2.86, Dam.Isid.23, Procop.Arc.29

εὐθυγνωμίας.definition: witness who gives direct evidence, Phot

εὐθυγραμματίζω.definition: reduce to a rectilinear figure, Phlp.in APr.477.2

εὐθύγραμμος.definition: = foreg., Arist.Cael.286b13, al.; Oenopides ap. Procl.in Euc.p.333F., cf. Euc.1.44; rectilinear figure, Arist.APr.69a31, Pr.913b18, Thphr.HP1.12.1

εὐθυδικία.definition: direct trial, on the merits of the case, without exceptions or technical pleas, Is.7.3; D.34.4; also Id.45.6, Is.6.43; Mitteis Chr. 31 vi 13

εὐθυδρομέω.definition: of ships, run a straight course, Ph.1.131, 327, Act.Ap.16.11: metaph., of persons, Agath.2.21

εὐθυδρόμος.definition: running a straight course, Plb.34.4.5; Orph.H.22.10

εὐθύληπτος.definition: easy to get at, to procure, Anon. ap. Suid

εὐθυμέω.definition: to be of good cheer, E.Cyc.530, AP5.100; trans., cheer, delight, A.Fr.350.4, cf. Democr.279:—Pass., to be cheerful, Id.3, X.HG7.4.36; Id.Cyr.4.1.19; Arist.Rh.1379b18; Aret.CA1.1

εὐθυμία.definition: cheerfulness, contentment, Pi.I.1.63; personified, Pi.Fr.155, Memn.4.2, LW45

εὔθυμος.definition: kind, generous, Od.14.63; cheerful, Democr.174, X.Cyr.6.4.13 , Pl.Lg.792b; Ion Eleg.1.14; Pi.O.5.22; of horses, spirited, X.Eq.11.12 ; = Plu.2.1106c, D.C.42.1. Adv. cheerfully, Batr.159, A.Ag.1592: Comp. X.Cyr.2.2.27:…

εὔθυνος.definition: corrector, chastiser, judge, A.Pers.828; at Athens and elsewhere, public examiner , IG12.188, Decr. ap. And.1.78, Pl.Lg.945a sq., Arist.Pol.1322b11, Ath.48.4, SIG 38.3 ; official of a guild, Supp.Epigr.2.458 , etc

εὐθυπλοέω.definition: sail straight, Str.11.2.3, cf.Arr.Cyn.25.8: metaph., Cerc.5.16

εὐθύπλοια.definition: straight voyage, in dat. Str.3.3.1, prob. l. in Id.6.3.7

εὐθυπλοκία.definition: straight weaving, evenness of texture, Pl.Plt.283a, 311b

εὐθυρρημονέω.definition: speak in a straightforward manner, 'call a spade a spade', Zeno Stoic.1.22; utter off-hand, Plu.Demetr.14

εὐθυρρημοσύνη.definition: plainness of speech, Phld.Rh.2.281 S., M.Ant.11.6, S.E.M.2.22

εὐθύρριν.definition: straight-nosed, PAmh.2.51.23 , BGU993 ii 11 , al.; nom. Poll.2.73

εὐθύστομος.definition: talking plainly, EM191.33, Sch.Luc.JTr.27; f.l. for Poll.5.60

εὐθυτενής.definition: straight, Ph.1.456, cf. Dion.Byz.3; Iamb.VP3.16; Ael.NA4.34: Medic., Antyll. ap. Orib.44.8.1. Adv. ib.9, Ph.1.338, Gal.18.797

εὐθυτράχηλος.definition: with a straight neck, of the bladder, Sor.1.18

εὐθυτρεχής.definition: running in a straight line, IG22.463.73

εὐθυφερής.definition: running in a straight line, Pl.Lg.815b

εὐθύφλοιος.definition: straight-barked, name of a kind of oak, Thphr.HP3.8.2

εὐθύφρων.definition: gen. whole-hearted, sincere, A.Eu.1040, f.l. ib.1034

εὐθύχαλκος.definition: payable on demand in cash , POxy.1482.15

εὐθυωρία.definition: straight course or direction, Pl.R.436e, Ti.45c, Arist.de An.406b31; longitudinally, Id.PA654a17; also to oppose directly, Id.Rh.1379a11; opp. Ti.Locr.94b; in an infinite series, Arist.Metaph.994a2; SIG685.65 , cf. ib…

εὐθύωρος.definition: in a straight direction: mostly in neut. as Adv., = X.An.2.2.16, Ael.NA11.16; ib.7.5: as Adj., Anon. ap. EM391.42, cf. Procop.Aed.2.2

εὐίατος.definition: Ion. easy to heal or remedy, Arist.EN1121a20, Thphr.HP5.4.5, Porph.Abst.1.56, freq. in Comp., Hp.Art.14, X.Eq.4.2, etc

εὐίλατος.definition: very merciful, of deities, PCair.Zen.34.19 , IG3.73, GDI 3543 , etc.; LXXPs.98.8; also PPetr.2p.45 ; later written GDI 3536 , UPZ109.6 :—hence to be merciful, LXXDe.29.20, al

εὐκαθαίρετος.definition: easy to conquer, Th.7.18 ; easily exhausted, Herod.Med. ap. Orib.5.30.11; unstable, Vett.Val.175.30,212.21

εὐκάθεδρος.definition: gloss on Hsch., Sch.Od.2.390, etc.; on Sch.A.R.1.4

εὐκάθεκτος.definition: easy to keep under or restrain, X.Cyr.7.5.69

εὔκαιρος.definition: well-timed, seasonable; of places, convenient, well situated, PPetr. 2p.28 , cf.Plb.4.38.1 , D.S.1.63, etc

εὐκαμπής.definition: well-bent or curved; flexible, Thphr.HP3.10.4; Str.15.1.20; Plu.Sull.17; of timber, Orib.9.19.2 ; slippery, Aret.SD1.10. is corrupt: easily swallowed, Salm.)

εὐκαρπέω.definition: bear good fruit or crops, Hp.Ep.10, Thphr.CP1.20.5, HP2.7.7, Str.5.2.7, BGU1040.5

εὔκαρπος.definition: fruitful, of women, h.Hom.30.5; of; Act., fruitful, fertilizing, Thphr.CP2.3.3; epith. of Aphrodite, S.Fr.847; of Dionysus, AP6.31; of Demeter, ib.7.394

εὐκατάκαυστος.definition: easily burnt, gloss on Suid., Phot

εὐκατακράτητος.definition: easy to hold or defend, Plb.4.56.9

εὐκατάληπτος.definition: easy to apprehend or recognize; Adv. to be easily bandaged by , Hp.Off.9

εὐκατανόητος.definition: easy to observe or understand, Plb.18.30.11, Ptol.Tetr.30

εὐκαταπάλαιστος.definition: easy to throw in wrestling, EM400.5

εὐκατάπρηστος.definition: easily kindled or set on fire, Ph.Fr.103 H., Suid

εὐκατάσειστος.definition: easily shaken or thrown down, Eust.969.61

εὐκατάστατος.definition: well-fixed, firmly established, Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.87, cf. Asp.in EN106.11; A.D.Adv.157.16

εὐκατάστροφος.definition: brought to a good conclusion, well- turned, of a period: only in Adv. Demetr.Eloc.10

εὐκατάτακτος.definition: easy to set in order, Ptol.Geog.1.1

εὐκατατρόχαστος.definition: easily overrun or attacked, Str.14.5.6; of writers, open to attack, incorrect, Id.1.2.2:—also Hsch

εὐκαταφρόνητος.definition: easy to be despised, contemptible, X.HG6.4.1, cf. Cyr.8.3.1, D.4.18, Men.Sam.297, Arist.Pol.1312b24, etc.; negligible, Epicur.Sent.Vat.4, cf. Phld.D.1.25, al.; esp. in Lit. Crit., D.H.Comp.3, Longin.3.1, Demetr.Eloc.4…

εὐκαταφρόντιστος.definition: well considered, dub. l. in Ph.1.664

εὐκατάψευστος.definition: safe to tell lies about, Str.1.2.19

εὐκατέργαστος.definition: easy to work, Thphr.CP4.7.3; easy to subdue or conquer, D.H.3.20; Plu.Pyrrh.19

εὐκατηγόρητος.definition: easy to blame, open to accusation, Antipho Soph.51, Th.6.77, Plb.4.29.3

εὐκατοίκητος.definition: convenient for dwelling in, gloss on Sch.E.Or.1621

εὐκατόρθωτος.definition: easily effected, D.S.34/5.2.45; Heliod. ap. Orib.44.23.23. Adv. Sch.A.R.1.246

εὐκερματέω.definition: to be rich in money, Eub.144; condemned by Phryn.339

εὐκίνητος.definition: easily moved, agile, Hp.Aph.3.17; easily moved, changeable, Arist.Cat.8b35; fickleness, Hdn 7.7.1. Adv. D.S.20.95

εὐκλεΐζω.definition: bring honour to, Sapph.118.6; praise, Tyrt.12.24: Dor. aor. 1 Pi.P.9.91, B.6.16; IG12.1085

εὐκληματέω.definition: grow luxuriantly, of vines, LXXHo.10.1, Ph.1.681, Phlp.in GA43.26

εὐκληρέω.definition: to be fortunate, Telesp.60 H.: c. acc. cogn., AP11.128

εὐκλήρημα.definition: a piece of good fortune, Antiph.317, Telesp.26 H., D.S.18.13, Str.5.3.7

εὔκληρος.definition: Dor. fortunate, LXXDe.4.20, APl.4.296 , Ael.Fr.288: euphem. of the dead, BGU1209.5

εὐκοινώνητος.definition: easy to deal with, Arist.EN1121a4, cf. Them.Or.22.269c

εὐκοπία.definition: ease, facility, D.S.1.36, 3.17, LXX2 Ma.2.25; PMag.Par.1.159

εὔκοπος.definition: easy, Plb.18.18.2: mostly in Comp., Dsc.1.39; c. inf., Ev.Matt.9.5, 19.24, etc. Adv. Hp.Epid.2.6.31, Ar.Fr.783, D.S.3.24, Ph.Bel.56.16: Comp. Antip.Stoic.3.256

εὐκοσμία.definition: orderly behaviour, good conduct, decency, E.Ba.693, X.Cyr.1.2.3, Arist.Pol.1299b16, etc.; IG22.354.16 ; ib.22.223B8; SIG1007.24 ; Pl.Prt.325d; CIG3185.19 ; IGRom.4.582

εὐκρατόω.definition: temper, in Pass., Sch. Hes.Th.p.461 G., Sch.Lyc.177

εὐκρινέω.definition: keep distinct, keep in good order; judge fit, decide, PCair.Zen.150.22

εὐκρινής.definition: well-separated, X.Eq.Mag.3.3; distinct, clear, then the winds are regular, steady, Hes.Op.670; Is.10.2; there is no clear discernment, Arist.Pr.903a17. Adv. Pl.Sph.242c; Id.R.564c; . . . . without distinction, Str.16.…

εὐκρίνητος.definition: highly sensitive, prob. f.l. for Aret.SD1.6

εὐλάβεια.definition: Ion. Thgn.118, AgathoinPLGii; c. gen., caution or discretion in a thing, Antipho3.3.11; avoidance of . . , Pl.Lg.815a; Arist.EN1121b24; S.OC116; Id.El.1334; careful employment of . . , Phld.D.3 Fr. 32

εὐλαβέομαι.definition: take care, Ar.Ach.955; Pl.Lg.927c, Ion537a; Id.Lg.691b; Luc.Gall.21: abs., S.OT47; Pl.Prt.333e, cf. 316d; without reserve, D.18.159; take precautions, Arist.Pol.1303b27

εὐλαβής.definition: taking hold well, holding fast; metaph., undertaking prudently, discreet, cautious, Democr.91, Pl.Plt.311a, al.; = ib.b; Plu.CG3; Hdn.2.8.2; keeping from . . , LXXLe.15.31. Adv. Pl.Sph.246b; D.S.13.12, etc.: Comp. E.I…

εὐλείαντος.definition: and easily triturated, Xenocr.42; Arist.PA674b33: Comp., Antyll. ap. Orib.10.13.12

εὐληματέω.definition: to be of good spirit, A.Fr.106

εὐλίμενος.definition: with good harbours, E.Hel.1463; Pl.Lg.705a, cf. 704b, 704d; Archestr.Fr.26: c. gen., App.Anth.3.81 : —also Procop.Aed.1.5

εὐλογέω.definition: of God or men, LXXGe.35.9,al., Act.Ap.3.26,al.: freq. in pf. part. Pass. as LXXDe.28.3,Ev.Luc.1.28

εὐλογία.definition: good or fine language, Pl.R.400d; plausibility, Thphr.CP6.31.1; habet Cic.Att.13.22.4, cf. Ep.Rom.16.18; prob. in Phld.Sign.27; Id.Herc.1251.8

εὐλογίζω.definition: = v.l. in LXXTo.4.12:—Pass., v.l. in Ph.1.395

εὐλογιστέω.definition: act rationally, prudently; = II, bless, Ph.1.125,130,al

εὐλογιστία.definition: circumspection, prudence, Pl.Def.412e; = III, blessing, Ph.1.597,al

εὐλόγιστος.definition: easily computed, hence of ratios; well-weighed, Id.1.4; well-calculated, reasonable, Id.5.55; rational, Antip.Stoic.3.253, Chrysipp. ib.46; Phld.Rh.2.160 S.; Hierocl.in CA11p.441M

εὐλογχέω.definition: to be lucky, prob. in Hsch. for

εὐλοκοπέομαι.definition: to be eaten of worms, Artem.5.81

εὐλύρας.definition: = epith. of Apollo, Sapph.Supp.20c.5, B.Scol.Oxy.1361 Fr. 12, E.Alc.570 , Ar.Th.969 , Limen.4

εὐλυτέω.definition: discharge a debt, prob. in Hsch. s.v

εὐμάθεια.definition: readiness in learning, docility, Pl.R.490c, Arist.Rh.1362b24, Call.Fr.32 P., etc.: pl., Ph.1.326: also in poet. form Pl.Chrm.159e, Men.88a: Ion. AP6.325 , al

εὐμαθής.definition: ready or quick at learning, opp; Pass., easy to learn or know, intelligible, A.Eu.442, Arist.Rh.1409b4; well-known, S.Aj.15; X.Oec.20.14, cf. S.Tr.614: Comp., Plb.14.12.5

εὐμάρεια.definition: ease of movement, dexterity, E.Ba.1128, cf. Arist.Mu.398b35; of internal condition, ease, comfort, S.Tr.193; but also euphem. for alvum exonerare, to ease oneself, Hdt.2.35, cf. 4.113; to provide easy or ready means, …

εὐμέλεια.definition: melody, D.S.4.84, Plu.2.456b, etc; melodious language, Longin.28.2; v.l. for D.H.Comp.18; Phld.Rh.1.196S

Εὐμένειος.definition: Adj. of pr. n. of two kings; festival in honour of Eumenes II of Pergamum, at Pergamum, OGI267.34; at Aegina, ib.329.40; at Sardes, ib.305.9

εὐμενέτης.definition: poet. for well-wisher, Od.6.185, IG 12.23 :—fem. Hsch

εὐμενής.definition: well-disposed, kindly, to; of men, A.Pers.175 , Supp.488 ; S.Ant.212, etc.; well-disposed for it, Plu.Luc.42; = Pl.Lg.792e; . . Hdt.7.237: in Dor. Prose, Schwyzer 84

εὐμετάβλητος.definition: easily changed, changeable. Arist.Rh.1373a30, M.Ant.5.33, etc.; of food, easy of digestion, Hp.Alim.49; = foreg., Aesop.367, Adv. Sch.Th.3.37

εὐμετάβολος.definition: = foreg., changeable, of things and persons, Gorg.Hel.13, Pl.R.503c, X.HG2.3.32, Arist.EN1100b3, etc.; . . Diph.118; LXXPr.17.20; = M.Ant.4.3; Diogenian.Epicur.2.60

εὐμετάδοτος.definition: readily imparting, generous, 1; Pass., easily imparted, Sch.Ar.Pl.1014; of leprosy, contagious, Paul.Aeg.4.1. Adv. Hsch. s.v

εὐμετακίνητος.definition: easily moved or changed, Arist.Metaph.1019a28; caprice, M.Ant.1.16

εὐμετακόμιστος.definition: ready to migrate, Sch.Th.1.2; portable, Aët.1.39

εὐμετάπτωτος.definition: unstable, Thphr.Sens.45; D.S.9.10, cf. Secund.Sent.9. Adv. v.l. in Arr.Epict.2.22.8

εὐμετάρρευστος.definition: easily diverted from its course, Aët.5.57

εὐμετάτρεπτος.definition: revocable, gloss on; easy convertibility, Gal.6.825

εὐμετάφορος.definition: easily moved: moving quickly, EM255.52; gloss on Sch.A.R.1.741

εὐμεταχείριστος.definition: manageable, of persons; in Act. signf., Adv. handily, adroitly, Philostr.Gym.19, cf. Eustr.in EN343.32

εὐμηχάνημα.definition: ingenious contrivance, dub. in Chrysipp. ap. EM701.25

εὐμηχανία.definition: Dor. skill in devising means, c. inf., Pi.I.4.2, Pae.7 Fr.16.11; = Stoic. 3.64, Plu.Tim.16; inventive skill, Andronic.Rhod.p.578 M., Luc.Phal.1.12

εὐμήχανος.definition: of persons, skilful in contriving, inventive, opp. A.Eu.381 , Pl.Prt.344d, etc.: c. gen., Id.Cra.408b; Opp.H.4.593: with a Prep., of birds, full of devices for supporting life, Arist.HA614b34, cf. 616b34: Sup., of the…

εὐμοιρία.definition: happy possession of a thing, Luc.Eun.8, Salt.72; excelling, Id.Rh.Pr.8; Ph.1.238, al.: abs., D.H.Rh.5.3; good fortune, Plu.2.14c, etc

εὔμοιρος.definition: well-endowed by fortune, B.5.1; opp. Pl.Smp.197d, cf. Ph.1.282, Call.Del.295, AP6.278 , Luc.JConf.19. Adv. J.AJ8.12.6; IG12.319 : Comp. App.Hann.29

εὐμολπία.definition: sweet song, Hsch.: title of poem by Musaeus, Paus.10.5.6

εὔμολπος.definition: sweetly singing, AP9.396 : as pr.n.in h.Cer.154, etc

εὔμορφος.definition: fair of form, comely, goodly, Sapph.76 , Hdt.1.196, A.Ag.416, 454 ; . . S.Fr.88.10: D.H.11.2, Ph.2.478 : metaph., A.Ch.490

εὔμουσος.definition: skilled in the arts, esp. in poetry; musical, melodious, E.IT145 ; Ar.Th.112 ; Luc.Am.53; AP9.661 . Adv. gracefully, Corn.ND14, Plu.2.1119d

εὐνήτης.definition: Dor. = E.Med.159 , cf. Hsch.:—fem. S.Tr.922 codd

εὐνοέω.definition: to be well-inclined or favourable, c. dat., Hdt.7.237; S.Aj.689, Lys.13.13, Ar.Nu.1411, X.Oec.12.5, etc.; . . OGI532.9 ; be at peace with, Ev.Matt.5.25: abs., Hdt.9.79; one's well-wisher, Arist.EE1241a11:—Med., Phalar…

εὐνομέομαι.definition: fut. Hdt.1.97, Pl.R.380b: aor. 1 Hdt.1.66, Th.1.18: pf. Epimenid. ap. D.L.1.113:— have good laws, be well- ordered, Hdt.ll.cc., Th.1.18, etc.; Pl. l. c.; D.24.139, cf. Arist.Rh.1354a20, Pol.1294a3; Aeschin.1.171; when…

εὐνουχεῖον.definition: a kind of lettuce, = Plin. HN19.127

εὐνουχίζω.definition: castrate, Ev.Matt.19.12 , Luc.Sat.12, etc.; Xanth.19: metaph., Philostr.V A6.42; Archig. ap.Orib.8.2.8:—Pass., Gal.4.570, D.C.68.2

εὔογκος.definition: of good size, bulky, massive, Hp.Art.23; of moderate or convenient bulk, compact, Aen. Tact.29.6 , 31.23 , Arist.Mete.380a5 , GA766b20, Mnesith. ap.Ath.7.357f, etc.; portable, Thphr.HP9.16.8; Plu.2.969e; of manageable…

εὐοδέω.definition: have a free course or passage, of running; metaph., fare well, prosper, Theopomp.Com.74, cf. Ph.1.430, b; Herm.in Phdr.p.155 A.; Ph.1.687, 240; ib.145; Dam.Pr.376; . . M.Ant.6.17; on a gravestone, IG12.449

εὔοδος.definition: easy to pass, of mountains, X.An.4.8.10; metaph., free from difficulty, simple, Epicur.Fr.18, Ptol.Alm.1.2 . Adv. simply, readily, Phld.D.3.11: Sup. ib.Fr.81

εὐοδόω.definition: help on the way, c. dat. pers; Pass., have a prosperous journey, LXXDa.8.11, al., Ep.Rom.1.10; of things, prosper, be successful, v.l. in Hdt.6.73; = 1 Ep.Cor.16.2, cf. Act.Ap.11.29

εὐοικονόμητος.definition: well arranged, only in Adv; easy to digest, Diph.Siph. ap. Ath.2.54d: Comp., Id.ib.3.80c, Eust.866.21

εὐοίνιστος.definition: of good wine, dub.l. in Orph.A.603

εὔοινος.definition: abounding in wine, Hermesian.7.55, cf. Str.5.4.2; AP6.300.5 : Sup., Max.Tyr.3.10

εὐόμιλος.definition: sociable, Com.Adesp.1015, Vett.Val.40.4, M.Ant.1.16, Hld.3.10, Dam.Isid.49, Agath.1.13

εὐοπλέω.definition: to be well-equipped, AP12.120 , Ph.1.20, Hld.8.16, Arr.Tact.5.3

εὔοπλος.definition: well-armed, well-equipped; with good hoofs, Poll.1.194
